title: Barley Net Blotch Initiative (BNBI) Program 2 – Host and pathogen genetics
description:
Net blotches pose an escalating and urgent threat to Australian barley, costing the industry an estimated $122 million each year through disease-related yield losses, downgraded grain quality, and higher fungicide management costs. Widespread planting of susceptible varieties, the practice of growing barley on barley, and an over-reliance on fungicides with a singular mode of action are driving net blotch pathogens to evolve and spread faster than current surveillance, varietal resistance breeding, management and extension efforts can respond.
This investment seeks to help Australian barley growers keep ahead of a threat that is moving faster than current tools can handle. It will be delivered through a five-year, nationally focused Barley Net Blotch Initiative (BNBI) comprising three interlinked programs supported by a dedicated coordinator:
? Program 1 - Pathogen surveillance, monitoring, and screening
? Program 2- Host and pathogen genetics
? Program 3 - Integrated disease management and extension
? Program C - Coordination and capacity development
GRDC is seeking a capable partner to deliver BNBI Program 2 that will fast-track delivery of high levels of durable host resistance in well-adapted backgrounds supported by breeder-deployable validated markers, characterised resistance sources, insights and capability from foundational and expanded pathogenic genomics research, a new durability risk-assessment framework, and a feasibility assessment of genome-editing capability.

title: Open innovation call to realise step changes in soil and water productivity and unlock plant potential
description:
PLEASE SEE THE APPROACH TO MARKET ON THE GRDC WEBSITE FOR ALL AVAILABLE INFORMATION FOR THIS REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL: https://grdc.com.au/research/partnering-in-rde-investment/opportunities/current-opportunities/open-innovation-call-to-realise-step-changes-in-soil-and-water-productivity-and-unlock-plant-potential
Background to the open innovation call
A concerted RD&E focus on improving water use efficiency (WUE) has enabled Australian growers to become world leaders in dryland grain production. Improved varieties, agronomic practices, cropping sequences, soil amelioration and other innovations have underpinned these gains. However, growers still have a need to take these gains in water use efficiency and push them even further given climate projections of hotter, drier conditions across most of southern Australia, a decline in cool-season rainfall, and more frequent and extreme weather events. Growers’ ability to outpace these challenges through new frontiers in soil and water productivity and unlocking plant potential will be a key determinant of future profitability and resilience.
Overview of the open innovation call
There is significant value to be captured for growers through the removal of soil constraints, increasing water and nutrient uptake, and increasing the efficiency with which water and nutrient reserves are used by crops. GRDC has made substantial investments in soil amelioration and soil re-engineering to help growers and will continue to do so. These investments have generated valuable knowledge and demonstrated substantial productivity gains. However, key questions remain about the soil–plant–microbial processes behind these gains, particularly why some interventions do not deliver the expected benefits. This open innovation call will complement existing investments by addressing these and other knowledge gaps and unlock further production potential.
The opportunity to drive innovation in these areas is often constrained by a lack of foundational knowledge below-ground on soil-plant-microbial interactions. Foundational knowledge on root form, function, and diversity, soil microbial function and community dynamics, rhizosphere interactions, below-ground phenotyping and related areas underpin the opportunity to create new frontiers in soil and water productivity and the unlocking of plant potential.
Therefore, GRDC is progressing an open innovation call to address these foundational knowledge gaps and create the capacity and momentum that could enable crops to gain access to more water and nutrients and use them more effectively. GRDC is seeking project proposals that deliver against one or more of six-high level scope areas that represent key gaps in the GRDC portfolio (Table 1). GRDC expects that projects established through this open innovation call may be connected into a future ‘below-ground mission’ through research forums, study tours, and other mechanisms that foster mutually beneficial collaborations.
Applications are encouraged from:
• Australian and/or international organisations,
• Public and/or private entities, and
• Existing GRDC projects that could be strategically varied/expanded to address the scope areas.

title: Grain Automate Open Innovation Call
description:
Grain Automate is a national research, development and extension initiative of the Grains Research and Development Corporation. It seeks to accelerate the development, validation and adoption of machine automation, autonomy and intelligent systems, across a range of form factors, including machinery, implements, UAVs and digital systems, that deliver measurable value to Australian grain growers. This call builds on the approach of the Grain Automate Program.

title: Early Intervention Triage and Treatment Program
description:
The Department of Industry, Science and Resources is seeking a suitably qualified supplier to deliver an integrated, nationally accessible Early Intervention Triage and Treatment Program for eligible employees experiencing new or emerging physical or psychological injury, illness or symptoms that are affecting, or may affect, their ability to work.
The service will provide a single point of access to timely nurse-led clinical triage, assessment and advice. Where clinically appropriate and eligibility requirements are met, employees will be supported to access short-term treatment through suitably qualified and experienced health practitioners, including general practitioners, physiotherapists and psychological support services.
The service must provide coordinated pathways from initial contact and triage through to treatment, follow-up and completion of services. This includes appropriate referral and appointment coordination, communication with employees and practitioners, follow-up of treatment and required documentation, and, where relevant, information to support an employee's capacity to remain at work or safely return to work.
The successful supplier will be responsible for the effective end-to-end delivery of the service and active management of its practitioner network. This includes practitioner selection and onboarding, maintaining current program and referral information across the network, quality assurance, monitoring service delivery and documentation, and proactively identifying and addressing recurring or systemic issues.
The service must be accessible to employees across Australia, including regional and remote locations, with virtual or telehealth options where clinically appropriate. Service delivery must also be accessible, inclusive and responsive to disability and other accessibility requirements and individual cultural, communication and other needs.
The department is seeking a supplier that will actively manage the service throughout the contract period and work collaboratively with the department to maintain and improve service quality and employee experience. This includes proactive contract and relationship management, meaningful reporting and service insights, billing and financial administration, communication and promotion of the service, performance monitoring and continuous improvement.
The supplier will also be required to support transition and implementation of the service, including practitioner network readiness, service pathways, systems and administrative arrangements, reporting and billing arrangements, and operational documentation, communications, forms and templates required for service commencement.
Service performance will be monitored against agreed service levels and performance measures, including timeliness, accessibility, practitioner network performance, documentation, responsiveness, billing accuracy, reporting, issue resolution and implementation of corrective actions.

CASA is seeking to engage a Supplier to manage CASA’s e-Commerce service and the warehousing and distribution of items offered for purchase through the e-Commerce service.
CASA currently offers approximately 300 products for sale to CASA staff, the aviation industry and the public. Products range from pads of forms to multimedia products and safety promotional material including uniforms.
The e-Commerce website provides CASA with an online electronic shopfront (shopping cart) for the benefit of CASA staff, the aviation industry and the public to be able to order products. This website includes catalogue and search functions, and a function that retains regular customer details to simplify repeat ordering.
The Supplier will be required to implement and manage the supply chain for CASA’s products from customer order to delivery and restocking on a fee for service basis.
Current warehouse storage space requirements are approximately 200 pallets. Subject to fluctuation, currently holding 160 pallets of CASA materials.
Indicative order volumes per annum:
· 3,000 individual domestic (within Australia) orders and 70 international orders.
The Supplier is required to undertake the following:
· e-Commerce website – Managing CASA’s Shopify 2.0 site including back-end management
· Subscription management
· warehousing and distribution services
· product assembly (Pick-n-Pack)
· online order tracking, email ordering and shipping customer confirmation notification
· computerised inventory restocking, receiving and warehousing
· real time inventory management, reporting and analysis (online)
· provision of best practice online sales and secure money transaction facilities processed in Australia, including customer invoicing and secure funds transfer to CASA
· quality control
· customer complaints and returns handling.
Refer to documentation for more information.

title: Request for Tender in relation to a Social Cohesion Framework for Schools
description:
This procurement is being undertaken to identify a supplier with the appropriate expertise, capability and capacity to develop a Social Cohesion Framework for Schools (the Framework). The Government is delivering the Framework in response to Recommendation 29 of the Special Envoy to Combat Islamophobia's report, A National Response to Islamophobia: A Strategic Framework for Inclusion, Safety and Prosperity, which calls for a framework to address all forms of racism and discrimination in schools.
The Framework will be voluntary and non-regulatory in nature, and will provide practical, evidence-based guidance to support inclusive, safe and respectful learning environments and strengthen schools' ability to prevent and respond to racism, faith-based discrimination, and other forms of discrimination. It will be available for all schools and education sectors and will be designed to be nationally relevant while complementing existing jurisdictional and sector policies and processes. It is intended for use by school leaders, teachers, support staff, students, parents and carers, and school system and policy teams.
The project will include:
Extensive stakeholder consultation to ensure the Framework is practical, accessible and implementable for school sectors.
Review of contemporary research evidence and best-practice approaches for addressing social cohesion and discrimination the Australian context.
Development of the FRamework and accompanying practical implementation guidance products that will support schools to implement the Framework's guidance and key principles.
User testing of the Framework and its accompanying products.
Reporting requirements including a Project Plan and Project Report.
Please refer to the Statement of Requirements for the full description of services.

title: Nuclear Medicine Manufacturing Facility - Safety Analysis Report
description:
The Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO) seeks to engage a suitably qualified and experienced consultant to provide Safety Analysis Report (SAR) consulting services for the Nuclear Medicine Manufacturing Facility (NMMF) project at Lucas Heights, NSW. The NMMF will replace ANSTO's existing radiopharmaceutical manufacturing facility and support the long term supply of nuclear medicines for Australia.
The successful consultant will be responsible for developing, coordinating and maintaining the overarching Safety Analysis Report (SAR) and associated Plans and Arrangements (P&A) required to support staged regulatory licence applications to the Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency (ARPANSA). Services include development of regulatory submission documentation, integration of safety inputs from multiple design consultants and stakeholders, management of review and approval processes, preparation of supporting regulatory forms, and support for ANSTO during licence assessments and approvals.
The consultant will work collaboratively with ANSTO consultants and other project stakeholders to develop a comprehensive safety case for the facility in accordance with applicable ARPANSA regulatory guidance and ANSTO requirements. Detailed scope is outlined in the attached specification.
The services are expected to support multiple licence application packages associated with the design, construction and operation of the NMMF, a nationally significant nuclear medicine manufacturing facility.

title: Private Hospital Services
description:
DVA is seeking the provision of Private Hospital services for Entitled Persons by publishing this Invitation to Provide Private Hospital Services to the Veteran Community.
DVA serves Australia’s veteran community, through the provision of programmes of care, compensation and commemoration.
DVA’s aim is to secure high quality private hospital care for Entitled Persons delivered for a fair price, at the most convenient locations for Entitled Persons. As the veteran community ages, their capacity to access a wider range of care appropriate to their needs is increasingly important. Managing emerging and different needs of contemporary veterans is also a priority. DVA also aims to continually improve the quality and safety of services, and the health outcomes for DVA clients, through the purchase of evidence-based treatment services.
DVA’s New Approach to Contracting for Private Hospital Services
In the past DVA contracted with Private Hospitals for services to Entitled Persons through a Request for Tenders (RFT).
The current process that DVA is engaging in with Private Hospital providers is not an RFT.
DVA has introduced new arrangements for providers to contract with DVA. This is a simplified contracting model that DVA is using to facilitate engagement with suitably qualified providers.
A summary of the key features of the new arrangements are:
maximising the numbers of participating providers to achieve wide access to private hospitals services for the veteran community;
there is no competition, all qualified providers can participate;
while providers are required to submit the fee tables, there is no requirement for tender submission or evaluation of tenders;
providers self-certify their compliance with DVA’s terms and conditions of the Hospital Services Agreement;
providers can enter into the Hospital Services Agreement at any time and the Hospital Services Agreement will continue until DVA ends the arrangements or the Contracting Entity exits the arrangements with DVA; and
negotiation only on fees to ensure value for money.

title: Virtulisation Platform
description:

• what the market can deliver
• how available options could be implemented
• the full cost of available options over time
• security and sovereignty considerations
• workforce impacts
• purchasing options

title: Notice of RFT - Refresh and Expansion of the Professions of the Panel of Outreach Program Counsellors for the
description:
This is a pre-release notice to provide advance notification of a proposed RFT for the Refresh and Expansion of the Professions of the Panel.
Please note, eligibility, application requirements, assessment processes, and contractual arrangements will be set out in the forthcoming RFT. No evaluation criteria, scoring methodology, or commercial terms are being released at this stage. The Department reserves the right to modify or cancel the proposed RFT at its discretion.
Background on Open Arms
Open Arms is Australia’s national accredited provider of mental health and wellbeing services for veterans and the families of veterans.
Open Arms provides mental health counselling, relationship counselling, peer support services, and group programs for people with Australian Defence Force (ADF) service (current and former serving members) and their immediate families.
Open Arms provides free and confidential counselling through a national network of multidisciplinary mental health professionals, delivered in dedicated Open Arms centres by the DVA’s staff, or through the Panel; being a network of accredited mental health clinicians, engaged to support the delivery of services on behalf of Open Arms across Australia through the Outreach Program.
Open Arms can provide counselling, care coordination and peer support services to veterans and the families of veterans within an episode of care model, where clients engage with our services for goal directed interventions for a defined period.
Open Arms aims to provide timely access to appropriate services and care, based on a comprehensive holistic assessment and integrated care pathways to meet client needs and support recovery. This includes working in partnership with health systems, including primary health, as well as other community agencies to ensure comprehensive support for our clients.
Background on the Panel and Outreach Program
Open Arms’ Model of Care provides the organisational framework that underpins the delivery of all Outreach Program services. It guides how we support veterans and the families of veterans through trauma-informed, military-aware, recovery-oriented care, while ensuring consistent clinical governance, quality service delivery and positive client outcomes. In 2024 the Panel was established through which Outreach Providers provide Open Arms services to clients. The Panel is the mechanism for Open Arms to engage with Outreach Providers to ensure the highest level of support can be delivered to clients. Only organisations or individuals appointed to the Panel can provide Open Arms Outreach Program Counselling Services.
The categories of services that are delivered through the Panel include:
Outreach Program Counsellors (OPCs), who provide individual, couples, or family counselling
Group Program Facilitators (GPFs), who facilitate evidence-informed, military-aware group programs that strengthen resilience, build practical skills, and promote wellbeing
Clinical Supervisors, who provide professional supervision to Open Arms’ staff.
Outreach Providers on the Panel can provide one, two or all three service streams, depending on their qualifications, experience and the services they are approved to deliver.
Go to the Open Arms website for further information:
https://www.openarms.gov.au/about/open-arms-outreach-program
Expansion of definition of OPC
In 2025 the Veterans’ Entitlements (Treatment Principles) Amendment (Outreach Program Counsellor) Determination 2025 and the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation (Treatment Principles) Amendment (Outreach Program Counsellor) Determination 2025), were enacted which amended the MRCA Treatment Principles (No. MRCC 53/2013) and the Treatment Principles (Instrument 2013 No. R52) – (collectively the Treatment Principles) – to expand the types of professions who can provide Outreach Program Counselling as an Outreach Program Counsellor (OPC). Now that occupational therapists, registered nurses, social workers (general) and counsellors are recognised as additional profession types eligible to apply to become a provider, the Department wishes to update the Panel accordingly through the proposed RFT.
The Department is therefore looking to procure Outreach Providers from the following eligible professions:
a person who is registered with AHPRA as a psychologist;
a person who is registered with AHPRA as an occupational therapist;
a person who is registered with AHPRA as a registered nurse;
a person who is eligible for membership with the Australian Association of Social Workers;
or
a person who is registered:
as a registered clinical counsellor with the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia;
as a counsellor at registration category Level 3 or Level 4 with the Australian Counselling Association Limited.
The Department is currently planning to release the RFT to market through publication on AusTender in September 2026, however this timeframe may be subject to change.
Please note that this is not an RFT and does not commit the Department to proceed. The Close Date and Time stated in this notice relates to this pre-release notice only and does not reflect the proposed RFT commencement and closing dates for potential tenderers to lodge their submissions. The RFT, where undertaken, will be published on AusTender and will include the Closing Date and Time for lodgement of submissions.

publicQuestions.question: Is 11,000 kg GVM a strict maximum requirement, or would a higher GVM be acceptable? Current chassis options within the 11,000 kg GVM range are limited, and a higher-rated chassis may provide greater flexibility for payload, equipment stowage, and operational capability.
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Valued Suppliers,

The mandatory requirement of an 11 tonne GVM chassis can be found at Attachment A2 Specification Response Schedule C1.a. Suppliers should also pay particular attention to B4.a and B1.g in relation to proportionately balanced axel weights. This size is necessary for the RFSQ so that the appliance can be accommodated within existing stations and brigade sheds, can be effectively driven by volunteers and can traverse narrow tracks located in rural and remote parts of Queensland. Generally, it is recommended that suppliers consider heights to 3.1 metres and length to 7.8 metres (dual-cab).

Kind Regards,

Mabel

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Queensland Fire Department Procurement Team,

Regarding ITO VP512877 – Supply of Minimum 70 x Medium Attack Appliances, we have reviewed Parts A, B and C and the associated technical specifications.

Before commencing detailed engineering, chassis selection and commercial pricing, we kindly request clarification of the following:

1. Overseas Manufacturer Eligibility

Can an overseas fire appliance manufacturer participate directly as the prime tenderer without an Australian ABN/ACN, provided it appoints suitably qualified Australian subcontractors for vehicle certification, delivery, servicing and warranty support?

Is Australian company registration or a minimum Australian local-content percentage mandatory?

2. Vehicle Certification and Approvals

Can Australian Design Rules (ADR), NHVR vehicle modification certification and applicable vehicle registration approvals be completed through authorised Australian engineering partners after contract award but before vehicle delivery?

Which certificates and approvals must already be submitted with the tender?

3. Chassis Manufacturer Authorisation

Can the required cab-chassis OEM authorisation and evidence of training for vehicle modification and maintenance be provided after contract award, or must they accompany the initial tender submission?

4. Partial Offers and Contract Allocation

Would QFD accept separate offers for the 30 × 8,000 kg GVM vehicles and the 40 × 11,000 kg GVM vehicles, or for individual vehicle configurations?

Must every bidder offer all 70 appliances?

5. Technical Compliance and Alternatives

Where an overseas manufacturer proposes an equivalent technical solution meeting the required operational performance and safety standards, may it be submitted as an alternative offer?

Which specification requirements are strictly non-negotiable?

6. Financial Security and Insurance

Please confirm whether any bid security, bid bond, cash deposit or performance bank guarantee is required.

Can the required AUD 20 million public/products liability and AUD 5 million professional indemnity insurance policies be arranged after selection and before contract execution?

We would appreciate clear written confirmation, particularly regarding eligibility and the timing of technical approvals, so that manufacturers can commence compliant design and production planning without delay.

Thank you for your assistance.

publicQuestions.question:
Subject: Tender SC10186 – Request for Site Inspection and Clarifications

Dear Tender Team,

We are currently preparing our submission for Tender SC10186 – High-Pressure Cleaning Services and would appreciate clarification on the following matters:

Site inspection and scope

1. Would Council be able to arrange a site inspection or site briefing for prospective tenderers prior to the closing date?

2. Could Council provide an estimated breakdown of square metres requiring high-pressure cleaning at each of the 15 business centres?

3. Could Council clarify the exact boundaries of the cleaning areas, including whether kerbs, gutters, street furniture and adjoining public spaces are included in the annual cleaning program?

Existing contract and expenditure

4. Are these services currently delivered internally or through an external contractor? If outsourced, could Council identify the incumbent contractor?

5. Could Council provide the historical annual expenditure on these services for the past two financial years?

6. Approximately how many additional, urgent and emergency cleaning requests have been undertaken annually?

Operational requirements

7. Will Council provide access to water supply points at each location, or must contractors supply their own water?

8. Could Council clarify its specific requirements for wastewater collection, treatment and disposal?

9. Are any additional traffic management arrangements, permits or approvals anticipated for the nominated cleaning areas?

Contract structure

10. Would Council accept a tender from a principal contractor that manages the contract while subcontracting 100% of the physical cleaning services to suitably qualified and insured subcontractors?

11. Does Council intend to appoint a single contractor or establish a panel of service providers?

12. If a panel is established, how would work allocations be determined, and is there an anticipated minimum volume of work per provider?

Thank you for your assistance. We look forward to your response.

Kind regards
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Please see the below responses:

Site inspection and scope

1. Council does not intend to hold a formal site briefing or inspection. Tenderers may undertake their own inspections of the business centres during the tender period. Any inspections must be conducted from publicly accessible areas and in a manner that does not disrupt businesses, pedestrians or Council operations.

2. The total approximate area subject to the annual high-pressure cleaning program across the 15 business centres is 33,000 m².

3. All footpaths and paved areas are inside the Business Centres. Kerbs included to maintain visual appearance of footpath area.

Existing contract and expenditure

4. Currently carried out by several contractors on an ad-hoc basis.

5. Council will not be disclosing an indicative budget or historical expenditure for these services. Consistent with Council's procurement practices, Council resolved a number of years ago not to disclose indicative budgets for procurement activities, as doing so may influence pricing outcomes. This approach supports the achievement of competitive pricing and value for money through the tender process.

6. Less than five (5) annually.

Operational requirements

7. Contractors are required to supply their own water for the performance of the services.

8. Must be managed in accordance with relevant legislation and environmental requirements.

9. Potential for traffic control requirements when cleaning footpaths on arterial roads.

Contract structure

10. Yes, this will be considered if a conforming tender is submitted.

11. Council's preference is to appoint a single contractor to deliver the services under the contract. However, Council reserves the right to appoint more than one contractor should it determine that doing so represents the best value outcome and is in Council's interests.

12. This will depend on contractor availability. No minimum volume of work will be provided.

Thank you

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please clarify the following for the High-Pressure Cleaning Services tender?

1. On average, how many times per year is each of the 15 business centres currently pressure cleaned, including scheduled and ad hoc visits? Are any centres typically cleaned more than once a year? If so, could Council indicate which centres and how often?

2. Does the scope include any shopfront cleaning, such as exterior windows or building façades? If so, could Council confirm which locations and surfaces are included and how often they need to be cleaned?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Please see the below responses.

1. Currently, scheduled pressure cleaning is generally undertaken every 1 to 2 years across the business centres. In addition to these scheduled cleans, Council undertakes ad hoc or spot cleaning throughout the year as required to address specific issues.

As part of this procurement, Council may seek to increase the frequency and overall standard of pressure cleaning services. No centres are currently subject to a fixed cleaning schedule of more than once per year; however, ad hoc cleaning may result in some locations receiving additional cleaning visits where operationally required.

2. No. The scope does not include the cleaning of shopfronts, exterior windows, or building façades.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Section 1 of the RFI describes the process as establishing a register of pre-qualified suppliers, with the SLA confirming pre-qualification. However, the draft SLA expressly states that inclusion does not constitute pre-qualification, approval or endorsement.

•	Is the intention to assess suppliers' overall capability to deliver Targeted Engagement Programs, or are we required to submit fully developed programs for assessment? Can programs instead be designed and negotiated with individual schools based on their needs?

•	Is there a defined scope or minimum set of requirements for what constitutes a Targeted Engagement Program?

•	Can programs include community-based activities, outreach and off-site learning experiences for disengaged students, or are they intended to be delivered exclusively on school premises?

•	Can suppliers nominate multiple programs or service models, and subsequently add or amend these without undergoing the full assessment process again?

4. With regard to contractual arrangements and responsibilities –

•	Will the Department provide a standard agreement for schools to use when engaging suppliers, or will contracts be negotiated directly between schools and providers?

•	How will responsibilities for student supervision, duty of care, risk assessment, attendance and incident management be shared between schools and providers?

•	Will schools be responsible for obtaining parental consent, assessing student suitability and providing relevant information about student needs and risks before participation?

•	Will providers retain the ability to decline or discontinue a student's participation where there are concerns about their suitability or safety?

5. With regard to insurance and liability –

•	Is product liability insurance mandatory for providers delivering educational and engagement programs that do not involve supplying products?

6. Assessment and ongoing requirements –

publicQuestions.answer:
RFI Section 1:

1. Section 1 of the RFI describes the process as establishing a register of pre-qualified suppliers, with the SLA confirming pre-qualification.

The draft SLA expressly states that inclusion does not constitute pre-qualification, approval or endorsement.

Q1. Could you clarify the intended status and purpose of the register?

Clarification Q1: A revised RFI has been launched on VendorPanel which clarifies the purpose of the register.

Q2.a). How will this framework interact with existing arrangements between schools and external service providers, including Approved External Agency (AEA) arrangements for Youth Support Coordinators/Student Wellbeing Officers?

Clarification Q2a): TEP is a new program offering a range of services to a broader cohort of eligible students.

Q2b). Will providers delivering existing programs need to participate in this process to continue offering those services? Clarification Q2b): No

Q2c). Will existing contracts or arrangements be affected? Clarification Q2c): No.

Q3a). With regard to the scope of Targeted Engagement Programs – Is the intention to assess suppliers' overall capability to deliver Targeted Engagement Programs? Clarification Q3a): No.

Q3b). Will providers delivering existing programs need to participate in this process to continue offering those services? Clarification Q3b): No

Q3c). Can programs instead be designed and negotiated with individual schools based on their needs?

Clarification Q3c): Programs can be designed and negotiated with individual schools based on their needs.

Q3d). Is there a defined scope or minimum set of requirements for what constitutes a Targeted Engagement Program?

Clarification Q3d): Clarification: Refer to the RFI documentation which sets out the minimum criteria.

Q3e). Can programs include community-based activities, outreach and off-site learning experiences for disengaged students, or are they intended to be delivered exclusively on school premises?

Clarification Q3e): The schools will determine the specific requirements which will outline delivery requirements and locations.

Q3f). Can suppliers nominate multiple programs or service models, and subsequently add or amend these without undergoing the full assessment process again?

Clarification Q3f): Suppliers are recommended to identify all programs/service models suitable for TEP delivery to avoid potential re-assessment.

Q4. With regard to contractual arrangements and responsibilities –

Q4a). Will the Department provide a standard agreement for schools to use when engaging suppliers, or will contracts be negotiated directly between schools and providers?

Clarification Q4a). This is outlined in the RFI revision 1 - Schools will be provided with a Short-form Contract where the school's specific requirements will be negotiated with the selected Supplier

Q4b). How will responsibilities for student supervision, duty of care, risk assessment, attendance and incident management be shared between schools and providers?

Clarification 4b): This is outlined in the Short-form Contract which will also include their School Details Form.

Q4c). Will schools be responsible for obtaining parental consent, assessing student suitability and providing relevant information about student needs and risks before participation?

Clarification Q4c): The Supplier must obtain additional consent forms from the students and parents/guardians enrolled in the Program before starting the Program.

Q4d). Will providers retain the ability to decline or discontinue a student's participation where there are concerns about their suitability or safety?

Clarification Q4d): Parents/caregivers and/or school staff (i.e. teachers) may nominate eligible students for enrolment in the Program.

The School Principal must approve the enrolment and withdrawal of students from the Program. If Our School Principal determines a student is to be withdrawn from the Program, the date of and reasons for their withdrawal must be provided.

Q5. With regard to insurance and liability –

Is product liability insurance mandatory for providers delivering educational and engagement programs that do not involve supplying products?

Clarification Q5: Product Liability Insurance may be required if the Supplier provides products or equipment as part of the TEP deliverables specified by the school. This will be determined on a case-by-case basis.

Q6. Assessment and ongoing requirements.

 Q1a). Will the register identify the specific programs or types of services each supplier has been assessed as capable of delivering?

Clarification Q1a): No, the register will only state what regions of QLD the supplier services.

Q1b). Beyond the reassessment process outlined in the SLA, will the suppliers be required to provide regular performance or program outcome reporting to the Department.

Clarification Q1b): Yes, this will be outlined in the Short-form Contract between the School and the Supplier.

Q7. When it comes to attaching documents, is there a maximum amount that can be uploaded?

Q7 Clarification: The RFI section two (2) - Supplier's Response advises criteria and information required. Responses of max 500 words to each Criteria is advised. The requirement is that each criterion is responded to with relevant information within the maximum word count. There has been no limit of supporting documentation requested, however supporting documents should be aligned with the criteria questions.

Q8. Can you please confirm is sole traders are allowed to apply?

Clarification Q8: Sole traders can apply however they must comply to the mandatory requirements, and have the Capability, Experience and Capacity to provide the required services as set out in Section 2, item 3 of the RFI as well as completing all requirements of the RFI including the Supplier Authorisation (Item 5).

title: CN2027-025 – Water and Wastewater Condition Assessment
description:
The Water and Wastewater Condition Assessment Program is one of the projects being delivered through the Major Capital & Recovery Works Program of Douglas Shire Council (DSC) under contract CN2025-066. The project is supported by the Queensland Reconstruction Authority (QRA) Water Betterment funding.

Tropical Cyclone (TC) Jasper crossed the Queensland coast in the vicinity of Wujal Wujal in north Queensland on the evening of the 13th of December 2023. TC Jasper was associated with an extraordinary flooding event causing significant impacts to the region in north Queensland.

In the months following TC Jasper (16th of December 2023 to May 2025), pipeline failures increased noticeably against pre-event rates. It is considered that the cause of failure is in part, a result of the events that occurred during TC Jasper, including significant ground movement, prolonged saturation of the soil surrounding buried assets, and significant pressure fluctuation caused by repeated starting and stopping of the water supply, stressing pipe walls and joints. The traditional age-based renewal trigger previously used by DSC is likely to be inaccurate because it assumes typical operating conditions.

Therefore, the intent of the Water and Wastewater Condition Assessment Program is to undertake a complete condition assessment of DSC’s water supply and sewerage asset base so that renewal prioritisation moves from age-based triggers to measured condition, and so that post-TC Jasper renewal liability is quantified with field evidence rather than desktop estimation.

THIS TENDER REQUIRES A MANDATORY SITE VISIT.

Please provide the existing approved airside evacuation arrangements and identify the routes, perimeter gates and assembly areas available to serve the upgraded terminal. Please confirm airport security restrictions affecting emergency gate operation, including any required fire alarm or access control interfaces.

Reference: PPR Emergency and Evacuation Plan, page 22. NCC D2D15 and D3D26.

RFI 007 Water supply pressure and flow testing

Please provide a current water authority statement of available pressure and flow, together with site pressure and flow test results representative of the proposed fire service connection. Results should identify the test location and date, static pressure, residual pressures and corresponding flow rates, and any supply limitations. If current results are unavailable, please arrange testing before tender close. We have experienced low water pressure on other works in the area and need this information to assess potential fire water storage, pumps or supply upgrades. Please also provide records of existing fire water infrastructure available to serve the terminal.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 9 and 12. NCC E1D2 and AS 2419.1. FRNSW Hydraulic fire safety system design position statement.

RFI 008 Retained glazing and Section J upgrade scope

Please provide any existing energy assessment and clarify the required treatment of retained glazing and building fabric where existing and new spaces are combined. Please confirm the scope boundary for upgrades identified by the contractor's Section J assessment, including retained departure lounge glazing and areas outside the highlighted refurbishment footprint.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10 and 23. PPR Sustainability, page 29. NCC Section J.

RFI 009 Mechanical coverage and performance requirements

Section 10 requires new reverse cycle heating and cooling throughout the entire terminal. Please provide Council's required indoor design conditions, operating hours and zoning criteria, including the front waiting area, cafe, baggage collection and exit areas. Please identify any spaces intended to remain unconditioned and requirements associated with frequently opening external doors.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 10, pages 13 and 14. PPR Mechanical, pages 26 and 27.

RFI 010 Alternative heating solutions

Would Council consider hydronic or radiant heating as a supplement to, or a separately priced alternative to, the specified reverse cycle arrangement? Please confirm the acceptance criteria and tender presentation requirements for any alternative proposed to address the high internal spaces and intermittent terminal occupancy.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 10. PPR Value for Money, page 20.

 RFI 011 Plant room location discrepancy

Please reconcile the plant room shown on CD2 and the north elevation on CD3 around grids 6 and 7 with Section EE on CD4, which shows plant above the parents room and cafeteria around grids 5 and 6. Please confirm any mandatory location or slab requirement and whether alternative engineered support arrangements may be proposed.

Reference: CD2, CD3 and CD4 Section EE. Design Requirements Section 22, page 34.

RFI 012 Plant access and external openings

Please arrange tender inspection access to the plant rooms and equipment that could not be accessed during the site visit. Please identify restrictions on introducing external louvres, maintenance openings or temporary openings for plant removal and replacement, and any plant access routes that must remain available throughout construction.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10, 22 and 24. PPR Roof and Other High Level Access, page 21.

RFI 013 Existing structural drawings and investigation records

Please provide the 1984 and 2007 existing airport drawings referenced in the PPR attachments, together with any available original structural calculations and historical geotechnical records, including records held by the original structural engineer. We note that no geotechnical report has been issued and that existing information requires verification by the contractor.

Reference: PPR Site Information, pages 13 and 14, and Section 7 Attachments. Design Requirements Sections 2, 3 and 7.

RFI 014 Electrical supply capacity and upgrade boundaries

Please provide available electrical single line diagrams, switchboard schedules, supply capacity information and relevant authority correspondence. Please confirm the geographical extent of incoming supply upgrades to be included, including any upstream network works, and identify known supply authority restrictions or required upgrades relevant to the proposed terminal loads.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 11, page 15. PPR Electrical, page 25.

RFI 015 Stormwater infrastructure and drainage constraints

Please provide existing drainage surveys and records showing pipe sizes, levels, pits and outfalls around the road and proposed extension. Please identify infrastructure that must remain in position, approved discharge points, and restrictions on diversions or road excavation. Please confirm any mandatory constraints affecting roof drainage connections and overflow discharge locations.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 8, page 11. PPR Civil and Roof Drainage, pages 24 and 25.

 RFI 016 Cafe scope and retained fitout

Section 19 states that the cafe is to remain generally unchanged. Please confirm whether Council requires any cafe fitout or equipment work beyond the specified replacement furniture, protection and necessary service interfaces. Please identify additional requirements arising from the existing lease or cafe operator, including any nominated future tenancy works.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 19 and 20. Furniture Schedule DEP-04.

RFI 017 Furniture quantities and charging positions

Please confirm whether the minimum 160 departure seats, 20 table or stool or chair positions, 20 working bench positions, four modular or booth sets and four cafe sets are separate cumulative requirements. Please nominate seats per booth set and chairs per cafe set, and confirm the required overall seating capacity. Please confirm the charging requirements for each relevant furniture group.

Reference: Furniture Schedule DEP-02 to DEP-06. Design Requirements Sections 20.2, 20.3 and 20.5.

RFI 018 Screening equipment and passenger recomposure facilities

Please provide the Council supplied screening equipment schedule, layouts, service requirements, installation clearances and delivery dates. Please confirm responsibility for equipment installation and commissioning. Please also confirm the required quantity and arrangement of seating and benches immediately after screening for passengers to replace footwear and repack belongings.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 14, pages 20 and 21, and Section 18, page 26.

RFI 019 Aboriginal artwork and relocation requirements

Section 20.4 requires retention or relocation of existing artwork glazing, while CD2 identifies cladding with Indigenous artwork. Please confirm whether the cladding incorporates relocated artwork, reproduction of existing images or newly commissioned artwork. Please provide the required extent, relocation destination and approval arrangements, including any restrictions on removal or temporary storage.

Reference: CD2. Design Requirements Section 20.4, page 29.

RFI 020 Curved roof barge and external door requirements

Please confirm any mandatory architectural requirements for the curved roof barge, including whether a continuous rolled finish is required or segmented construction is acceptable. Please also identify any nominated external door construction, or confirm that durable metal faced or metal clad doors may be proposed through design development.

Reference: CD3 and CD4. Design Requirements Sections 5, 20 and 23.

RFI 021 Operational staging and service changeovers

Please provide operational restrictions relevant to staging, including minimum passenger facilities, permitted service shutdown windows, cafe continuity requirements and notice periods. Please identify constraints affecting mechanical plant removal, temporary heating and cooling, and retention of existing walls until later construction stages. Please confirm the process and review periods for approving these arrangements.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 6, 24 and 25. PPR Contractor's Program and Emergency and Evacuation Plan.

1.	Can you please provide the Draft Schedule/Program mentioned in PPR3.3 (attached to the RFT Terms).

Tenderers are to develop and submit their own proposed project program, incorporating the relevant activities and work packages identified in Part B2 – Returnable Schedules (Pricing), together with the design, construction, approval, coordination, testing and commissioning requirements outlined in the Principal’s Project Requirements and Design Requirements.

2.
Is there a hazardous materials register for the 1984 terminal? PPR 6.8.5 refers to areas Council will remedy separately, but none are identified

Council has an Asbestos Register and Management Plan for the Wagga Wagga Regional Airport. This is the only hazardous materials register currently available and is provided with this tender clarification for reference.

The register identifies asbestos-containing materials in certain airport buildings and also notes limitations to the inspection, including areas that were not readily accessible.

Tenderers shall review the register and consider its findings and limitations when developing their tender submissions and proposed construction methodology. Where works may disturb suspected asbestos-containing materials, the Contractor shall undertake the necessary investigations and manage the materials in accordance with applicable legislation and the project requirements.

4.
The BMS Work Specification is an image-only PDF. Is a searchable version available?

The BMS Work Specification issued with the RFT is the available version of the document. A searchable electronic version is not currently available for issue.

Tenderers shall refer to the specification provided and allow for the requirements contained within it.

- 1 week (PPR 1.2, Agenda item 4.06),

- 2 weeks (PPR 5.7.4) and

publicQuestions.question:
What is the council’s required timeframe for completion?

Please advise of the physical security requirements for the building including elements such as wall construction specification, wall heights, glass specifications etc.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Required Timeframe for Completion

Council has not specified a separate timeframe for completion. The Contractor shall develop and submit a detailed program identifying the proposed design, approvals, construction, testing, commissioning and handover activities, with completion in accordance with the submitted and approved program and the Contract requirements.

2.	Physical Security Requirements

The Contractor shall provide physical security measures appropriate for the Airport Terminal, in accordance with the RFT requirements, applicable aviation security legislation, the Airport Operator's security requirements and the National Construction Code (NCC).

The RFT does not prescribe specific wall construction specifications, minimum wall heights or security glazing specifications. These shall be determined by the Contractor as part of the detailed design, taking into consideration the security requirements of the building and the separation between public, staff and security-controlled areas.

Glazing shall comply with the applicable NCC requirements and relevant Australian Standards, including AS 1288 (Glass in buildings – Selection and installation) and AS 2047 (Windows and external glazed doors in buildings), as applicable.

The Contractor shall submit the proposed wall, door and glazing specifications and associated security arrangements to Council and the Airport Operator for review and approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Please see below RFIs:

Can you please confirm the scope of works to occur within the 'Cafe/Caffeteria' space?

Are there any height restrictions/requirements for crane operations during construction?

Can you please confirm the number of seats that need to be supplied for the 'Departure Lounges'. There is a quantity of 378 shown in the concept drawings which conflicts with the 160 listed on the Furniture & Finishes Schedule.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The existing café area within the Airport Terminal is to remain generally unchanged as part of the project.

The Contractor shall allow for protection of the existing cafe fitout and equipment, together with coordination of any necessary building services interfaces associated with the Works.

No additional cafe fitout or equipment replacement is required beyond the documented scope. Any works arising from the existing cafe lease or operator requirements that are not identified in the RFT documentation shall be referred to Council for direction.

2. No specific maximum crane height.

The Contractor shall coordinate all crane and lifting operations with Council and the Airport Operator before commencement. The Contractor shall submit a crane and lifting plan identifying the proposed crane location and configuration, date and duration, maximum crane height, operating radius and potential impacts on aircraft operations, passenger movements, airport access, security and emergency access.

All required approvals must be obtained before crane operations commence. Operations shall only occur during approved hours. Any operation outside approved hours requires prior approval from Council and the Airport Operator.

3. The concept drawings are provided for reference purposes only. The Contractor shall allow for the supply and installation of all seating and furniture in accordance with the quantities specified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule.

DEP-05: 20 working bench positions.

The quantity of 378 seats shown on the concept drawings is indicative only and does not override the quantities specified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule.

The Contractor shall develop the final furniture layout and propose the number of seats within each booth and cafe furniture set, ensuring adequate passenger circulation and accessible paths of travel, for Council's review and approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Can you please review and respond to below:

Pricing and contract

1.	Where provisional sums and alternatives go. “The pricing schedule (Part B2) has no line items for the provisional sums and separately priced alternatives Council has asked for. These are the slat ceiling, bathroom compliance changes, and the hydronic/radiant heating alternative. Please confirm how and where these are to be shown.”

2.	Unknown risks. “Will Council accept provisional sums for items that can’t be quantified before tender? These are asbestos or hazardous materials outside the 2015 register, a substation or supply authority upgrade, and fire water storage or pumps. PPR 6.8.5 refers to areas ‘the Principal will remedy separately’. Please confirm whether hazardous materials not identified in the register will be treated as a variation.”

3.	Completion date and novation. “The Date for Practical Completion is ‘TBC’ (Annexure Item 9) and liquidated damages are $2,000 per day. Please confirm the date will be set from the tendered program, and whether any separable portions apply. Please also clarify what Council expects tenderers to nominate under Item 24 (subcontractors that may be novated).”

Services

4.	Substation upgrade. “If maximum demand exceeds the existing 300 kVA substation, are the substation and upstream network works in the Contractor’s scope? Has Council had any correspondence with the network operator?”

5.	Fire detection. “The Fire Safety Schedule (7 Jul 2025) lists no fire detection or alarm system. Please confirm whether the terminal has any detection or occupant warning system. If the Works trigger one, is it required for the whole terminal or only for new and altered areas? Please also provide the fire safety certification mentioned in RFI 002 once it is issued.”

Airport security and operations

6.	Security approvals. “Will the upgrade need a change to the airport’s Transport Security Program or approvals. If so, who prepares and lodges it, and how long should the program allow?”

7.	Screening during construction. “Will the existing screening equipment stay in use until the ProVision 2 is commissioned? Is removing the existing equipment in the Contractor’s scope? When will Council deliver the ProVision 2, and who receives and stores it?”

8.	Working hours. “The PPR allows work from 7 am to 5 pm on weekdays. Will Council permit night or weekend work for shutdowns, noisy work, and work in passenger areas outside flight times?”

Scope gaps

10.	Passenger information. “What does pricing item E3 (passenger information systems) require? Please give the number and locations of flight information screens, the existing system or data feed, and who supplies the software and licences.”

11.	Hire car desk and pay station. “Who supplies the car park pay station machine, and what parking management system and supplier must it connect to? Is the hire car desk one shared counter or one per operator?”

12.	Public Wi-Fi. “Is public passenger Wi-Fi required, and does Council have an existing provider?”

Approvals and design

14.	REF timing. “What timeframe should tenderers allow for Council’s REF determination? Can investigations or enabling works proceed before determination?”

15.	Artwork. “For the Indigenous artwork cladding, is there a budget or provisional sum? Who is responsible for engaging an artist and for Aboriginal community consultation?”
publicQuestions.answer:
Pricing and contract

1. Where Part B2 does not provide specific line items, Tenderers may provide the relevant provisional sums and separately priced alternatives on a separate sheet within the Returnable Schedules, clearly identifying and cross-referencing each item.

The base tender price shall remain clearly identifiable. Separately priced alternatives shall not be included in the base tender sum unless expressly stated.

2. The Contractor shall undertake site investigations and verify existing conditions. The 2015 Asbestos Register and Management Plan has been provided as available site information.

Under PPR Section 6.8.5, the Contractor must immediately notify the Superintendent if asbestos or other contamination is discovered. The affected material must not be disturbed. The discovery of hazardous materials outside the areas identified in the 2015 register will be assessed in accordance with the Contract and will not automatically constitute a variation.

Council accepts substation or upstream network upgrades, and additional fire water storage or pumping infrastructure, as provisional items.

Tenderers shall separately identify and price these items as provisional sums in the Returnable Schedules. The final scope will be confirmed following the Contractor's investigations and consultation with the relevant service authorities. Any expenditure will be subject to Council's direction and acceptance in accordance with the Contract.

3. Tenderers shall provide a detailed construction program identifying the proposed duration, key milestones, critical path, design and approval periods, construction stages, testing, commissioning and handover.

The Date for Practical Completion will be established in accordance with the agreed Contract Period and the executed Contract. The applicable liquidated damages remain as stated in the Contract Annexure.

No separate separable portions have been identified in the RFT documentation. Any proposed separable portions shall be clearly identified by Tenderers, including their proposed scope and completion milestones, for Council's consideration.

Under Item 24, Tenderers shall identify any proposed subcontractors or specialist suppliers that they consider may be suitable for novation to Council or the successful Contractor, where applicable. Tenderers should provide the relevant company details, proposed scope of services and current contractual arrangements. Any novation will be subject to Council's review and agreement and the terms of the Contract.

Services

4.The Contractor shall undertake electrical investigations and maximum demand calculations to establish the capacity and suitability of the existing electrical supply for the proposed terminal upgrade. Where the existing supply or distribution infrastructure is inadequate, the Contractor shall identify the required upgrades and allow for the necessary electrical works.

The RFT does not confirm the available capacity of the existing 300 kVA substation or establish whether upstream network augmentation will be required. Tenderers shall identify this as a design and authority coordination risk and allow for investigations and consultation with the relevant electricity network operator.

Council will need to confirm whether any existing correspondence with the network operator is available for issue. The extent and responsibility for any upstream network augmentation will be clarified following confirmation of the maximum demand assessment and network operator requirements.

5. The Contractor shall investigate and verify the existing fire protection and life safety systems, including any existing detection and alarm arrangements, as part of the detailed design.

In accordance with Design Requirements Section 12 and the PPR Fire Services requirements, the Contractor shall develop the fire protection and life safety design for the completed terminal. This shall include fire detection, alarm and emergency warning systems as required by the applicable NCC, Australian Standards and approved design.

The extent of any new or modified system, including whether additional coverage is required in retained areas, shall be determined through the Contractor's fire engineering and compliance assessment and submitted to Council for review.

Council will provide the available fire safety certification documentation once it has been finalised and is available for issue.

Airport security and operations

6.The Airport's Transport Security Program (TSP) will require amendment to accommodate the proposed upgrade. The amendment will be prepared and lodged by Airport Management.

The Contractor shall coordinate with Airport Management and allow for the required consultation and approval process within the construction program.

7.The existing screening equipment will remain operational throughout the works.

Council will receive and store the ProVision 2 equipment and arrange delivery to site when required. The existing screening equipment provider will be responsible for relocating and removing the existing equipment as required.

The Contractor shall coordinate with Council, Airport Management and the equipment providers to facilitate the installation and integration of the ProVision 2 into the terminal.

8. The permitted working hours are 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, Monday to Friday. Saturday works require prior approval from the Superintendent. Work on Sundays and public holidays is not permitted without prior written approval.

Any proposed night works, weekend works, noisy activities or works requiring service shutdowns or access to passenger areas outside the permitted hours must be submitted to the Superintendent for approval. Tenderers shall identify these activities in their construction methodology and program. All works must be coordinated with Airport Management to minimise disruption to airport operations.

Approval for works outside the permitted hours will be subject to Council's consideration and is not guaranteed.

Scope gaps

10. Council confirms that the existing Flight Information Display System (FIDS) is a standalone system operated by the airport check-in staff.

The existing arrangement includes two display screens at the check-in area, with a small cabinet housing the computer.

Two additional display screens will be provided in the passenger seating area.

The Contractor shall allow for the installation of the additional screens, including the required power and communications connections, and coordinate with Council regarding integration with the existing FIDS.

11.

Car Park Pay Station

APS is the existing car park service provider. Council will arrange with APS to relocate the existing pay station to the new location.

The Contractor shall provide the required power point at the new location. Council will arrange for the relocation of the existing communications cabling.

Hire Car Desk

The hire car desk shall comprise one continuous bench counter with six (6) individual workstations, one for each hire car operator.

The Contractor shall allow for the supply and installation of the counter, including the required power points and relocation of existing communications connections to the new location.

12. The public passenger Wi-Fi service is owned and operated by Council.

The Contractor shall coordinate with Council's IT team to confirm the required network connections, data cabling, equipment locations, power supply, network access and integration with the existing Council network. The Contractor shall submit the proposed arrangements to Council's IT team for review and approval prior to installation.

The Contractor shall also coordinate testing and commissioning with Council's IT team to ensure the Wi-Fi service is operational before handover.

Approvals and design

14. A period of two (2) weeks for review and determination of the REF following submission of the complete REF and supporting documentation.

The Contractor shall prepare and submit the REF and supporting documentation to Council and allow for the two-week review period in the construction program.

Site investigations may proceed before REF determination, provided they are legally permissible and all necessary approvals are obtained. Construction or enabling works requiring REF determination or other statutory approvals shall not commence until the relevant approvals are in place.

15. Council will be responsible for engaging the artist and undertaking the Aboriginal community consultation.

The Contractor shall allow for the design and detailing required to carefully remove and relocate the existing Indigenous artwork cladding to an alternative location within the Airport, as agreed with Council.

The Contractor shall also allow for the careful removal, protection, relocation and reinstallation of the existing artwork, including all associated installation works.

For tender pricing, can we assume that the existing pits in this car park discharge into the adjacent stormwater line and that the pit affected by the proposed extension can be relocated and reconnected to that same line?

2- Permanent relocation of the car park vehicle entry

For the car park shown on Detail 2/CD1, Rev B, please confirm the proposed location and extent of works for the permanent relocation of the vehicle entry. Should tenderers allow for a new concrete layback and hardstand, including tie-ins to the existing access road and car park pavement?

3- New footpaths

Please provide a marked-up plan showing the location, widths and extent of new footpaths around the building, including any connections to existing paths.

4- Existing toilet refurbishment

Please confirm whether tenderers are to allow for refurbishing the existing toilets within the current layout or reconfiguring them to meet current accessibility requirements. Please confirm the extent of refurbishment works and provide a revised floor plan for pricing if the layout is to change.

5- Cafe refurbishment and equipment

Please confirm the extent of the cafe refurbishment, including which parts of the existing fitout and equipment are to be retained, relocated or replaced. Please provide any available fitout drawings and equipment schedules, and confirm who is responsible for supplying, installing and connecting each item of new equipment.

6- Mechanical services replacement and NCC Section J

The proposed mechanical upgrade appears to require replacement of the existing evaporative cooling and gas heating systems throughout the terminal. Please confirm the extent of replacement tenderers are to allow for, including whether the works extend beyond the refurbishment areas and whether any existing plant, ductwork or controls are to be retained.

Please confirm what NCC Section J requirements apply to the existing building envelope in connection with the mechanical upgrade. The existing glazing appears unlikely to achieve the thermal performance expected of new glazing. For tender pricing, can tenderers assume the existing glazing and frames will be retained, or should upgrades be included?

If upgrades to the glazing or other parts of the existing envelope are required, please identify the affected areas, extent of works and target thermal performance, and provide any available Section J assessment

publicQuestions.question:
The Principal’s Project Requirements (pp. 9 and 14) require the Contractor to prepare the Review of Environmental Factors (REF) and supporting assessments for Council’s Part 5 determination. Given the proposed terminal extension and associated excavation for footings, stormwater and services, please clarify the following.

1- Please provide any existing AHIMS searches, Aboriginal heritage assessments or due diligence reports held by Council or Defence that cover the proposed works area.

2- Please confirm whether Council requires a standalone Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Assessment Report (ACHAR) for the REF, or whether documented due diligence will be accepted where the findings support a low-risk conclusion.

3- Please confirm whether Council or Defence has already consulted with relevant Traditional Owners or other Aboriginal stakeholders. If further consultation is required, please confirm who will lead it, when it must be completed and whether any Defence heritage clearance is required.

4- If the need for further assessment will only be known after initial due diligence, please confirm the pricing and programme allowances tenderers should adopt for any field investigations, consultation, formal assessment or Aboriginal Heritage Impact Permit.
publicQuestions.answer:
Please ref to uploaded AHIMS search report dated 17 November 2026 (AHMIS Report Airport).

The search identified no recorded Aboriginal sites or declared Aboriginal places within or near the proposed works area.

The Contractor is only required to include the attached AHIMS report with the REF submission. No pricing or allowance is required from the Contractor for Aboriginal heritage due diligence, consultation or further assessments.

WWCC will undertake the Aboriginal heritage due diligence, coordinate consultation with the relevant Aboriginal stakeholders and prepare any further reports required, including an Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Assessment Report (ACHAR), if necessary. WWCC will also arrange and provide an Aboriginal Heritage Impact Permit (AHIP), if required.

WWCC is not currently aware of any Defence heritage constraints affecting the proposed works. No relevant items have been identified on the NSW State Heritage Register. If any Defence heritage clearance or approval is required, we will coordinate and provide the necessary approval.

No further Aboriginal heritage assessment, consultation or approval costs are to be included in the Contractor's tender price.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement Team,

Please clarify the following for RFT CT2027017 Wagga Wagga Airport Terminal Upgrade.

1. Second plantroom. The marked-up sections issued on 17 November (Markup 5.11.2026, Sections CC and EE) show a "Possible plant room" over Grids 5-6, above the existing parents room and cafe. The response to RFI 011 (4 November) states that the plantroom is not intended to be located above the parents room or cafe. Please confirm whether tenderers should allow for one plantroom only, over the new toilets, or also for the possible plantroom over Grids 5-6.

2. Baggage make-up building. Design Requirements Section 10 and the response to RFI 009 require reverse-cycle heating and cooling to the "entire Airport Terminal". Does this include the 2007 baggage make-up building, or only the passenger terminal areas?

3. Provisional sums. Council's answer of 18 November asks for provisional sums to be shown on a separate sheet within the Returnable Schedules. Please confirm whether the provisional sums (existing bathroom compliance works, substation or upstream network upgrade, and fire water storage and pumps) are to be included in the lump sum in Returnable Schedule 2, or shown only on the separate sheet and excluded from the lump sum.

4. Council sewer. Before You Dig records show a Council gravity sewer about 15-20 m west of the existing west wall, on or beside the extension footprint and the Grid 9 footings. Will Council, as sewer authority, allow building over or beside the sewer (for example on piers founded below the zone of influence), or will it require encasement or a diversion? As this cannot be verified before tender, will Council accept sewer protection or diversion, and any new stormwater outfall needed if the existing car park drainage is found unsuitable, as provisional sums in the same way as the substation and fire water items?

5. Network operator correspondence. Council's answer of 18 November noted it would confirm whether any existing correspondence with the electricity network operator is available. If any exists, please issue it before tender close.

6. Floodlight mast. The floodlight mast beside the existing baggage claim awning, at the west end of the terminal, appears to be in or next to the works. Who owns it, and is its relocation part of the Contractor's scope?

7. Tile mural. The external tile mural on the curved brick wall at the west end of the terminal is in the works area. Is it to be salvaged and reinstated, handed to Council, or demolished? If it is Aboriginal artwork, please confirm it is to be treated under Design Requirements Section 20.4.

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The preferred location for the new plantroom is above the proposed toilet area. However, the final plantroom size and arrangement will depend on the mechanical system selected by the Contractor.

If the selected system requires additional space, the Contractor shall propose a suitable alternative arrangement, including any additional plantroom area required, for Council's review and approval. The plantroom shown above the existing parents' room and café is not a confirmed requirement.

2. The new reverse-cycle heating and cooling system is required throughout the passenger terminal areas only (Arrivals & Departure). No mechanical upgrades required to baggage make-up building area.

3. The following items shall be separately identified and priced as provisional sums on a separate sheet within the Returnable Schedules:

•	Additional compliance works to existing bathrooms.

•	Substation or upstream electricity network upgrades.

•	Additional fire water storage and pumping infrastructure.

These provisional sums are to be excluded from the base lump sum tender price. Any expenditure will be subject to Council's direction and acceptance in accordance with the Contract.

4. Council accepts sewer protection/diversion works and any required new stormwater outfall to be included as provisional sums in the Returnable Schedules, subject to investigation and confirmation of the required works.

5. Council has provided the available incoming mains voltage and current monitoring records for reference. No network operator correspondence confirming upgrade requirements has been identified.

6.The floodlight mast relocation, if required, will be undertaken by Council in accordance with the relevant regulations. Tenderers are not required to include this work in their scope or pricing.

7. The existing external tile mural can be demolished as part of the works. No salvage or reinstatement is required.

title: RFT260119 Park Avenue WWTP Emerald - Sedimentation Tanks - Cleaning & Remedial Works
description: Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking to engage a suitably qualified and experienced Contractor to conduct high-pressure water cleaning and concrete remedial works on two primary sedimentation tanks at Park Avenue WWTP located in Emerald. The plant is an operational treatment facility, and works must be completed with minimal disruption to process.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
20 Rivergum Dr
Emerald, Queensland 4720
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Central Highlands region is in Central Queensland, Australia. The region encompasses an area of around 60 000 square kilometres, making it just short of the size of Tasmania.

It is home to around 30 000 people who live in the thirteen unique communities of Arcadia Valley, Bauhinia, Blackwater, Bluff, Capella, Comet, Dingo, Duaringa, Emerald, Rolleston, Sapphire Gemfields, Springsure and Tieri.

Our region is rich in minerals and agriculture, thriving on irrigation sourced from water storage on the Nogoa and Comet rivers. We claim the largest sapphire-producing fields in the Southern Hemisphere.

Major freight routes through the region include the north-south link between Charters Towers and northern New South Wales—identified as the inland transport alternative between Cairns and Melbourne.
