publicQuestions.question:
Could you share how QGAir has previously arranged drug and alcohol testing at Horn Island, particularly after an incident? Were testers generally flown in from Cairns or another mainland base, or did QGAir use a qualified tester on Horn Island or Thursday Island?

If figures are available, roughly how many planned visits and urgent callouts were there in the past 12 months, and how many urgent callouts occurred overnight or on weekends?

We’d appreciate knowing what worked well, what caused delays and what QGAir would like the next provider to improve. In particular, when the next scheduled flight was too late to complete breath testing within eight hours of an incident, what arrangement worked in practice? If this hasn’t occurred, what fallback would QGAir consider acceptable?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your question.

QGAir has no confirmed historical delivery arrangements or a reliable breakdown of planned visits, urgent callouts and overnight or weekend attendance at Horn Island. We cannot provide verified figures or examples of previous incident responses at this stage. This should not be interpreted as nil activity. Any further information made available will be shared with all participating suppliers through VendorPanel.

The RFP invites suppliers to propose a practical service model for Horn Island. This may involve local providers on Horn Island or Thursday Island, mainland-based personnel, or a combination of arrangements. Suppliers should distinguish existing capability from arrangements that would need to be established before commencement. QGAir is seeking timely access to testing, clear arrangements for urgent requests and reliable alternatives when travel or local services are unavailable. Proposals should explain:

-how planned and urgent testing would be delivered, including overnight and weekend coverage

-how alcohol testing within eight hours and drug testing within 32 hours of an accident or serious incident would be supported

-the proposed fallback where scheduled flights would not allow testing within those timeframes

-any limitations, dependencies, establishment costs or additional callout and travel charges.

Suppliers may propose separate arrangements for local breath testing and urine collection, provided they explain how each would meet the specified testing, competency, equipment, reporting and quality requirements. Any reliance on QGAir personnel, equipment or transport must be expressly identified and must not be assumed.

QGAir has not nominated a pre-approved fallback for circumstances where timely testing cannot be achieved. Proposed alternatives will be assessed against the RFP requirements and QGAir’s DAMP.

Suppliers must clearly identify any circumstances in which they cannot meet the required timeframes, together with their proposed escalation and response arrangements.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

We would like to clarify please whether 'clinics' a mandatory requirement or simply a wording choice? Can all testing be conducted on site at QGAir locations or are there specific instances where off site testing must be conducted please?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your question.

References to clinics describe an intended service delivery option. The Supplier is not required to own or operate a clinic and may provide this capability through suitable collection centres, subcontractors, or partner providers.

QGAir requires both onsite testing and access to offsite testing. Offsite testing is specifically included for pre-employment or commencement testing, including candidates located outside QGAir’s primary locations. The indicative pricing assumptions also use clinic-based testing for Mt Isa routine testing and additional individual testing, such as missed or return-to-work tests.

Planned group testing is generally intended to occur onsite at QGAir locations. The location for other testing events will depend on the circumstances, available facilities, and the authorised testing request. Suppliers should not assume that every person requiring testing can attend a QGAir base.

Suppliers may propose an alternative delivery model, including greater use of mobile or onsite testing.

The proposal must explain how it would meet the complete requirement, including access for pre-employment candidates outside QGAir locations, individual appointments, and urgent testing. Identify any reliance on QGAir facilities or personnel, service limitations, and all associated charges.

Any alternative must be clearly identified, with departures recorded in Section 2.3. QGAir will assess the proposed arrangements against the RFP requirements, service accessibility, and value for money.

title: BSC - AERODROME RUNWAY AND TAXIWAY PAVEMENT RENEWAL, RESEALING AND LINE MARKING
description:
Balranald Shire Council invites quotations from suitably qualified contractors for the assessment, surface correction, resealing and remarking of the sealed runway and taxiway at Balranald Aerodrome.

The objective of this project is to improve pavement condition, rectify ride quality concerns, address localised ponding issues where practical, extend pavement life and reinstate all required aerodrome markings in accordance with applicable aviation standards. The aerodrome's runway and taxiway have undergone periodic crack sealing over recent years, and Council has identified surface irregularities, rough ride characteristics and localised water ponding requiring investigation and treatment.

All aerodrome markings shall be reinstated in accordance with the applicable requirements of Part 139 (Aerodromes) Manual of Standards 2020 and relevant guidance material issued by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA).

title: Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment
description:
The Opportunity:

Ports North is pleased to advise that Request for Proposal (RFP) Phase 1 for the Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment Opportunity has now commenced.

Ports North is proposing the development of the Cairns Marine Precinct – Common User Facility, a major maritime infrastructure project, to expand the marine vessel maintenance capability and capacity in Far North Queensland to support the continued growth of the region’s maritime industry. The proposed facility responds to increasing demand for maritime maintenance, repair, and overhaul services as global vessel fleets expand and age, alongside sustained investment in Australia’s maritime defence capability driving long-term sustainment demand.

Ports North has identified a Finance (co-funded), Design, Build, Operate and Maintain (FDBOM) commercial delivery model as the most efficient means of Project delivery to successfully facilitate achievement of the Project Objectives. As the Project will benefit from a significant contribution of funds from the Queensland and Commonwealth Governments, the physical facilities coming into existence as a result of the Project will be a common user facility available for use by the operator and customers including vessel owners and ship maintenance and repair service providers.

Ports North is seeking a private sector proponent to co-fund, develop, operate and maintain the facility under a long-term arrangement on Ports North-owned land at the Port of Cairns.

This RFP follows the successful completion of an Expression of Interest (EOI) process. Participation in the EOI process was not a prerequisite for participation in RFP Phase 1. Ports North welcomes registrations and proposals from organisations that did not participate in the EOI and may be engaging with the opportunity for the first time.

Purpose of this Request for Proposal:

The purpose of this RFP is to elicit proposals from the market that address the Project Objectives and develop the CMP-CUF, including the following:

•	the co-funding of the Project;

•	the design, construction and commissioning of the CMP-CUF; and

•	the operation and maintenance of the CMP-CUF on a common user basis.

How to Participate in RFP Phase 1:

Proposals are being accepted only via the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room. Submissions via this Queensland Procurement Solution may not be eligible.

To participate:

- register online via https://www.portsnorth.com.au/ports-north-projects/cairns-marine-precinct

- Shortly after, Ports North will provide access to the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room

- Access the RFP documentation within the CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room

- Submit your RFP via the CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room prior to 1200 AEST on Friday 18 December 2026.

Enquiries regarding the procurement process may be directed to cmpenquiry@portsnorth.com.au.

title: ITT2550 - Sports Field Construction Packages - Honey Farm Road Sports Precinct
description:
Sunshine Coast Council is seeking experienced contractors for the construction of 3 x soccer and 2 x cricket turf sports fields and associated works. The site is located within Council’s Honey Farm Road Sports Precinct, 4 Honey Farm Road, Meridan Plains.

The scope of work will include, but not be limited to:

1.	Separable Portion 1 - Construction of 3 x turf soccer fields

2.	Separable Portion 2 - Construction of 2 x turf cricket fields.

Construction activities include:

·	Construction of turf fields, surrounds and access

·	Perimeter security

·	Survey of subgrade prior to handover and site possession

·	Importing of materials to site

·	Safe storage of materials on site

·	Fenced construction compound

·	Full rectification of any damaged surfaces – geotechnical approval of rectifications

·	Disposal of all waste materials

·	Full RPEQ certification of works

·	Survey pick up and full ADAC

·	Warranty and Maintenance period

It is anticipated that works will commence early 2027 with a minimum 6 month establishment period required prior to handing back to Council. Functional completion of all fields is required no later than February 2028.

Council reserves the right to award separable portions to separate contractors to ensure construction resourcing is sufficient to ensure all fields are established and operational by the required date.

The successful Contractors will be required to provide all materials, plant and labour, and to perform all necessary operations of whatever kind, to ensure the completion of works associated with this Contract.

Sites can be reorganised by suburb.

publicQuestions.question: Can we choose between horticulture or mowing? And should I bid for all parks and reserves or can select specific one's ?
publicQuestions.answer:
Can we choose between horticulture or mowing?

Yes. Tenderers may submit for Part A, Part B, or both Parts A and B. However, Council's current intention is not to award both parts to the same contractor.

Do we need to bid for all parks and reserves, or can we select specific sites?

No. Tenderers must submit pricing for all sites within the relevant tender part. Partial submissions for selected parks, reserves or sites will not be considered compliant. For example, a tender submission for Part A must include pricing for all Part A sites.

The formula in Column P of Table 1 – Part A – Lump Sum should be multiplied by 12 visits for Rows 182 to 205.

Tenderers should allow for 12 Routine Maintenance Interventions (RMIs) per annum for these items when completing their pricing.

The tender pricing sheet has been updated and added as Addendum1:

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - UPDATED Section B - Attachment 1 - Schedule 2 - Tender Prices - Addendum 1

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning,

We refer to document titled “2627-17 – Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services – Section D – Attachment 2 – Part A & B – Assets Table”.

We have identified the following discrepancies in the Road Reserves tab:

Q1. Row 86 appears to duplicate the information provided in Row 80. Can Council confirm if this is correct?

Q2. The street address for Row 89 appears to be missing. Can Council provide the applicable street address?

Can Council please clarify these matters and, if necessary, issue an amended spreadsheet?

Kind Regards
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Council confirms that Row 86 is a duplicate of Row 80 and was included in error. Duplicate has now been removed.

Q2. Council confirms the street address for Brady Road Overpass is - Next to 83 Brady Road, Dandenong North.

An amended Assets Table has been re-issued reflecting the above corrections.

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - Section D - Attachment 2 - Part A & B - Assets Table - Addendum 2

publicQuestions.question: When reviewing the asset list included with the attachments, is there any indication as which sites will require traffic management? Are sites listed as road reserves the only sites that will require traffic management?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council advises that Assets Table (Section D – Attachment 2) does not identify sites requiring traffic management.

Traffic management may be required at locations other than road reserves, depending on site-specific conditions and operational requirements.

Tenderers are encouraged to utilise the geopackage and associated asset location information to assess likely traffic management requirements.

Tenderers should make their own assessment and allow for any necessary traffic management within their submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Pricing Schedule – Site-Specific Pricing Clarification

The pricing schedule requests a rate per square metre (m²) for each site.

Could you please confirm whether contractors are permitted to provide an individually calculated fixed price for each site, rather than applying a standard m² rate?

The level of maintenance required varies significantly between sites due to factors such as trimming requirements, site layout, accessibility and walking distances.

Applying a standard m² rate across all sites may not accurately reflect the actual labour and maintenance requirements of each location.

We believe that pricing each site individually would allow for a more accurate and competitive quotation that better reflects the work required.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council acknowledges that maintenance requirements vary between sites.

Tenderers can submit pricing on a site-by-site basis, or apply a uniform rate to all sites, provided pricing is provided per intervention (Column O) and annual cost (Column P).

publicQuestions.question: In Relation to the SOR items for Mulch (S2.1,2 & 3), can I confirm if there is plant & Equipment available for Loading at Council Stockpile location or should the Contractor allow for Floating of equipment for loading in m3 rate? To avoid inflated rates, would an additional rate item be preferred for Floats / Plant etc ?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council advises that no Council plant or equipment will be available for loading mulch at stockpile locations.

Tenderers should allow for all labour, plant, equipment, transport and associated costs required to load, collect and deliver mulch within the nominated Schedule of Rates items.

No additional rate item is proposed.

publicQuestions.question: Can you advise what application is required to view the contents of the .GPGK files provided ?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council advises that files provided in GeoPackage (.GPKG) format can be viewed using GIS applications such as QGIS (free software) or ArcGIS.

Tenderers are responsible for obtaining suitable software to access and review the data.

publicQuestions.question:
The contract conditions refer to performance security equivalent to 5% of the contract sum.

Could Council confirm whether this security is mandatory for the successful contractor and what form of security is required?
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes. Performance Security is required from the successful Contractor.

The security must be equivalent to 5% of the Contract Sum and may be provided as a cheque, irrevocable bank guarantee, or insurance bond in a form approved by Council.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1 - A Granitic	Please confirm how the 43 granitic path/hardstand asset areas in Part A Attachment 2, totalling 32,262.14 m², are to be priced, given that no separate corresponding rows appear in Part A Table 1 of Schedule 2. Are these areas intended to be included within existing lump sum mowing items, or will a revised pricing schedule be issued to separately identify these assets?

Q2 - B Areas	Please confirm the quantities to be used for Crompton, Darby and Marconi Drive (2,865.04m² versus 6,008.99m²) and Thornton Court (9-13) Reserve (1,145.13m² versus 9,042.27m²), as the Part B tender prices and Addendum 2 assets differ.

Q3 - Batter	Please confirm whether Springvalley Reserve Batter is to receive 4 RMIs p.a. as specified in the Part A pricing schedule or 12 RMIs p.a. as shown in the Addendum 2 asset schedule.

Q4 - Allocated Admin It	Please confirm whether the dedicated contract and operational administration and technology/systems administrator positions may be allocated fractional FTE subject to a named, dedicated point of accountability and full delivery of Council's required reporting and system obligations.

Q5 - Outcome Frequency	Please confirm how additional maintenance attendance required to achieve specified Service Outcomes under clause 6.8.3 will be distinguished from Council-directed changes to Service Frequencies treated as variations under clause 6.8.4, particularly where the prescribed 12 or 4 RMIs per annum are insufficient to maintain the required standards.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Council confirms that the granitic path and hardstand asset areas identified in Part A Attachment 2, form part of the service scope.

Please see updated Tender Prices Table.

Note: Table 1 – Part A Lump Sum Tab now includes Granitic path and Hardstands Assets. To receive four (4) \interventions per annum as per the specification.

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - UPDATED Section B - Attachment 1 - Schedule 2 - Tender Prices - ADDENDUM 3

Please see updated Assets Table. Note Part A – Granitic Areas Tab has now been updated to the correct frequency of four (4) interventions per annum.

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - UPDATED Section D - Attachment 2 - Part A & B - Assets Table - ADDENDUM 4

2.	Council confirms the following corrections apply:

-	Crompton, Darby and Marconi Drive: the correct area is 6,008.99 m².

-	Thornton Court Reserve (9-13): the correct area is 1,142.12 m².

The Tender Price Table and Assets Table have been reviewed and updated with the correct data.

3.	Council confirms that 4 RMIs per annum is the service level required for the Springvalley Reserve Batter.

4.	Tenderers are to provide an overall organisational chart and chart depicting personnel responsible for the delivery of the services.

Tenderers are to provide a list of all in house staff that will be allocated to the carry out the works for this Contract.

This list should include all Key Personnel intended to be engaged in the management and delivery of the works as per the specification including percentage of time key personnel are solely dedicated to service this contract.

5.	6.8.3 Service Frequencies – Contractors are required to achieve applicable service outcomes during interventions.

When service outcomes are not met, the Contractor may be issued with a corrective action from Council, directing them to make a return visit and ensure service outcomes are met.

Changes to specified frequency will be issued as a variation in accordance with 6.8.4 of the Specification.

This is in an instance where Council has directed additional interventions beyond the specified service program.

These additional interventions will be treated as a Variation in accordance with the Specification.

publicQuestions.question:
Conflicting information:

1. Schedule 1 Tender Form states "The tendered amounts include GST and are not subject to cost adjustment." This form will be signed by the tenderer.

2. Section B Attachment 1 Schedule 2 Tender Prices Addendum 1 clearly shows all pricing in this spreadsheet to be exclusive of GST and states "The Pricing shall be exclusive of GST..."

Please confirm if all pricing is GST inclusive or exclusive. If exclusive, are we allowed to modify Schedule 1 Tender Form to show GST exclusive?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer: Schedule 1 is inclusive of GST, as stated, while Schedule 2 is exclusive of GST. Please populate the schedules accordingly, either inclusive or exclusive of GST as indicated.

publicQuestions.question:
GCC cl 4.5; Section B Schedule 2; Schedule 1 Tender Form; Spec cl 18.3

Please confirm by Addendum that the Schedule of Prices (Annual Lump Sum Prices and Schedule of Rates) will be adjusted on each anniversary of the Commencement Date throughout the Initial Contract Term and any extension, applying the formula in GCC cl 4.5 / Spec cl 18.3.3, and that GCC cl 4.5 and the Schedule 1 Tender Form will be amended accordingly.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that both the Annual Lump Sum and Schedule of Rates will be adjusted annually in accordance with CPI on each anniversary of the Commencement Date of the Contract.

This adjustment will apply throughout the initial three (3) year Contract Term and any exercised extension term, in accordance with the price adjustment formula specified in Section D – Specification.

To provide clarity and ensure consistency across the Contract documents, amendments have been made to the following documents:

1.	2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - Section C - General Conditions of Contract Services - Long Form - ADDENDUM 5; and

2.	2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - Section D - Specification - ADDENDUM 6.

publicQuestions.question:
GST Treatment – Schedule 1 Tender Form and Schedule 2 Tender Prices

We refer to Council's clarification issued on 5 November 2026 regarding the GST treatment of Schedule 1 and Schedule 2. We seek further clarification as the response does not appear to resolve the inconsistency between the two documents.

Schedule 1 – Tender Form does not contain any fields for entering GST-inclusive pricing. Instead, it refers directly to the Lump Sum Price and Schedule of Rates submitted separately under Schedule 2 Tender Prices.

However, Schedule 1 states that “The tendered amounts include GST”, whereas Schedule 2 – Tender Prices (Addendum 1) expressly requires all prices to exclude GST.

As the Tender Form must be signed, please confirm whether Council will amend Schedule 1 to state that tendered amounts exclude GST, consistent with Schedule 2, or alternatively confirm how tenderers should address this inconsistency without altering the prescribed Tender Form.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council has updated Section B Tender Schedules - Schedule 1 - Tender Form and Schedule 2 – Schedule of Lump Sum .

Updates now clarify that tendered amounts are exclusive of GST.

Please refer to updated document - 2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - Section A, B & C - Tender Conditions, Tender Services & General Conditions - ADDENDUM 7

Hello,

publicQuestions.question:
Part A Pricing Schedule: Unit of Measure

In the updated Schedule 2 Tender Prices workbook, the rate-basis/unit cells for Part A appear to identify the unit as m³. However, the corresponding asset areas are expressed in m².

Could Council please confirm whether the Part A pricing unit shown as m³ should read m², and whether tenderers should complete the applicable rates on an m² basis?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the unit of measure for Part A is m² (square metres).

The reference to m³ in the updated Schedule 2 Tender Prices was an administrative error and has now been corrected.

Please refer to: 2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - Section B - Attachment 1 - Schedule 2 - Tender Prices - ADDENDUM 8

publicQuestions.question:
Part B: Granitic Path / Hardstand Assets

The updated asset information for Part B appears to include a number of assets described as granitic paths or similar path areas, including Dandenong Bike Trail granitic path. Path and hardstand maintenance also appears within the Part A service scope.

Could Council please confirm whether all granitic/path-labelled assets currently listed under Part B are intended to remain within the Part B Horticulture Maintenance scope and are to be priced accordingly by Part B tenderers?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the granitic path and hardstand assets currently listed under Part B will remain within the Part B Horticulture Maintenance scope and are to be priced accordingly by Part B tenderers.

These assets are generally associated with landscaped and horticultural areas maintained under Part B. E.g. Granitic Tree Plots.

In many cases there are no adjoining or nearby grass areas to maintain. Accordingly, these assets will remain within the Part B scope.

publicQuestions.question:
CPI / Price Adjustment

The tender documents appear to contain differing provisions regarding the timing and application of price adjustments/indexation during the contract term.

Could Council please confirm the applicable price-adjustment mechanism for the contract, including the nominated CPI or other index, reference period, first adjustment date, frequency of adjustment, and whether adjustment applies during the initial contract term and any extension periods?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the price adjustment mechanism is annual CPI indexation

The Annual Lump Sum and Schedule of Rates will be adjusted on each anniversary of the Commencement Date using the CPI (All Groups Melbourne) published by the ABS, in accordance with the formula specified in the Contract.

The first adjustment will occur on 10 May following the first year of the Contract and will apply annually thereafter.

The CPI value used will be the most recent CPI (All Groups Melbourne) published by the ABS at the time of the adjustment.

Price adjustments will apply throughout the initial three (3) year Contract Term and any exercised extension term.

publicQuestions.question:
Performance Security: Contract Sum

Council has confirmed that the successful contractor is required to provide Performance Security equivalent to 5% of the Contract Sum.

Given that the tender pricing comprises lump-sum service pricing together with Schedule of Rates and potentially variable quantities:

Could Council please confirm how the “Contract Sum” will be calculated for the purpose of determining the 5% Performance Security, including whether Schedule of Rates or estimated/variable service quantities will form part of the calculation?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that, for the purpose of calculating the Performance Security, the Contract Sum will be based on the successful Tenderer's Annual Lump Sum Price.

Schedule of Rates items and any variable quantity works will not form part of the Performance Security calculation.

publicQuestions.question:
With reference to Specification released in Addendum #6, we note that this extends CPI adjustment under clause 18.3 to the Annual Lump Sum, but Schedule 1 (Tender Form) states that tendered amounts “are not subject to cost adjustment”. Please confirm that clause 18.3 prevails and that the Annual Lump Sum and Schedule of Rates are both adjusted on each anniversary of the Commencement Date ?.

Please also confirm clause 17.1.2 (should refer to clause 14, not 16) and for reference clause 6.3.1 has a broken cross-reference.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that clause 18.3 of the Specification and clause 4.5 of the General Conditions of Contract apply to both the Annual Lump Sum and the Schedule of Rates.

Accordingly, both the Annual Lump Sum and Schedule of Rates will be adjusted on each anniversary of the Commencement Date in accordance with the nominated CPI adjustment formula for the duration of the Initial Contract Term and any exercised extension period.

The statement in Schedule 1 (Tender Form) that tendered amounts are "not subject to cost adjustment" refers to the tendered prices submitted at tender close and does not override the contract price adjustment provisions that apply annually after contract commencement.

Council also confirms that clause 17.1.2 should refer to clause 14 (Reporting and Meeting Requirements) rather than clause 16.

In addition, Council acknowledges the broken cross-reference in clause 6.3.1.

Intended clause reference is 5.3.2 in place of the wording ‘Error! Reference source not found’

publicQuestions.question:
Q6-SOR A & B

As the locations and site-specific requirements for future SOR works have not been identified, dedicated traffic management costs cannot be reliably determined at tender stage. Please confirm whether SOR rates may include routine worksite signage and pedestrian controls, with dedicated traffic management crews, lane closures and associated plans and permits separately quoted for Council’s approval against each relevant work order.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that any traffic management requirements associated with a particular New Works Order or Schedule of Rates work are to be included in the pricing submitted for that work.

The Specification provides several mechanisms under which New Works Work Orders may be delivered.

Please refer to Clause 5.3.3.2 of the Specification. New Works Orders and variations may be priced:

•	in accordance with, or pro rata to, an equivalent item in the relevant Annual Lump Sum Prices;

•	under the applicable item(s) detailed in the Schedule of Rates;

•	under Quotation Services; or

•	under Daywork Services,

The pricing mechanism will be determined by the Contract Manager following consultation with the awarded Contractor.

publicQuestions.question:
With reference to Clarification response received 10/11/2026 :

The buyer repliedTuesday 10 November 2026 02:44 PMwith:

Council confirms that the granitic path and hardstand assets currently listed under Part B will remain within the Part B Horticulture Maintenance scope and are to be priced accordingly by Part B tenderers.

These assets are generally associated with landscaped and horticultural areas maintained under Part B. E.g. Granitic Tree Plots.

In many cases there are no adjoining or nearby grass areas to maintain. Accordingly, these assets will remain within the Part B scope.

On Review of Assets table released with Addendum 4 and Updated Scope document (Addendum 6), Granitic paths are listed as Part A items.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the majority of granitic path and hardstand assets form part of the Part A scope of works.

However, a small number of granitic path and hardstand assets have been included within Part B.

The rationale for their inclusion in Part B is outlined in Council's previous tender clarification response.

Tenderers are advised that granitic path and hardstand assets listed within Part B are to be priced and maintained in accordance with the Service Specification requirements for Path and Hardstand Maintenance 7.1.2.

publicQuestions.question:
We refer to the updated Annexure in Addendum 7 and clauses 2.2.2 and 2.2.3 of the General Conditions issued under Addendum 5.

The updated Annexure specifies a maximum two-year extension under clause 2.2.2.2 and 90 days’ notice under both extension clauses. However, it does not specify the minimum extension period referenced in clause 2.2.2.1 or the extension duration referenced in clause 2.2.3.

Could Council please clarify how these provisions are intended to operate for the single optional extension of up to two years, and update the Annexure to align with the applicable clauses?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that the Contract includes a single optional extension period of two (2) years.

For the purposes of clauses 2.2.2 and 2.2.3 of the General Conditions, the minimum and maximum extension period is two (2) years.

If Council elects to exercise the option, it will do so for a period of two (2) years by providing not less than ninety (90) days' notice to the Contractor.

publicQuestions.question:
Can you please clarify in spreadsheet - Section B - Attachment 1 - Schedule 2 - Tender Prices - Addendum 8

Table 1 - Part A - Lump Sum and Table 3 - Part B - Lump sum - the lump sum calculation is incorrect based on the rate in column N, should column N be a service rate? instead of an annual rate.
publicQuestions.answer:
The Tender Price CSV allows for the submission of a rate per square metre ($/m2).

This rate is to be entered in Column N of Table 1 (Part A) and Column K of Table 3 (Part B).

The nominated rate will be multiplied by the applicable area (m²) quantity to calculate the intervention rate and annual cost for each site.

As previously advised, tenderers may alternatively submit pricing on a site-by-site basis if they do not wish to apply a uniform $/m² rate across all sites, provided pricing is submitted on a per intervention basis for each site and an annual cost for each site is also populated.

title: Cold Chain Monitoring - Bayside
description: The procurement is for the implementation of a cloud-based cold chain monitoring system across Bayside Health Service (BHS) to monitor the temperature of medication, vaccine, and pathology storage refrigerators. The solution will replace three separate legacy monitoring systems currently in use: ACR Trendreader (AXIOM), Quirks LogTags, and BMS. The new system will provide continuous 24/7 temperature monitoring, real-time alerts, centralised data access, audit trails, reporting, and regulatory compliance capabilities. The need arises from ageing and unsupported infrastructure, fragmented monitoring processes, incompatibility with newer refrigeration equipment, and increasing clinical and operational risks associated with temperature-sensitive products.
buyer: Metro South Hospital and Health Service

•	Data storage and reporting capability with retention of historical data for at least two years.

•	Integration with existing Metro South Health infrastructure, including BMS and alert escalation pathways.

•	Remote monitoring capability through QH-certified devices and VPN access.

•	Installation, calibration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and ongoing support services.

•	Integration with existing BMS systems and alert escalation pathways.

•	Access through Queensland Health-certified devices.

•	VPN-enabled remote monitoring and administration capabilities.

title: Gold Standard Early Intervention – Proven Initiatives Round 3
description:
The Department of Youth Justice and Victim Support (the Department) is seeking proposals to deliver the Gold Standard Early Intervention – Proven Initiatives program. This program is designed to prevent and reduce youth offending and improve life outcomes for youth at-risk of offending.

The target cohort for this program is youth aged 8 to 17 years who are:

• displaying early signs of criminal and/or anti-social behaviours (e.g. drug and alcohol misuse, anger management issues); and

• disengaged from school or at high risk of exclusion; or

• at risk of coming into contact with police and/or court systems; or

• siblings of youth on youth justice orders.

This group is at risk of escalating into the statutory youth justice system without timely and effective intervention.

The program aims to:

• Provide timely and effective interventions for youth at risk of entering the statutory youth justice system.

• Strengthen family and community supports to build protective factors.

• Improve engagement with education, training, or employment.

• Enhance wellbeing and resilience.

Suppliers are expected to deliver structured, evidence-based services that align with these goals and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

title: ITT263 - Memorialisation Products, Materials and Services
description:
Sunshine Coast Council’s cemetery services offer a range of memorial products available for purchase to customers as a personalised tribute to a loved one.

Tenders are invited for the provision of memorial products, materials and services across the following separable portions:

A – Supply of Memorial Plaques and above ground ashes interment options - Supply of metal alloy plaque products including but not limited to bronze, brass and aluminium.

B – Supply and Install of Memorial Monuments - Supply and install granite, porcelain and similar memorial products.

C – Supply of Pre-fabricated Memorial Concrete Products - Supply and install precast concrete memorial products.

D - Supply of Laser Engraver Materials - Supply of materials suitable for laser engraving of memorial products.

E - Monument Maintenance - Provision of maintenance and repair for existing memorial monuments, including cleaning, restoration and minor repairs.

Respondents may tender for one, multiple or all Separable Portions. Council reserves the right to award to one (1) or more Respondents for one or more portions at its sole discretion. Council does not provide a guarantee of volume of supply during the term of this Contract.

This is a schedule of rates contract for a term of three (3) years, with the option of one (1) further term of up to 24 months, at Council’s sole discretion.

An online Information Session will be held covering all Separable Portions.

publicQuestions.question:
We are preparing a submission for ITT263 – Memorialisation Products, Materials and Services, limited to Separable Portions A and D, and would appreciate clarification on the following additional matters. These questions do not repeat earlier enquiries lodged on 15 and 16 November 2026.

1. Clarification cut-off

The VendorPanel request states that the cut-off for supplier queries is Thursday, 3 December 2026 at 12:00 PM Australian Eastern Standard Time. Invitation to Tender, Schedule 1 Item 8, states that requests for clarification or further information “will not be accepted on or after the date that is 3 business days prior to the Closing Date.” Three business days prior to the Closing Date of Tuesday, 8 December 2026 is Thursday, 3 December 2026, which can be read as meaning that questions are not accepted on that date.

Could Council please confirm the last date and time at which clarification questions will be accepted?

- Document and clause: VendorPanel Request Summary, “Cut-off date for supplier queries”; Invitation to Tender, Schedule 1 Item 8 (and Process Terms cl 3.10, as cited in that Item).

- Reason: The two documents can be read as setting different last times, and the remaining questions below need a clear deadline.

2. Information session

Page 1 of the Invitation to Tender, and the VendorPanel Request Summary, state that an online Information Session will be held covering all Separable Portions. Invitation to Tender, Schedule 2, states “Not applicable” and no date or joining details are given.

Could Council please confirm whether an information session will be held and, if so, the date, time and how respondents may attend?

- Document and clause: Invitation to Tender, page 1 (Contract Overview) and Schedule 2; VendorPanel Request Summary, “What’s required.”

- Reason: The pack contradicts itself, and respondents should not miss a session if one is in fact being held.

3. Online design platform and proofing (clause 5)

Service Specification clauses 5.1 to 5.4 require the Contractor to provide methods and technologies that reduce proofing time, and a secure, user-friendly online self-service design platform that enables Council customers to design memorial plaques, review proofs and request amendments, with a version history and with Council’s final approval required before manufacture.

Could Council please confirm:

- whether clauses 5.2 to 5.4 apply to a respondent tendering only for Separable Portions A and D on a supply-only basis;

- whether a platform provided by an authorised manufacturer or wholesaler, used under the principal contractor’s contract and giving Council final approval before manufacture, would satisfy clauses 5.2 to 5.4; and

- whether a respondent supplying only laser-engraver materials under Portion D (with Council undertaking engraving in-house) is still required to provide a customer-facing plaque design platform?

- Document and clause: Service Specification (Schedule 5, Attachment 1), clauses 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 (including 5.3(a)–(d)) and 5.4, page 3 of 14; Tender Response Form, Part 3.2, value-added services and systems.

- Reason: The platform is written as mandatory for “the Contractor,” but it sits in the general specification rather than in the Portion A or D scope, and it is a substantial system obligation for a supply-only model.

4. Proof and amendment turnaround after the first proof

Clause 3.3 requires custom proofs and/or quotations within five (5) business days of a request. Clauses 5.2 and 5.3 contemplate multiple rounds of review and amendment, but no timeframe is stated for subsequent proofs after the first.

Could Council please confirm the required turnaround, in business days, for revised proofs and for responding to customer or Council amendment requests after the first proof has been issued?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.3, 5.2 and 5.3, pages 2–3 of 14.

- Reason: The first-proof time is clear; later rounds, which the platform must support, have no stated service level.

5. Samples and technical data for Portions A and D

The Service Specification requires physical colour swatches and certificates of origin at commencement for Portion B (clause 8.6), and samples and product information at commencement for Portion E (clauses 11.6 and 11.7). No equivalent sample, swatch or technical-data requirement is stated for Portions A or D, and no pre-award samples are requested in the Tender Response Form.

Could Council please confirm whether respondents for Portions A and D must provide, either with the tender or at commencement of the contract, product samples, colour swatches, coating specifications, or manufacturer’s technical data and warranty documentation and, if so, for which items?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 7.3, 8.6, 10.1–10.2, 11.6–11.7; Tender Response Form, Parts 1–4 (no sample schedule).

- Reason: Sample obligations are spelled out for B and E only, leaving A and D unclear, including where an alternative coating is proposed under clause 7.3.

6. Portion D delivery location

Portion A has nominated delivery addresses for plaques and for above-ground ashes products (clauses 7.14 and 7.15). Portion D has a four-week delivery time (clause 10.3) but no portion-specific delivery address. General clauses 3.6 to 3.9 require pre-arranged delivery, possibly to alternate locations within the Sunshine Coast local government area, at the contractor’s cost.

Could Council please confirm the default delivery address, or addresses, for Portion D laser-engraver materials, and whether the addresses in clauses 7.14 and 7.15 also apply to Portion D unless otherwise directed?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.6–3.9, 7.14, 7.15 and 10.3, pages 2, 5 and 9 of 14; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-D ~ Laser Engraver Materials.”

- Reason: Freight must be included in the unit rates, but the destination for Portion D is not stated.

7. Portion D material specification (thickness, alloy, default colour, edges and fixings)

Clauses 10.1 and 10.2 require architectural-grade aluminium with an exterior-grade powder coating or an external-quality anodised finish, suitable for long-term outdoor use in South-East Queensland. The Schedule of Rates does not state sheet thickness, alloy grade or temper, edge finish, or hole size and position. Only two line items specify a colour (50 × 30 Reserve tag (red) and 50 × 30 Vacant (green)). Other sizes have no default colour. Fixings are a separately priced extra.

Could Council please specify, for each SP-D line item where it is known:

- the required or typical sheet thickness;

- the required alloy grade and temper, if any, beyond “architectural-grade aluminium”;

- the default colour and finish for items that do not have a colour in the line description;

- any required edge finish; and

- standard hole sizes, positions and clip types, where fixings are ordered?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 2.4, 10.1 and 10.2, pages 2 and 9 of 14; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-D ~ Laser Engraver Materials,” heading and rows for 380 × 280, 254 × 152, 160 × 140, 200 × 150, 15 × 50, 160 × 70, 100 × 50, 50 × 30 Reserve tag (red), 50 × 30 Vacant (green), additional cost for a non-standard colour, and additional cost for fixings.

- Reason: These physical details are needed to obtain comparable wholesale prices. This question does not ask whether red or green, or anodised or powder-coated finishes, are mandatory, which was raised on 16 November 2026.

8. Warranty period for Portion D materials

Clause 6.6 warrants all memorial products against manufacturing defects, from delivery, for 20 years for plaques, 50 years for granite memorial installations, and otherwise the manufacturer’s standard warranty but not less than twelve (12) months. Clause 10.1 refers to Portion D items as “laser-engraved aluminium plaques.”

Could Council please confirm which warranty period in clause 6.6 applies to Portion D laser-engraver materials, including blanks, tags, row markers and name markers: the 20-year plaque warranty, or the manufacturer’s standard warranty of not less than 12 months?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 6.6 and 10.1, pages 4 and 9 of 14.

- Reason: The 20-year and 12-month periods differ substantially, and clause 10.1’s use of “plaques” makes it unclear which period applies to blanks and tags.

9. Lead time for above-ground ashes interment products, and for custom-sized plaques

Clause 7.12 requires alloy plaques to be delivered within six (6) weeks of the order. Clause 3.2, which deals with inability to meet prescribed lead times, cites clauses 7.12, 8.11, 8.12 and 10.3 only. There is no stated lead time for above-ground ashes interment products (sleepers and cylinders) under clauses 7.15 and 7.16 or the corresponding Schedule of Rates items. Clause 7.6 also requires custom-sized plaques, without a separate lead time.

Could Council please confirm:

- the required delivery period for sleeper and cylinder products under Portion A; and

- whether custom-sized plaques under clause 7.6 must also be delivered within the six-week period in clause 7.12, or whether a different period applies?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.2, 7.6, 7.12, 7.15 and 7.16, pages 2, 4 and 5 of 14; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques,” rows “Sleeper/ Cylinder (Small)” to “(XLarge).”

- Reason: Cancellation rights in clause 3.2 turn on “prescribed lead times,” but two product groups in Portion A have no clear prescribed time.

10. Sleeper and cylinder sizes

The Schedule of Rates prices sleeper/cylinder products as Small, Medium, Large and XLarge. Clause 7.16 sets material standards (durable materials, consistent cast bronze, Grade 316 marine-grade stainless steel hardware, and resistance to corrosion and galvanic reaction) but does not give dimensions, capacities or configuration. Schedule 5, Attachment 2 (Standard Drawings) contains typical details for granite and concrete monuments only, and does not include sleepers or cylinders.

Could Council please provide the required dimensions, capacity, configuration and any drawings or reference products for the Small, Medium, Large and XLarge sleeper/cylinder items?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clause 7.16, page 5 of 14; Schedule of Rates, SP-A, “Above Ground Ashes interment options”; Schedule 5, Attachment 2 (no corresponding drawing).

- Reason: These four lines cannot be priced, or sourced from a manufacturer, without sizes or a drawing.

11. Bookstyle plaque pricing structure

The Schedule of Rates includes, as separate lines, “380 × 280 Bookstyle Bronze Plaque,” “380 × 280 Bookstyle Aluminium Plaque,” “380 × 280 Bookstyle Bronze Plaque – With first plaque,” and “Second plate for Bronze bookstyle plaque.” A refurbishment line is described as “Bookstyle plaque with first leaf (380 × 280).”

Could Council please confirm what is included in each of these rates — in particular, whether the “Bookstyle” rate is for the base or cover only, whether “With first plaque” includes the bookstyle unit plus the first inscription plate, and whether the “Second plate” is only the additional detachable plate?

- Document and clause: Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques,” burial plaque and refurbishment rows; Service Specification, clauses 7.8 and 7.9.

- Reason: The three new-supply bookstyle lines can be read in more than one way, and a misreading would produce inconsistent prices.

12. Undefined additional options on SP-A

Several priced options are not defined in the Service Specification or the Standard Drawings:

- “165 × 133 Bronze plaque with soldier hump” — no drawing or profile is provided;

- “120 × 160 Leaf shaped plaque” — no outline or thickness is provided;

- “Perpetual emblem for a bronze plaque”;

- “Plaque cleaner”;

- “Fast-tracked order cost (per order)” — no delivery period is stated that this extra rate must achieve;

- “Smart memorial added to an existing plaque/memorial order” and “Stand-alone smart memorial” (including what hardware, hosting, term, data and artwork are included in the rate); and

- “Tier 1 – simple,” “Tier 2 – intermediate” and “Tier 3 – complex” custom artwork re-draw — no criteria or examples distinguish the tiers.

Could Council please provide a short definition, specification or example for each of the items listed above and, for a fast-tracked order, the required delivery period from receipt of the order?

- Document and clause: Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques,” the rows named above (including the sheet spellings “Smart mewmorial” and “red-draw”); Service Specification, clauses 7 and 5.5; Schedule 5, Attachment 2 (no metal-plaque or smart-memorial drawings).

- Reason: These are priced lines on a sheet that, on its face, requires a unit rate for each item, but they cannot be quoted from the current specification.

13. Ceramic photo shapes and chrome plate specification

Clause 7.10 requires ceramic photos in oval, square and rectangular shapes, full bleed, surface-mounted and frameless. The Schedule of Rates prices photos only by size and by black-and-white or colour. Clause 7.9 states included inscription lines for ashes and burial plaques, but not for detachable plates. Chrome detachable plates have no alloy or finish standard, unlike bronze (C83600, AS 1565:2023) and aluminium (DA601, AS 1874:2000).

Could Council please confirm:

- whether the listed ceramic photo rates apply to all three shapes at the stated size, or whether shape is priced differently;

- how many inscription lines, if any, are included in the detachable plate rates; and

- the required material and finish standard for the 100 × 75 chrome plate?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 7.1, 7.2, 7.9 and 7.10, pages 4–5 of 14; Schedule of Rates, SP-A, detachable plates and photo options.

- Reason: Shape, included lettering and the chrome standard all affect cost and are not aligned between the specification and the price sheet.

14. Brass in the Invitation to Tender versus bronze in the specification

The Invitation to Tender overview, and the VendorPanel Request Summary, describe Portion A as including “bronze, brass and aluminium.” Service Specification clause 2.1 refers to “bronze, chrome and aluminium.” Clauses 7.1 and 7.2, and the SP-A price sheet, specify bronze and aluminium (and chrome plates) only. There is no brass line item and no brass alloy standard.

Could Council please confirm whether brass plaques are required, or whether “brass” in the overview should be read as bronze, consistent with clauses 7.1 and 7.2 and the Schedule of Rates?

- Document and clause: Invitation to Tender, page 1, Separable Portion A; VendorPanel Request Summary, “What’s required”; Service Specification, clauses 2.1, 7.1 and 7.2; Schedule of Rates, worksheet “SP-A ~ Supply Memorial Plaques.”

- Reason: An unexplained brass requirement would change the product range and pricing; it looks like an inconsistency between the overview and the detailed specification.

15. Packaging of Portion D materials

Clause 3.7 requires packaging that facilitates safe and convenient unloading by Council’s forklift if required, and states that items should be palletised and/or placed on Council work benches on delivery. Many Portion D items are small tags and markers (including 15 × 50 mm and 50 × 30 mm).

Could Council please confirm the expected packaging, palletisation and marking for Portion D materials, including small tags, and whether clause 3.7 applies in full to those items?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 3.7, 3.8 and 10, pages 2 and 9 of 14; Schedule of Rates, SP-D line items.

- Reason: The general packaging rule is written for larger memorial products and needs to be confirmed for small engraved-blank deliveries.

16. Supply-only application of experience, reporting and systems obligations

Several general contractor obligations are written as applying to “the Contractor” or to “all personnel undertaking the works,” without being limited to on-site portions:

- Service Specification clause 12.4, which requires personnel to have a minimum of five (5) years’ relevant industry experience;

- Service Specification clause 16, which requires a training matrix, completion schedule and defects and hazards reporting;

- Service Specification clause 17, which provides that contractors may be required to use Council’s Confirm asset management system; and

- General Terms and Conditions clause 7.1(d)(v) and clause 7.5, which require a statutory declaration in the form of Schedule 3, and a subcontractor payment register, with every payment claim.

Could Council please confirm which of these obligations apply to a respondent engaged only to supply and deliver products under Portions A and D, with no installation or cemetery-site work?

- Document and clause: Service Specification, clauses 12.4, 16.1–16.2 and 17.1, pages 11 and 14 of 14; General Terms and Conditions, clauses 7.1(d)(v) and 7.5, and Schedule 3.

- Reason: These are operational and compliance obligations that may or may not be intended for a supply-only contractor. This question does not ask again about insurance types or the Part 2.1 safety documentation, which were raised on 15 November 2026.

Thank you for your assistance.

title: Expression of Interest - Southern Water Treatment Plant Project
description:
Toowoomba Regional Council (Council) is one of Queensland’s largest regional Councils, serving approximately 184,000 people across a geographical area of 12,973 square kilometres. Located in South East Queensland, approximately 125 kilometres west of Brisbane, the Region encompasses the city of Toowoomba, the regional centres of Oakey, Pittsworth, Millmerran, Highfields, Crows Nest, Clifton, Greenmount and Yarraman, and numerous smaller townships.

Council is responsible for delivering and maintaining essential community infrastructure and services, including water, wastewater, waste, drainage, roads, bridges, footpaths, utilities and recreational facilities. Through its Water and Waste Services Group, Council manages the Region’s water treatment, storage and distribution assets, including the existing Mount Kynoch Water Treatment Plant (WTP).

Water security is fundamental to supporting the continued growth and prosperity of the Toowoomba Region. The construction of the Queensland Government’s Toowoomba

to Warwick Pipeline (T2WP) has created an opportunity for the Toowoomba region to benefit in exchange for the use of Council’s raw water infrastructure. Studies on the impact of the T2WP have identified an opportunity to construct a new Southern Water Treatment Plant (SWTP), now an initiative within the Toowoomba Regional Council Water Vision 2021–2071.

It involves a new plant of at least 25 ML/d capacity that will provide a reliable water source for the region to ensure long-term water security and support regional growth. The

new SWTP will facilitate population growth in the southern and western regions of Toowoomba by providing a new water source and alleviating the demands currently placed

on the Mt Kynoch WTP. Raw water for the new WTP is proposed to be taken from an offtake from the T2WP. Additional distribution assets to service the new WTP

include a 15 ML reservoir in the Mt Peel Bushland Reserve, a pump station, 15 km of trunk and distribution pipelines and other pipeline structures.

The Project will enhance the Region’s long-term water security, improve network capacity and resilience, and provide reliable water services to support existing communities and future population growth, particularly across the southern and western areas of Toowoomba.

Council seeks EOI Responses from suitably qualified and experienced Contractors with capability and capacity to deliver the scope of works detailed within this document.

The purpose of this Request for EOI is to:

- advise the market of the project and provide an overview of the likely scope of works

- describe the procurement process including indicative timeline for delivery of the Project

- provide an overview of the proposed commercial and legal framework

- enable Council to shortlist down to potentially two (2) suitably qualified Proponents to proceed to the Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) Phase of the evaluation process.

publicQuestions.question: Schedule W1.1 asks for recent and relevant experience in delivering Water Treatment Plant (WTP) and pipeline infrastructure completed in Australia. Is it acceptable to include projects that are substantially complete, e.g. 70% complete?
publicQuestions.answer: Respondents may, at their discretion, select the project examples they consider best demonstrate the experience requirements described in the EOI documents. Where a nominated project is not fully complete, the Respondent must clearly identify its current status and demonstrate how the experience gained to date is relevant to the requirements of Schedule W1.1. Council will assess the examples based on the information provided.

publicQuestions.question: Schedule W1.1 asks for recent and relevant experience in delivering Water Treatment Plant (WTP) and pipeline infrastructure completed in Australia. Given the limited number of comparable size and value WTP projects in Australia in the last 5yrs, it acceptable to include Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP) projects as well? If so, would these be considered equally relevant from a scoring perspective given the similarities in management of delivery challenges, issues and risks; complex multidisciplined works; and scalability and expansion?
publicQuestions.answer:
Respondents may include WWTP projects where they consider the experience relevant to the requirements of Schedule W1.1. While WWTP projects may involve similar construction activities and delivery challenges, the process design and technical requirements of a WTP are distinct.

Schedule W1.1 allows Respondents to nominate relevant project examples completed within the past 10 years. Each example will be assessed on its demonstrated relevance to the requirements of W1.1 and the applicable Returnable Schedules in Volume 2.

WWTP experience will not automatically be considered equally relevant to comparable WTP experience. Respondents should clearly explain how each nominated project demonstrates the required WTP, pipeline, multidisciplinary delivery, scalability and risk-management capabilities.

publicQuestions.question:
Attachment B - Key Terms Sheet - Schedule 1 - Item 2 outlines Council's preferred position on the Reimbursable Costs. We note several items which are directly project related costs are shown that they are not reimbursable and should be included in the Corporate Overhead and Profit (COP).

These are not in line with current market standards and include project specific costs such as: preparation of monthly progress claims by the project team; project based HR and/or IR advisors; coffee machines; mobile phone costs for project staff; project specific IT support & administration; project office IT hardware purchase; project specific software/licences.

This position may be consistent for most Respondents and prior to developing the D&C pricing during the ECI phase it is challenging to assess/value these and calculate the required adjustment to the nominated COP.

As such, would Council consider adjusting these now or do Respondents need to include them as departures under Schedule W5.2 and a caveat in Schedule W6.1 that the nominated maximum COP would increase if the departures are not accepted during the ECI phase as the ITC Deed is developed?
publicQuestions.answer:
The Reimbursable Cost Schedule reflects Council’s current preferred position and is intended to promote efficient administration and auditing of lower-value or less material project costs, based on Council’s experience with similar contracts.

Respondents should nominate a COP that is consistent with this position. Where a Respondent proposes an alternative treatment, it should clearly identify the departure in Schedule W5.2 and outline any associated assumptions or potential impact on the nominated COP in Schedule W6.1.

As part of the evaluation, Council will consider the extent to which each Respondent aligns with the position set out in the EOI documents, together with any commercial risk or additional administrative and auditing burden created by proposed departures. The Reimbursable Cost Schedule and associated commercial arrangements will be further developed during the ECI phase.

publicQuestions.question:

title: Richmond Village Green and Playground Upgrade - Design & Documentation Consultancy
description:
Clarence City Council (CCC) invites Quotations from suitably qualified Respondents to undertake a consultancy for the preparation of an Issue for Tender Package, including concept design, detailed design, drawings, details, schedules, specifications and supporting documentation as required under the Contract for the upgrade of the Richmond Village Green and playground at 54-56 Bridge Street, Richmond, Tasmania 7025

The Richmond Village Green and Playground Upgrade is the first project proposed for delivery under the Richmond Village Master Plan 2026, a strategic framework adopted by the CCC in June 2026 to guide planning, investment and development within Richmond over the next 20 years.

The Master Plan, developed and informed by engagement with residents, business and key stakeholders, establishes a vision for enhancing Richmond’s public spaces while protecting the village’s nationally significant heritage values and character. Key priorities include improvements to accessibility, pedestrian safety, visitor management and the quality of public open spaces.

As the first priority project identified within the Master Plan, this project is intended to contribute to these objectives by enhancing a key community gathering space for residents and visitors. Funding has been secured for the design phase of the project, including technical investigations and community engagement to inform the development of a preferred design.

The Master Plan establishes the preferred concept for the project. The role of the Consultant is to validate, refine and further develop the Master Plan recommendations through concept design, community engagement, cost planning, detailed design and construction documentation, rather than prepare alternative precinct concepts.

The purpose of this consultancy is to prepare a complete and coordinated design and documentation package to support future implementation of the project. While funding has been secured for the design phase, construction funding may be subject to future funding availability. Respondents should therefore assume that the primary outcome of this consultancy is the preparation of a tender-ready package for future procurement.

PRE-QUOTATION SITE MEETING

For clarification of the Services, a pre-Quotation site meeting is scheduled for at 10am Tuesday 17 November 2026. This meeting will convene on Site at the Forth Street Carpark by the Richmond Village Green at 54 Bridge Street, Richmond, Tasmania.

Attendance at the site meeting is not mandatory; however, Respondents are strongly encouraged to attend to familiarise themselves with the Site and project requirements prior to submitting a Quotation.

Respondents intending to attend this meeting are requested to inform the contact person nominated on the front cover of this Quotation Invitation prior to the meeting.

CLOSE OF QUOTATIONS

3pm Tuesday 1 December 2026

LATE QUOTATIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

title: Support the design, development, testing, validation of the FarmTechConnect AgTech Adoption program
description:
The Department of Primary Industries (DPI) is seeking supplier/s to provide specialist professional services supporting DPI-led delivery of FarmTechConnect. The supplier may engage subcontractors with relevant specialist expertise and will remain responsible for coordinating and delivering all contracted services and outputs. The completed package must be tested with producers and extension personnel, refined through documented feedback, and handed over with editable resources and clear guidance. Practical training must equip DPI and partner extension providers to confidently deliver, maintain and adapt the program beyond the supplier’s engagement.

title: Sunrise Way Roofing Replacement
description:
Darling Downs Hospital and Health Service invites offers for the provision of construction works for the Sunrise Way Roofing Replacement located at 9-13 Tourist Road, Toowoomba, Queensland in accordance with the requirements of this Request for Tender.

The purpose of this Request for Tender is to obtain fixed lump sum pricing. A mandatory site inspection has been scheduled for Friday, 20 November 2026, see Request for Tender on instructions to nominate an organisational representative.

The project aims to preserve and protect the heritage building & the health service it houses by replacing the deteriorated roofing materials with new, heritage approved, products. As well as the remediation of water ingress defects, restoration of heritage masonry elements, upgrade of stormwater drainage infrastructure, and repair of associated internal building damage. All works are to be delivered in strict accordance with the Heritage Exemption Certificate, approved design documentation, relevant Australian Standards, and statutory requirements, ensuring the preservation of the building's heritage significance while improving its long-term structural integrity, weatherproofing performance, and operational resilience.

It should be noted that this is a live residential care facility & will be occupied by staff and residents for the duration of the project. Strict patient care and safety is the number one priority.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
This heritage listed place, Unara, is a heritage-listed detached Federation Bungalow, originally built for Sir Littleton Groom Circa 1906. The Northern and Southern wings were added in the 1950’s & 1960’s respectively. Along with various alterations & additions over the years. The building currently houses Drug & Alcohol residential rehabilitation.

The building is currently experiencing roof leaks, with some isolated interior damage caused. It has been determined that new roofing including flashings and stormwater reticulation remediation is required. Structural tie down and insulation will be improved while the sheeting is off and the chimneys will be repointed to retain their integrity.

The stormwater reticulation downstream of the downpipes is in a failed state. The above ground reticulation, suspended from the floor joists, appears to have backfalls and some charged lines. Reticulation enters the ground on the Western side of the Northern extension, via a retention pipe which is currently disconnected from the inground pipe, discharging all stormwater to surface in the undercroft. This is presumably because the inground system is blocked. The inground stormwater reticulation direction, route & discharge point is unknown.

RFI01 - EOT Request

Hi Julianne,

We respectfully request an Extension of Time (EOT) for the submission of our tender for the Sludge Dewatering Upgrade Project, extending the current submission deadline of 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

This extension is requested to allow sufficient time to obtain and assess vendor package pricing, receive outstanding subcontractor quotations, and develop a complete and accurate tender submission that adequately addresses the complexities and various elements of the project.

The current tender timeframe has presented several challenges, including:

•	Vendor package pricing and lead times: The specialised nature of the sludge dewatering equipment requires engagement with multiple vendors to obtain compliant technical and commercial offers. Allowing sufficient time for vendors to review the project requirements and develop their submissions is essential.

•	Subcontractor responses: A number of subcontractor quotations remain outstanding, with additional time required to obtain, review and clarify pricing to ensure all relevant scope elements are adequately covered.

•	Limited supplier participation: Several suppliers have declined to provide pricing due to the short turnaround time available. This has restricted the number of competitive quotations received and increased the time required to identify and engage alternative suppliers.

•	Project complexity and scope coordination: The project involves multiple interfacing elements, vendor packages and subcontracted works that require careful coordination to ensure the proposed solution is technically compliant and commercially complete.

•	Tender accuracy and completeness: Additional time is required to review vendor and subcontractor submissions, reconcile scope gaps and exclusions, confirm pricing assumptions, and undertake a detailed internal review of the estimate and overall tender submission.

The requested extension will provide the necessary opportunity to obtain more complete and reliable pricing, properly assess the associated risks and exclusions, and ensure our final submission represents an accurate and considered offer that meets the project requirements.

We believe the additional time will support a more robust and competitive tender submission, reducing the likelihood of pricing omissions, scope gaps or assumptions that may otherwise affect the delivery and cost certainty of the project.

We therefore respectfully request approval to extend the tender submission deadline by 15 calendar days, from 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

Hi Julianne,

We respectfully request an Extension of Time (EOT) for the submission of our tender for the Sludge Dewatering Upgrade Project, extending the current submission deadline of 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

This extension is requested to allow sufficient time to obtain and assess vendor package pricing, receive outstanding subcontractor quotations, and develop a complete and accurate tender submission that adequately addresses the complexities and various elements of the project.

The current tender timeframe has presented several challenges, including:

•	Vendor package pricing and lead times: The specialised nature of the sludge dewatering equipment requires engagement with multiple vendors to obtain compliant technical and commercial offers. Allowing sufficient time for vendors to review the project requirements and develop their submissions is essential.

•	Subcontractor responses: A number of subcontractor quotations remain outstanding, with additional time required to obtain, review and clarify pricing to ensure all relevant scope elements are adequately covered.

•	Limited supplier participation: Several suppliers have declined to provide pricing due to the short turnaround time available. This has restricted the number of competitive quotations received and increased the time required to identify and engage alternative suppliers.

•	Project complexity and scope coordination: The project involves multiple interfacing elements, vendor packages and subcontracted works that require careful coordination to ensure the proposed solution is technically compliant and commercially complete.

•	Tender accuracy and completeness: Additional time is required to review vendor and subcontractor submissions, reconcile scope gaps and exclusions, confirm pricing assumptions, and undertake a detailed internal review of the estimate and overall tender submission.

The requested extension will provide the necessary opportunity to obtain more complete and reliable pricing, properly assess the associated risks and exclusions, and ensure our final submission represents an accurate and considered offer that meets the project requirements.

We believe the additional time will support a more robust and competitive tender submission, reducing the likelihood of pricing omissions, scope gaps or assumptions that may otherwise affect the delivery and cost certainty of the project.

We therefore respectfully request approval to extend the tender submission deadline by 15 calendar days, from 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

Thank you for your consideration of this request. We look forward to your response.

Hi Julianne,

We respectfully request an Extension of Time (EOT) for the submission of our tender for the Sludge Dewatering Upgrade Project, extending the current submission deadline of 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

This extension is requested to allow sufficient time to obtain and assess vendor package pricing, receive outstanding subcontractor quotations, and develop a complete and accurate tender submission that adequately addresses the complexities and various elements of the project.

The current tender timeframe has presented several challenges, including:

•	Vendor package pricing and lead times: The specialised nature of the sludge dewatering equipment requires engagement with multiple vendors to obtain compliant technical and commercial offers. Allowing sufficient time for vendors to review the project requirements and develop their submissions is essential.

•	Subcontractor responses: A number of subcontractor quotations remain outstanding, with additional time required to obtain, review and clarify pricing to ensure all relevant scope elements are adequately covered.

•	Limited supplier participation: Several suppliers have declined to provide pricing due to the short turnaround time available. This has restricted the number of competitive quotations received and increased the time required to identify and engage alternative suppliers.

•	Project complexity and scope coordination: The project involves multiple interfacing elements, vendor packages and subcontracted works that require careful coordination to ensure the proposed solution is technically compliant and commercially complete.

•	Tender accuracy and completeness: Additional time is required to review vendor and subcontractor submissions, reconcile scope gaps and exclusions, confirm pricing assumptions, and undertake a detailed internal review of the estimate and overall tender submission.

The requested extension will provide the necessary opportunity to obtain more complete and reliable pricing, properly assess the associated risks and exclusions, and ensure our final submission represents an accurate and considered offer that meets the project requirements.

We believe the additional time will support a more robust and competitive tender submission, reducing the likelihood of pricing omissions, scope gaps or assumptions that may otherwise affect the delivery and cost certainty of the project.

We therefore respectfully request approval to extend the tender submission deadline by 15 calendar days, from 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

Thank you for your consideration of this request. We look forward to your response.

Kind regards,","answeredAt":"2026-10-19T22:00:00.000Z","answer":"Please refer to Addendum #7"},{"askedAt":"2026-10-22T22:21:00.000Z","question":"RFI02 - Enquiry

However, the tender documents place significant design obligations on the Contractor that will affect tendered prices and programmes. So that all tenderers price and programme on a consistent basis, we request that Council clarify the following:

1. Contractor design scope

Please confirm that the Contractor’s design scope includes the following, and advise any additions or deletions:

a) pile design and certification;

b) equipment plinths and access platforms;

c) thrust blocks not detailed on the drawings;

d) thickener mechanism, bridge, influent and stilling well, weirs, access and coatings;

e) feed averaging tank mixer and davit;

f) vendor packages, including the screw press, chemical dosing systems, compressed air, cake pump and pumps;

g) switchboard design and AS/NZS 61439 design verification;

h) update of the power system analysis, protection settings and arc flash study;

i) earthing, lighting and emergency lighting;

j) instrumentation design and the Functional Specification;

k) motorised gates and access control;

l) service water route and the conduit holds shown on the civil drawings.

2. Design verification and changes to the IFC design

Where vendor requirements, site conditions, authority requirements or design verification require changes to the IFC design, please confirm who is responsible for verifying the IFC design and identifying the changes needed to incorporate the vendor package designs.

3. Allocation of design risk

The Contract requires the Works to be fit for their purpose and requires the Contractor to warrant that the contract documents are complete and adequate. Once the IFC design has been updated, please confirm whether the Contractor bears the risk of any error, omission or inadequacy in the design, including any resulting time and cost.

4. Design reviews and approvals

Given the design scope above, please advise the number and stages of design submissions required, Council’s review periods, and all certification and authority approvals the Contractor must obtain, including building certification and Ergon approvals.
