title: Identity Governance Administration (IGA) & Privileged Access Management (PAM) Solutions and Services
description:
Suppliers are invited by the State of Queensland (acting through the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) – the Customer) to submit Offers for either one or both Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) Solution and / or Privileged Access Management (PAM) Solution and associated maintenance and support Services as further specified in this Invitation to Offer (ITO) TMRICT26098.

Suppliers may submit an Offer for:

	(a) an IGA Solution, maintenance and support Services only; or

	(b) a PAM Solution, maintenance and support Services only; or

	(c) both an IGA Solution and PAM Solution, with maintenance and support Services for both/each; or

	(d) a single Solution that meets the Requirements for both IGA and PAM, with maintenance and support Services.

All technology types will be considered (that is, Suppliers are not limited to submitting Offers for As a Service based solutions only), as well as alternative and innovative solutions which meet the Customer’s objectives and Requirements.

The Requirements are set out in the Invitation Documents and include the following in-scope Products and Services:

(a) IGA Solution and Services: a solution to satisfy the identity governance and administration Requirements including:

 (i) all applicable product components such as Licensed Software including modules, connectors, agents and related third party software (if any); and/or

 (ii) all applicable hosted components such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) / Platform as a Service (PaaS) including modules, connectors and agents (if any); and

 (iii) associated ongoing maintenance and support Services such as monitoring, maintenance, provision of updates, patches, new releases, remedial response and rectification, and provision of user documentation and continuous improvement; and/or

(b) PAM Solution and Services: a solution to satisfy the privileged access management Requirements, including:

 (i) all applicable product components such as Licensed Software including modules, connectors, agents and related third party software; and Hardware or on-premise installed components (if any); and/or

 (ii) all applicable hosted components such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) / Platform as a Service (PaaS) including modules, connectors and agents (if any); and

 (iii) associated ongoing maintenance and support Services such as monitoring, maintenance, provision of updates, patches, new releases, remedial response and rectification, and provision of user documentation and continuous improvement.

The following is out of scope:

	(a) configuration and customisation of the offered Solutions;

	(b) provision of integration services (other than supply of out-of-the-box connectors);

	(c) implementation services (including transition-in and transition-out services); and

	(d) end user help desk support (Level 1 Support Services) for the Customer’s end users – this will be managed by the Customer.

Any contract formed subsequent to this Invitation must be governed by the QITC Framework, Comprehensive Contract Conditions - ICT Products and Services, and the Draft Contract issued with the Invitation Documents.

Please submit all enquiries or clarifications directly through Vendor Panel.

DATA SOVEREIGNTY (MR2)

1. Does MR2 apply equally to all categories of Customer Data held by an identity governance or privileged access platform (for example, usernames, group memberships, entitlement metadata and authentication logs), or will TMR consider a risk-based approach based on the data's security classification?

2. What information security classification does TMR expect the Customer Data in the IGA and PAM Solutions to carry (for example, OFFICIAL or OFFICIAL: Sensitive)?

3. Schedule TMR1 requires that only false or non-personally identifiable data is used in non-production environments. Would TMR consider an offer where the Design, Build and Implement phase uses non-production environments hosted outside Australia (containing no Customer Data), with production hosted in Australia before go-live?

4. Will TMR consider an offer where Australian hosting is committed to by a contractual date, for example before production go-live of the relevant Solution?

5. Would customer-managed encryption keys held within Australia (so that data cannot be decrypted by parties outside Australia) be considered in assessing compliance with the "accessed" component of MR2?

6. Schedule D allows Innovative Offers that may not meet one or more Mandatory Requirements. Will TMR evaluate an Innovative Offer that does not fully meet MR2 against the same criteria as Conforming Offers? Are there particular conditions under which TMR would consider one?

SCOPE AND OFFER STRUCTURE

7. Part A 6.3(d) allows TMR to accept "Offers in part". Would TMR consider a PAM offer that addresses a defined subset of the PAM capability domains (for example, endpoint privilege management, credential and secrets vaulting, and password management), to sit alongside another supplier's solution for the remaining domains?

8. Is TMR intending to retain OpenText NetIQ for any identity functions after the IDAM Project, or is it expected to be fully replaced?

9. Which Microsoft Entra ID Governance capabilities (under TMR's E5/E7 entitlements) does TMR already intend to use, and where specifically does TMR see the remaining gap that the IGA Solution must fill?

VIABILITY SCREENING AND EVALUATION

10. What are the product viability screening thresholds (Part A 4.2.4)? Are they weighted by requirement priority (Must, Should, Could), and are IGA and PAM screened independently?

11. For a PAM-only offer, how will the SAP firefighter, IBM RACF and OT-related requirements be weighted in screening and evaluation relative to core PAM capabilities?

12. Would TMR accept a cloud-brokered session management approach (no customer-hosted jump box) as meeting the jump box and session isolation requirements (C1 3.6.12 to 3.6.14)?

SAP AND IBM RACF

13. How central is native SAP S/4HANA and IBM RACF connector governance to the IGA evaluation? Would TMR consider an approach where SAP and RACF governance continues through existing tooling, with the IGA Solution integrating via API or SCIM?

CERTIFICATIONS

14. Addendum 2C sets ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27017 and ISO 27018 as minimum certifications. Will an offer be excluded if it holds only some of these at submission, or will TMR consider a committed certification roadmap or equivalent attestations?

title: Culvert Replacement Works - Kellys Road, Omeo Valley
description:
Two existing failing pipe culverts that are located along Kellys Road over minor tributaries of the Mitta Mitta River are the subject of this report. At each of the sites, an existing reinforced concrete pipe culvert has deteriorated in condition to the extent that the East Gippsland Shire Council is investigating repair or replacement works.

An assessment of the existing sites has been carried out to determine and assess the range of options available for replacing each of the culverts. It is proposed for Site A that the existing DN1200 mm concrete pipe be replaced with single cell reinforced concrete culvert on a similar horizontal and vertical alignment as currently exists. The existing DN900 mm pipe at Site B can be repaired to a serviceable condition by re-laying the pipes at the culvert outlet.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
273 Main St
Bairnsdale, Victoria 3875
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Our Vision is to make East Gippsland an inclusive and innovative community that values its natural environment, puts community at the centre of Council decision-making and creates conditions in which communities can thrive.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Wednesday 25 November 2026 02:00 PM (AUS Eastern Daylight Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Kellys Road extends from the south east end of the Omeo Valley Road, which follows the Livingstone Creek from the Omeo Highway to the Hinnomunjie bridge across the Mitta Mitta River. The section of Kellys Road that is under the control of the East Gippsland Shire Council continues for 9.7 km to the Nine Mile Creek crossing. The road section that is the subject of this report was reconstructed and substantially upgraded by the former Omeo Shire Council in the early 1970’s, in accordance with an overall strategy to establish an alternative route between Omeo and Mitta Mitta that was less susceptible to winter snowfalls.

The road initially passes through open farmland that is used for stock grazing, before entering the Alpine National Park. The road section has a formed and gravelled surface, which is well maintained by the Council. The road has been subjected to oversize vehicles for past logging and bushfire suppression operations in the area but is predominately used for access to the farm properties, as well as by 4WD based visitors to numerous camping spots along the nearby Mitta Mitta River and within the National Park.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.01 – Construction window

Reference: Part 1 Item 4 (Tender Timetable); Part 2 Annexure Part A cl 27.1 & 35.2; Part 3 cl 1.25 (Project Timelines)

Part 1 indicates a March 2027 commencement. With possession 10 weeks after signing and Practical Completion 12 weeks later, site works would fall in winter (approx. May–August 2027). Please confirm Council's intended construction window and whether tenderers may nominate a later start (e.g. Spring 2027).
publicQuestions.answer: For the purpose of tendering Council an intended construction window.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.02 – Date for Practical Completion – conflicting provisions

Reference: Part 2 Annexure Part A cl 35.2 vs Part 3 cl 1.25 (Project Timelines)

Part 2 fixes the Date for Practical Completion at 12 weeks from possession of Site, while Part 3 cl 1.25 requires tenderers to nominate the contract period, commencing from acceptance of Tender. Please confirm which provision governs.
publicQuestions.answer: Contractors are required to nominate when works will commence and be completed, within the 12 week window from possession of site.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.03 – Liquidated damages cap / inclement weather

Reference: Part 2 Annexure Part A – Liquidated Damages; Part 3 cl 1.25 (Project Timelines)

Liquidated damages are $250.00 per day with the limit stated as 'Unlimited'. Please advise whether Council will accept a cap (e.g. 10% of the Contract Sum), and confirm that extensions of time apply for inclement weather and total fire ban days.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will not accept a cap on liquidated damages of 10%. Extensions of time do apply for inclement weather and total fire ban days. Contractors will be required to notify Council on the day where either instance occurs.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.04 – Site inspection and access

Reference: Part 1 Item 3 (Tender Briefing / Site Inspections)

No briefing or site inspection is scheduled. Please confirm tenderers may inspect both sites unaccompanied, and advise any access restrictions and a contact for access.
publicQuestions.answer: Council requests that all tenderers familiarise themselves with the site prior to submitting tender. Both sites are still open to the public and do not require access approval.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.05 – Side track vs road closure (Site A)

Reference: Part 3 cl 1.3 (Site A) & cl 1.10 (Site Access); Att. 2 Site A item 1.6

Part 3 cl 1.10 requires the road to remain open with a side track. Please confirm: (a) whether a short full closure with detour would be accepted at Site A for critical activities; (b) any requirements for the side track location or design (item 1.6 notes it is subject to the Superintendent's Representative's approval); and (c) that the side track footprint is covered by the NECMA permit and cultural heritage due diligence.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will consider a short full closure. Tenderers should provide details and benefits as a part of their tender submission. The installation of the sidetrack will be covered by the terms of the contract and will to ensure excavation and vegetation removal are kept to an absolute minimum.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.06 – Site A pipe class and construction method

Reference: Part 3 cl 1.3 (Site A) & cl 1.17; Drawings 256999A Rev C; Attachment 6

Please confirm whether the construction method described in the Part 3 Site A Scope Statement (rebuilding and compacting the embankment, then trenching through the compacted fill) is mandatory, or whether Council would consider alternative methods or pipe classes put forward by tenderers.
publicQuestions.answer: Council will accept alternate tenders however they must be accompanied by a conforming tender.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.07 – Site B salvaged pipes – rejection

Reference: Part 3 cl 1.4 (Site B); Att. 2 Site B item 5.1

If the salvaged DN900 pipes are rejected, please advise how Council intends the replacement pipes to be supplied and paid for (noting provisional item 5.1 in the Site B Pricing Schedule).
publicQuestions.answer: Contractors are to price supply and installation of 2 x 900mm pipes, if not required for these works, Council will purchase unused pipes.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.08 – Spoil disposal at Omeo Transfer Station

Reference: Part 3 cl 1.15 & 1.20

Part 3 cl 1.20 nominates the Omeo Transfer Station for excavated material, while cl 1.15 requires the removed concrete pipes to be disposed of away from the site but not within the nominated fill disposal areas. Please advise any charges or conditions at the Omeo Transfer Station, and where Council expects the removed pipes to be disposed of.
publicQuestions.answer: Contractor is to make themselves aware of fees and charges required to complete the works.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.09 – Wombat burrow at Site A outlet

Reference: Part 3 cl 1.3 (Site A – Existing Culvert)

Please advise of any fauna management requirements for the wombat burrow at the Site A outlet, and who is responsible for them.
publicQuestions.answer: Contractors are to ensure that all native fauna is protected at all times, however, certain cases may require intervention measures to be undertaken. In those cases, all attributable costs will be costed against the dayworks provisional item.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.10 – Site A – in-situ culvert backfill quantity

Reference: Att. 2 Site A item 2.4; Att. 6 (CPAA PipeClass – Site A); Dwg 256999A_9

Item 2.4 allows 1,460 m³ (solid) of selected in-situ backfill. The CPAA PipeClass Installation & Quantities sheet (Attachment 6) gives backfill of 38.804 m³/m and excavation of 41.8 m³/m, which over the 31.8 m culvert equals ~1,234 m³ backfill (~1,329 m³ excavation). Please provide the basis of the 1,460 m³, including the assumed extent and batter slopes of the excavation to remove the existing pipe, and confirm whether the quantity is measured solid (compacted).
publicQuestions.answer: 1460m3 allows for extra fill if required.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.11 – Site A – imported haunch/side/overlay zone material

Reference: Att. 2 Site A items 3.1 & 3.4; Att. 6 PipeClass; Part 3 cl 1.17

The basis of the imported haunch, side and overlay zone quantity in item 3.4 (50 m³) is unclear. Attachment 6 sets a 1.829 m trench width ('not to be exceeded') and a 100 mm bed zone, whereas Part 3 cl 1.17 requires the culvert base to extend 300 mm beyond the pipe (approx. 1.97 m wide) with 200 mm of bedding. Please confirm which requirement governs and the intended quantity, including whether the bed zone is included.
publicQuestions.answer: Supply of bedding is included in schedule item 3.01

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.12 – Site A – pavement depth and extent

Reference: Att. 2 Site A items 2.7 & 4.1; Part 3 cl 1.14 & 1.21; Dwgs 256999A_1 & _3

Item 4.1 (45 m³) and drawing 256999A_3 specify 150 mm of 20 mm Class 3 FCR, whereas Part 3 cl 1.21 specifies a total pavement depth of 150 mm comprising 100 mm of FCR. Please confirm the required FCR depth and the pavement extent measured in items 2.7 (220 m² subgrade trim) and 4.1, including the nominal 10 m of matching-in at each approach (cl 1.14).
publicQuestions.answer: Pavement makeup is 150 mm FCR.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.13 – Site B – in-situ backfill quantity

Reference: Att. 2 Site B item 2.4; Att. 5 (CPAA PipeClass – Site B); Dwg 256999B_5

Item 2.4 allows 260 m³ of selected in-situ backfill to the re-laid pipes and headwall. Only two pipes (4.88 m) are re-laid. Attachment 5 gives backfill of 10.988 m³/m and excavation of 12.9 m³/m, i.e. ~54 m³ backfill (~63 m³ excavation). Even allowing for the 1.0 m over-excavation (item 2.3) and headwall backfill, 260 m³ appears significantly higher than the design quantities. Please confirm the quantity and its basis.
publicQuestions.answer: Estimation is correct; it allows for over-excavation to bench the excavations to allow safe access.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.14 – Site B – imported haunch/side/overlay zone material

Reference: Att. 2 Site B item 3.4; Att. 5 PipeClass

Item 3.4 allows 50 m³ of imported zone material (the same quantity as Site A). For the 4.88 m of re-laid DN900 pipe, Attachment 5 gives haunch 0.241 + side 0.093 + overlay 0.560 = 0.894 m³/m, i.e. ~4.4 m³ (~5.1 m³ including the bed zone). Please confirm the intended quantity.
publicQuestions.answer: 15 cubic metres

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.15 – Site B – rock beaching quantity

Reference: Att. 2 Site B item 3.6; Dwg 256999B_1

The rock beaching quantity in item 3.6 (90 t) appears lower than the beaching areas shown on drawing 256999B_1. Please confirm the intended area, thickness and tonnage.
publicQuestions.answer: Tenderers to price supply & installation of 90t approved rock, as specified.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.16 – Site B – pavement reinstatement extent

Reference: Att. 2 Site B item 5.2; Part 3 cl 1.14 & 1.21; Dwgs 256999B_3, _4 & _5

Part 3 cl 1.21 requires reconstruction of the road pavement within the limits of work, and the Site B cross sections show a design pavement surface, but the Site B Pricing Schedule only includes provisional item 5.2 (20 m³). Please clarify the intended pavement scope and quantity at Site B.
publicQuestions.answer: Item 5.02 of schedule – Site B refers to “Site rehabilitation works” and not full pavement construction. The majority of the works required at Site B will be Pipe installation, backfilling and embankment formation.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01.18 – Site B – replacement pipe class and joint type

publicQuestions.answer: Site B nominates Tenderer to supply & install Class 2 pipes; whose dimensions and (default) interlocking joint will closely match the original DN900 (Class X) pipes that have been used at the site.

publicQuestions.question: RFI-01.19 - Site A – fill material balance / imported fill Reference: Part 3 – Proposed Works (Site A) & Earthworks; Att. 2 Site A items 2.3–2.5; Dwg 256999A_9 Part 3 states that the Site A culvert works are unlikely to generate sufficient suitable fill and that imported fill will be needed, but the Site A Pricing Schedule has no item for imported fill – only item 2.5 (300 m³ won from the adjacent cut batter). Based on the culvert long section (256999A_9), removing the existing culvert to 1.0 m below design invert on a 4.0 m base generates approx. 1,250–1,920 m³ of excavated embankment material (depending on batter/benching for safe access), against a fill requirement of approx. 1,650–2,470 m³ (over-excavation backfill, item 2.4 and formation outside the culvert excavation). Please confirm: (a) whether the cut batter source for item 2.5 is expected to make up the full shortfall, and its location; and (b) whether Council will add a provisional item for imported fill, or remeasure items 2.4 and 2.5.
publicQuestions.answer:
Tenderers are reminded that

1.1	Schedule of Quantities

A Schedule of Quantities for each site has been included in the Quotation documentation. No guarantee as to the completeness or accuracy of the items and quantities (excepting Provisional Quantities) shown in the Schedule is provided. The Contractor shall be responsible for determining the quantities (excepting Provisional Quantities), tasks and amount of work required to complete the works as specified.

Designers’ calculations indicate that Item 2.5 will be sufficient to make up the shortfall, but it entirely depends on how well the Contractor manages the site.

If unsuitable material is encountered within the excavations, then Item 2.8 allows for this.

Item 2.8 Provisional Qty has been increased to 250 Cubic .M to ensure sufficient fill is available.

Addendum 1 will be issued in due course.

publicQuestions.question: RFI-01.20 - Site B – replacement pipe class (schedule vs RFI response) Reference: Att. 3 Site B item 5.1; Council response to RFI-01.18 Site B Pricing Schedule item 5.1 describes the supply and installation of new Class 4 DN900 pipe, while Council's response to RFI-01.18 nominates Class 2 pipes with interlocking joints to match the existing Class X pipes. Please confirm the pipe class and joint type to be priced under item 5.1.
publicQuestions.answer: Site B - Tenderer to supply & install Class 4 pipes; whose dimensions and (default) interlocking joint will closely match the original DN900 (Class X) pipes that have been used at the site.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement Team,

In preparing our submission for CON2027 1806, we are seeking clarification on a few critical discrepancies between the specifications, drawings, and BOQ to ensure our pricing is accurate and compliant:

1. Headwall Specifications (Site B) Under "Supply and Delivery," Part 3 specifies the use of precast reinforced concrete headwalls generally in accordance with SD1931C. Conversely, under "Proposed Works – Site B," Part 3 requires a cast in-situ headwall, which is also what is detailed on Drawing 256999B_5. Please confirm if Site B headwalls are to be priced as precast or cast in-situ.

2. Pavement Depth Discrepancy Under "Pavement Make-up," the Specification states the pavement shall have a "total compacted depth of 150 mm". However, the very next sentence specifies the layer as Class 3 FCR at "100 mm compacted depth". The Typical Cross Sections (Drawing Sheet 3) show a 150mm compacted depth. Please confirm if the pavement layer is to be priced at 100mm or 150mm.

3. Concrete Pipe Disposal Location The Specification states that excavated concrete pipes must be disposed of "away from the site, but not within the nominated fill disposal areas" (the Omeo transfer station). No alternative tip facility is nominated. Does Council have a nominated facility for the concrete waste, or should tenderers price commercial disposal and transport independently?

4. Over-Excavation Base Width (BOQ vs. Drawings) BOQ Item 2.4 (Site A) and Item 2.3 (Site B) state an over-excavation base width of 3.0m (minimum). However, the Part 3 Specification and the Bedding Details on the drawings clearly dictate a minimum base width of 4.0m. Please confirm if tenderers should price the earthworks and backfill based on the 3.0m BOQ width or the 4.0m drawing width.

5. Site B Provisional Pipe Quantity (Item 5.1) Please confirm if the expected provisional quantity for Item 5.1 (Supply and Install new pipes in lieu of salvaged pipes) is strictly for 2 No. 2.44 m pipes to cover the missing section.

6. Missing Spreadsheet Formulas We note that multiplier formulas (Rate × Quantity = Amount) are missing in the provided Excel BOQ for Site A cells F6 and F30, as well as Site B cell F6. Please confirm if an updated BOQ spreadsheet will be issued, or if tenderers should manually correct these formulas in our submitted pricing schedules.

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Cast in Situ headwall required at site B

2. 150mm

3. Tenderers to price commercial disposal and transport independently

4. 4.0m Drawing width

5. Contractors are to price supply and installation of 2 x 900mm pipes, if not required for these works, Council will purchase unused pipes.

6. Council have checked formulas and they are all correct and working.

To Note: Addendum 1 will be issued in due course.

publicQuestions.question:
Which Defender product(s) are deployed/to be integrated — is Defender for Endpoint (the EDR) in use, or just built-in Defender AV? Any MDO/MDI/MDCA in scope?

M365 licensing (E3 / E5 / Business Premium / E3+MDE add-on)?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question: Which Defender product(s) are deployed/to be integrated — is Defender for Endpoint (the EDR) in use, or just built-in Defender AV? Any MDO/MDI/MDCA in scope?

Answer: Microsoft Defender is our current EDR.

AV is a blend of Microsoft Defender and Sophos Endpoint.

The capabilities of MDO/MDI/MDCA are all in scope, however these may be achieved via a different platform.

Question: M365 licensing (E3 / E5 / Business Premium / E3+MDE add-on)?

Answer: E5 and F3 licences.

publicQuestions.question:
1. What Microsoft 365 licensing tier does the City currently hold for staff (E3, E5, or other), and does it include Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P2 and Defender for Identity entitlements? This matters because REQ-21, REQ-60 and REQ-62 reference Entra ID signals and Defender, so knowing the licensing tier tells you whether that capability is already paid for or needs to be built into your price.

2. Does the City currently have an EDR or antivirus solution deployed across its servers and endpoints? If so, what product, and would it be retained, replaced, or made available to the Contractor at no cost?

3. Does the City currently operate a SIEM platform (for example Microsoft Sentinel) with an existing log workspace or retention, or is the Contractor expected to supply a SIEM entirely from scratch?

4. what are some key applications that require ingestions (understand TechOne is necessary) any others?

5. is there a current MDR, SOC in place already?
publicQuestions.answer:
Question 1. What Microsoft 365 licensing tier does the City currently hold for staff (E3, E5, or other), and does it include Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P2 and Defender for Identity entitlements? This matters because REQ-21, REQ-60 and REQ-62 reference Entra ID signals and Defender, so knowing the licensing tier tells you whether that capability is already paid for or needs to be built into your price.

Answer: E5 and F3 licences – Defender for Endpoint P2 and Identity is covered under E5.

Question 2. Does the City currently have an EDR or antivirus solution deployed across its servers and endpoints? If so, what product, and would it be retained, replaced, or made available to the Contractor at no cost?

Answer: Microsoft Defender is our current EDR.

AV is a blend of Microsoft Defender and Sophos Endpoint.

Question 3. Does the City currently operate a SIEM platform (for example Microsoft Sentinel) with an existing log workspace or retention, or is the Contractor expected to supply a SIEM entirely from scratch?

Answer: There is a basic Sentinel installation with an existing log workspace, this will need to be reviewed and fully configured or a new SIEM implemented.

Question 4. what are some key applications that require ingestions (understand TechOne is necessary) any others?

Answer: M365, TechOne and Sophos Firewall are the primary focus for applications.

Question 5. is there a current MDR, SOC in place already?

Answer: No.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Registration and licensing services are fundamental to road safety, personal mobility, economic activity and government service delivery across Queensland. They support customers and businesses, frontline employees, enforcement and regulatory activities, revenue collection, other government agencies, national transport arrangements and a large network of external service and data consumers.

At the center of this environment is the Transport Registration and Integrated Licensing System (TRAILS), first implemented in 1993 and progressively extended over more than three decades to support changing legislation, registration and licensing products, offences and sanctions, payments, customer channels, credentials and external interfaces.

TMR are seeking to determine whether a bounded Registration and Vehicle business capability can be progressively separated from the broader Registration and Licensing Services ecosystem without unacceptable disruption to services that remain dependent on TRAILS. The engagement must demonstrate how modern and legacy services can coexist; how nominated business processes, rules and transactions can operate outside TRAILS; how routing, integration, data ownership, write-back, synchronisation, reconciliation, security, recovery and operational continuity will be managed; and how the approach can scale beyond the initial use case without fundamental redesign. The resulting components and delivery patterns must reduce delivery risk, cost, dependency and complexity, provide a repeatable pathway for future modernisation horizons, materially reduce legacy dependency and establish retirement readiness. TMR must also retain sufficient knowledge, rights and practical capability for TMR or another delivery partner to operate, maintain, change and extend the resulting components independently.

TMR invites Offers for a market-led TRAILS Componentisation Proof of Concept (PoC)/Proof of Delivery focused on a bounded Registration and Vehicle capability. TMR may select one or more Suppliers for funded Concept Design. Suppliers that successfully satisfy the applicable progression criteria may subsequently be invited to deliver the Simple, Medium and Complex Use Case stages. Progression is not automatic, and TMR may stop or progress one or more Suppliers at each gate.

While the scope of this ITO covers the Funded Concept Design and potential PoCs, the PoCs will inform TMR’s future delivery and sourcing approach. TMR may progress one or more successful PoC Suppliers to subsequent implementation or scale activities or undertake a broader market approach. Any future approach will consider PoC outcomes, market and technology developments, value for money and TMR requirements. Participation in the PoC does not guarantee future work and progression may stop before Gate 5.

publicQuestions.question: Can you please clarify if the costs for geomembrane destructive testing and independent testing of geosynthetic material is to be included in this tender? As we have in-house NATA labs that can perform these tasks, we would like to include this price to give best value to the Council.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that tenderers are to include costs for geomembrane destructive testing and independent geosynthetic material testing as part of their tender submission.

Geomembrane destructive testing is already included under Item 16 of the Schedule of Rates and should be priced per test. As outlined in Clause 7.3.8.5 of S14, Council is responsible for the initial laboratory testing costs, with any additional testing resulting from failed destructive tests being the responsibility of the Geosynthetic Contractor.

Independent conformance testing of the GCL, HDPE geomembrane and protection and separation geotextiles is also required under the CQA Specification and S14. Tenderers should include separate rates for these tests under the ""Please insert any other applicable rates required to complete the works in accordance with the Specification"" section of the Schedule of Rates, including any associated sampling, transport and laboratory reporting costs.

Council has no objection to tenderers using their own in-house NATA-accredited laboratories, provided they are accredited for the relevant test methods, meet the independence requirements of the CQA Specification and are approved in accordance with the tender requirements.

All testing is to be carried out in accordance with the specified methods and frequencies. The Geosynthetic Contractor's existing CQC testing responsibilities remain unchanged.

publicQuestions.question:
We require some clarification on the Electrical Leak-Location Survey expectations and the intended methods of testing.

1. Can you confirm that the Electrical Leak-Location Survey is on the HDPE only?

2. Can you confirm that the grade of HDPE that is specified has a conductive backing to allow for a conductive element below the testing surface level?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Confirmed. Electrical leak-location surveys are required for the HDPE geomembrane only, in accordance with S14 Clauses 7.3.9.1 and 7.3.9.2.

2. The specified geomembrane is 2.0 mm thick, double-sided smooth black HDPE in accordance with S03 Clause 2.1. Conductive backing is not specified or required.

Tenderers are to allow for appropriate electrical leak-location testing methods suitable for the specified liner system, including the necessary electrical continuity and isolation arrangements in accordance with the applicable ASTM standards.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Coolroom and leaf store floor falls

Please provide the required gradients, finished floor levels and drainage layout for both rooms, including any revised slab/setdown details. Please also confirm how the falls are to be formed while maintaining the required minimum structural slab thickness and reinforcement cover, particularly now that no insulated PIR floor is required.

2. Drainage outlets and connections

Please confirm the number, locations, sizes and invert levels of the floor/channel drain outlets, their discharge destinations, and whether the 8 lm of grate/channel drainage allowed is sufficient.

3. Epoxy finish

Please confirm the coating specification, including any required coving, slip resistance or additional preparation/build-up.

4. Equipment pads

Please provide the confirmed condenser and other equipment locations, pad dimensions, loads and fixing requirements.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Coolroom and leaf store floor falls

Please provide the required gradients, finished floor levels and drainage layout for both rooms, including any revised slab/setdown details. Please also confirm how the falls are to be formed while maintaining the required minimum structural slab thickness and reinforcement cover, particularly now that no insulated PIR floor is required.

• Gradients to be in accordance with relevant Australian Standards

• Coolroom floor to drain out to Feed Prep Area, Feed prep area to have falls to grated drain

• No PIR panel in floor is assumed (TBC by coolroom manufacturer) (assumed PIR base is only required for freezers) if coolroom manufacturer requires a PIR base in coolroom and Leaf Store this will be treated as a variation to the contract.

• Falls to be formed by use of cementitious topping in setdowns.

• There is a wet area setdown detail shown on CS2798-ST5

2. Drainage outlets and connections

Please confirm the number, locations, sizes and invert levels of the floor/channel drain outlets, their discharge destinations, and whether the 8 lm of grate/channel drainage allowed is sufficient.

Grated drains per plan, allow single 100mm sewer outlet per grated drain, grated drain to have internal falls.

3. Epoxy finish

Please confirm the coating specification, including any required coving, slip resistance or additional preparation/build-up.

Allow fit for purpose, commercial grade 2 pack epoxy coating to coolroom and Leaf store floors, slip resistance per Aust Standards, applied direct to cementitious topping.

4. Equipment pads

Please provide the confirmed condenser and other equipment locations, pad dimensions, loads and fixing requirements.

Locations TBC on site, pad dimensions will need to be provided by mechanical subcontractor, concrete pads on ground for condensers and equipment, allow worst case scenario for service runs.

title: Expression of Interest - Head Contractor - UniSC Moreton Bay Stage 3
description:
The University of the Sunshine Coast (UniSC or the University) invites Expressions of Interest from suitably qualified and experienced Contractors for the delivery of the Moreton Bay Stage 3 (MBS3) project at the UniSC Moreton Bay Campus.

MBS3 comprises the construction of a new six-storey Building B1 and adaptive reuse of Building A1 Level 1, delivering additional teaching, learning, research, workplace and community-facing facilities required to support the continued growth of the Moreton Bay Campus.

Building B1 is anticipated to be approximately 11,500m² Gross Floor Area (GFA) and will incorporate a mix of contemporary learning and teaching spaces, learning commons, staff workspaces, research and industry collaboration facilities, simulation and visualisation environments, student-focused facilities, food and beverage offerings and community-facing clinical and engagement spaces.

Building A1 Level 1 will be refurbished and repurposed to provide specialist teaching, laboratory, simulation, research and support spaces integrated with the broader campus environment.

The project is being designed as a contemporary, high-quality higher education facility that reflects the University's strategic objectives for learning, research, industry engagement and sustainability. The design incorporates a hybrid mass timber and concrete structural solution, requiring respondents to demonstrate relevant capability and experience in the delivery of mass timber projects and associated procurement, construction and supply chain management activities.

title: QED 6537 2026 - Redcliffe SHS - SSS Home Economics
description:
Please contact Jaco Van Staden – Project Manager on jaco@honeywill.com.au with your company details and tender documentation will be emailed to contractors. Details of the site inspection will be advised in the email and letters to tenderers.

The Department of Education (DoE) is calling for tender submissions for the design and construction of a SSS Home Economics at Redcliffe SHS, located at 55 Klingner Rd, Redcliffe QLD 4020, as part of the Smart School Subsidy (SSS) program.

The existing heritage listed building is two levels and contains general learning classrooms and the existing home economics classroom. The refurbishment includes, but not limited to, the internal senior and junior kitchen upgrade of floors, walls, new equipment, extraction, electrical, new wash up area, new fridges and freezers, cameras, and storage space. All works are to be completed by April 2027.

Tender submissions will be accepted from contractors that meet the following requirements:

•	Appropriate QBCC Builders licences to undertake the entire scope of works

•	Professional Indemnity Insurance to the value of $1,000,000.00

Minimum PQC Level 2 Eligibility required.

Where a PQC Level is stated, the Principal is not obliged to provide tender documents, consider or accept a tender unless the tenderer is appropriately registered under the Queensland Government's PQC System for that PQC Level (or higher) and categories for which the tender is invited.

QBCC Licensing and Professional Indemnity Insurance

It is anticipated that a minimum of a QBCC (Low Rise) builders’ licence will be required for this project. Contractors are required to hold Professional Indemnity Insurance in accordance with the contract.

Submissions close on 27/11/2026 at 3:00pm via email to tenders@honeywill.com.au

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

1.	What is the total m2 area of wall and floor to be coated?

2.	What is the manufacturer, product name, formulation, thickness, age, or condition of the existing epoxy coating?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your questions.

1. Total area of walls and floors to be coated

The extent of the coating works is identified in the RFT scope of works. Tenderers are requested to calculate the approximate coating area using the existing drawings provided in 102991.3 Concrete Remediation 01 – Part 2A, Appendix ii – Existing Drawings, which forms part of the RFT documentation.

2. Details of the existing epoxy coating

The existing coating is in poor condition and requires removal as part of the remediation works.

The coating is understood to have been applied during the original construction of the inlet works in 1996. Council does not have records confirming the manufacturer, product name, formulation or thickness of the existing coating.

An addendum containing photographs of the existing structures will be issued through VendorPanel to provide additional information on their current condition.

Thank you.

publicQuestions.question: Is the overall vehicle length of 7,000 mm a strict maximum requirement, or would an increase to 7,500 mm be considered acceptable?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Alexander,

The 7,000mm for overall length is a guideline (based on one station maximum length of 7,000mm). Offer should include what is achievable as close as possible to 7,000mm.

publicQuestions.question: Is there a preferred equipment and stowage configuration to be adopted? The specification includes multiple equipment categories, including Standard Equipment, Bushfire Equipment, SFR Equipment, RCR Equipment, and BA Equipment. It is unclear whether the appliance is intended to accommodate all equipment categories simultaneously or a specific operational configuration.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Alexander,

The intent is for the design of the Appliance to able to carry all categories of equipment simultaneously. Regional requirements will dictate if certain categories will be fitted or remain empty.

General access for RCR and BA is normally preferred on the nearside of the Appliance (to mitigate risks when on the side of the road).

publicQuestions.question:

a defined equipment/stowage configuration; or

publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Alexander,

publicQuestions.question: Are QFD able to confirm if they will accept SCBA in seat with minimal cylinders in lockers?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Daniel,

Based on the Operational use of these Appliances QFD preference is to have Breathing Apparatus and spare cylinders stored in the body lockers and not in the cabin.

publicQuestions.question: Could QFD please confirm whether the non-coloured rows across all stowage tabs are to be supplied by QFD or are the Contractor's responsibility to supply?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Alexander,

Non coloured equipment is referencing equipment that is to be stowed on the Appliance but is not supplied by either QFD or the Supplier. It is used to reference space and stowage allocation.

publicQuestions.question:
1.	Does QFD require the automatic transmission and hydraulic retarder to be OEM factory fitted, or is an approved post-OEM conversion acceptable?

2.	The milestone payments in 3.2 add up to 100% (20/20/50/10) without any payment for receipt of the chassis. Will QFD consider a progress payment when the cab chassis is received, given its cost?

3.	Clause 15.1 asks for a “fully integrated hydraulic retarder”. Would an OEM exhaust or engine brake be acceptable as an alternative? Hydraulic retarders are limited or unavailable on most 4x4 chassis in this class.

4.	Clause 27.4 requires GOM and axle group loads not to exceed 90% of the Queensland regulatory maximum permissible limits. Please confirm whether the 90% requirement applies to the regulatory GVM/axle limits only, or also to the chassis manufacturer's plated GVM and axle ratings. For an 11,000 kg GVM chassis, does QFD therefore require the fully operational GOM to be no greater than 9,900 kg?

5.	The inventory tabs use colour coding for Contracted Supplier Supplied and QFD Supplied items; however, a significant number of items appear uncoloured. Please provide or confirm the definitive supply responsibility for every inventory item, including whether the listed weights and dimensions are the values to be used for tender mass and stowage calculations.

6.	33.1 ROPS. Please provide the required engineering/certification basis for the rollover protection structure, including the required load cases, factors of safety and applicable standard or QFD test criteria. Is QFD's preference for an internal cabin ROPS, an external/body-mounted structure, or is either arrangement acceptable subject to certification?

7.	Clause 13.5 states that the suspension system should be capable of being lowered when required. Please confirm whether this requirement applies to the iZone Medium 4x4 appliance and, if so, please define the required lowering functionality and purpose.

8.	13.2 108km/h. Please confirm whether the requirement to sustain a minimum 108 km/h at operational mass is an acceptance requirement. Where the selected chassis has an OEM speed limitation, does QFD expect that limitation to be modified, and will QFD's authorisation letter cover the required OEM/registration approval process?

9.	Clause 44 – Deluge System – Flow, Pressure and Operating Requirements

Clause 44.9 references Attachment E, CFA Ultra-Light Tanker Burn-Over Crew Protection System Specification, which specifies a nominal operating pressure of 220 kPa and total water flow of 10 L/min.

As this specification was developed for a single-cab ultralight appliance, could QFD please confirm whether these flow and pressure requirements are applicable to the larger iZone medium crew-cab appliance, particularly given the additional front bumper sprays and water-only wheel protection requirements?

10.	The IRR (3.75 m × 1.8 m) must be stowed below cab height (50.1). Is it acceptable for it to extend past the body footprint, given the length guideline of under 7,000 mm?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Chris,

See below responses.

Does QFD require the automatic transmission and hydraulic retarder to be OEM factory fitted, or is an approved post-OEM conversion acceptable?

Automatic transmission and hydraulic retarder are preferred to be OEM, but an approved post-OEM conversion is acceptable.

2. The milestone payments in 3.2 add up to 100% (20/20/50/10) without any payment for receipt of the chassis. Will QFD consider a progress payment when the cab chassis is received, given its cost?

The intent as stated in clause 3.2

1. Cab chassis - 100% receipt of base cab chassis (allows payment on the receipt of cab chassis)

2. Cab chassis - 100% receipt of cab chassis accessories and completion of Pre Delivery (allows payment on the receipt of accessories and completion of Pre Delivery at end of build)

3. Clause 15.1 asks for a “fully integrated hydraulic retarder”. Would an OEM exhaust or engine brake be acceptable as an alternative? Hydraulic retarders are limited or unavailable on most 4x4 chassis in this class.

A fully integrated hydraulic retarder is preferred but QFD is open to alternate offers.

4. Clause 27.4 requires GOM and axle group loads not to exceed 90% of the Queensland regulatory maximum permissible limits. Please confirm whether the 90% requirement applies to the regulatory GVM/axle limits only, or also to the chassis manufacturer's plated GVM and axle ratings. For an 11,000 kg GVM chassis, does QFD therefore require the fully operational GOM to be no greater than 9,900 kg?

This clause relates directly to the offered cab chassis taking into account front and rear axle limitations. At GOM - should not exceed 90% of front axle limits (TMR or OEM). At GOM - should not exceed 90% of rear axle limits (TMR or OEM).

5. The inventory tabs use colour coding for Contracted Supplier Supplied and QFD Supplied items; however, a significant number of items appear uncoloured. Please provide or confirm the definitive supply responsibility for every inventory item, including whether the listed weights and dimensions are the values to be used for tender mass and stowage calculations.

The uncoloured equipment is a reference to what is to be stored but not supplied by either Supplier or QFD. The supplied weights and dimensions are to be used for weight calculations and to identify storage solutions and locations.

6. 33.1 ROPS. Please provide the required engineering/certification basis for the rollover protection structure, including the required load cases, factors of safety and applicable standard or QFD test criteria. Is QFD's preference for an internal cabin ROPS, an external/body-mounted structure, or is arrangement acceptable subject to certification?

QFD would request a minimum of a FEA Analysis report of the proposed system as per Annex 5 ADR59/00 guideline. The calculation should consider loads according to ADR 59/00 Omnibus strength and conducted by a Registered RPEQ Engineer. QFD do not have a preference for an internal cabin ROPS or an external/body-mounted structure, either arrangement or combination is acceptable subject to certification.

7. Clause 13.5 states that the suspension system should be capable of being lowered when required. Please confirm whether this requirement applies to the iZone Medium 4x4 appliance and, if so, please define the required lowering functionality and purpose.

If an air bag suspension is offered this should have the ability to be lowered (to provide better ergonomics), however if this is not available on the offered cab chassis details of suspension should be provided.

8. 13.2 108km/h. Please confirm whether the requirement to sustain a minimum 108 km/h at operational mass is an acceptance requirement. Where the selected chassis has an OEM speed limitation, does QFD expect that limitation to be modified, and will QFD's authorisation letter cover the required OEM/registration approval process?

QFD will provide an authorisation letter cover the required OEM/registration approval process.

9. Clause 44 – Deluge System – Flow, Pressure and Operating Requirements

Clause 44.9 references Attachment E, CFA Ultra-Light Tanker Burn-Over Crew Protection System Specification, which specifies a nominal operating pressure of 220 kPa and total water flow of 10 L/min.

As this specification was developed for a single-cab ultralight appliance, could QFD please confirm whether these flow and pressure requirements are applicable to the larger iZone medium crew-cab appliance, particularly given the additional front bumper sprays and water-only wheel protection requirements?

QFD intent is to base the function on the, CFA Ultra-Light Tanker Burn-Over Crew Protection System Specification (Halo) and understand that there will be variances. Additional systems front bumper sprays and water-only wheel protection would be designed separately.

10. The IRR (3.75 m × 1.8 m) must be stowed below cab height (50.1). Is it acceptable for it to extend past the body footprint, given the length guideline of under 7,000 mm?

 

The IRR is acceptable to be partially inflated and as long as all regulatory requirements are met could extend past the rear body line.

publicQuestions.question:
Firm Pricing and Extraordinary Cost Escalation

Reference: Part B, Schedule 2, clauses 2.1–2.3, pages 26–27.

Given the potential duration of the program and the requirement for firm unit pricing, would QFD consider a provision for extraordinary, demonstrable increases in chassis, materials, imported components or freight costs arising from circumstances outside the supplier's reasonable control?

These may include geopolitical events, international trade restrictions, tariffs, shipping disruptions or other significant supply-chain events that could not reasonably have been anticipated when pricing was submitted.

Any adjustment would be subject to supporting evidence and agreement between the parties.

Firm Pricing and Extraordinary Cost Escalation

Reference: Part B, Schedule 2, clauses 2.1–2.3, pages 26–27.

Given the potential duration of the program and the requirement for firm unit pricing, would QFD consider a provision for extraordinary, demonstrable increases in chassis, materials, imported components or freight costs arising from circumstances outside the supplier's reasonable control?

These may include geopolitical events, international trade restrictions, tariffs, shipping disruptions or other significant supply-chain events that could not reasonably have been anticipated when pricing was submitted.

Any adjustment would be subject to supporting evidence and agreement between the parties.

2. Liquidated Damages and Delays Outside Supplier Control

Reference: Part B, Schedule 2, clause 1.7, page 26; Part B, clause 12 – Delivery Requirements.

QFD specifies liquidated damages of $500 per day for a maximum period of 90 days where contractual delivery dates are not achieved.

Can QFD confirm that liquidated damages will apply only to delays reasonably attributable to the supplier and that appropriate extensions of time will be available for circumstances outside the supplier's reasonable control?

Such circumstances may include chassis manufacturer delays, significant supplier disruptions, geopolitical events, international shipping delays, industrial action, natural disasters and delays arising from QFD-directed changes or approvals.

Where these circumstances occur, would QFD consider establishing a revised delivery schedule through agreement between the parties?

3. First-of-Type Appliance – Design Approval and Acceptance

Reference: Part B, Schedule 1 – Requirements; Schedule 2, clause 3.4, page 27.

Given the first-of-type engineering, integration and validation requirements associated with the 11-tonne iZone Medium appliance, can QFD confirm the proposed design review and acceptance process for the initial appliance?

Specifically, will QFD agree to defined review and approval milestones before full production of subsequent appliances commences?

4. Chassis Procurement and Supply Delays

Reference: Part B, Schedule 1 – Requirements; clause 12 – Delivery Requirements.

Given the reliance on vehicle manufacturers for chassis availability, production allocation and delivery, can QFD confirm whether contractual delivery dates will be established following confirmation of chassis supply arrangements?

Where an OEM subsequently changes chassis availability or delivery dates, despite timely ordering by the supplier, would QFD consider a corresponding extension to the appliance delivery schedule, subject to supporting evidence?

Contract Quantity and Purchase Order Commitments

5.Reference: Part A, section 1.2, page 4; Part B, Schedule 1, clauses 1.1–1.2, page 20.

The Invitation to Offer identifies a requirement for a minimum of 14 iZone Medium appliances.

Can QFD confirm whether the minimum quantity of 14 appliances will constitute a firm purchase commitment upon contract execution, or whether appliances will be ordered progressively through individual purchase orders?

This clarification will assist tenderers in establishing chassis procurement arrangements, component purchasing commitments, production capacity and pricing assumptions.

6. Liability and Insurance Exposure

Reference: Part B – Contract Details and Comprehensive Contract Conditions.

Can QFD clarify the intended application of the contractual liability cap, including whether the cap applies in aggregate across the contract or separately to individual claims?

Additionally, can QFD confirm how the liability provisions interact with the required public liability and professional indemnity insurance arrangements?

Warranty Commencement and Customer Acceptance

Reference: Part B – Warranty and Acceptance provisions.

Can QFD confirm that the warranty period for each appliance commences upon formal acceptance of that individual appliance rather than factory completion, invoice date or contract commencement?

Where acceptance is delayed for reasons unrelated to a defect or non-conformance attributable to the supplier, can QFD confirm how the warranty commencement date will be determined?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Chris

The department is intending to enter into a long-term contract with one or multiple suppliers for the build and delivery of iZone Medium Appliances.

The draft contract which was published alongside the specifications of this ITO is clear.

Suppliers are welcome to furnish preferred contract departures along with their offer, which will be considered if they are assessed as a preferred supplier.

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning,

Dear QFD Procurement Team,

To assist with our tender submission and ensure an accurate understanding of the appliance configuration, could you please provide photographs of the current iZone Medium Appliance?

We would appreciate images covering:

- Front, rear and both side elevations

- Roof and upper body areas (where available)

- Lighting installations and light towers

- Rear working area and equipment storage arrangements

- Pump and associated components

- Accessories, brackets and mounted equipment

- Internal storage compartments and cabinetry

- Any other features relevant to the appliance fitout

These photographs will assist us in confirming design assumptions and preparing an accurate and compliant submission.

Thank you for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Jo-anne,

As the iZone Medium Appliance is now based on a 11 tonne chassis photos of the current build would not be relevant. QFD would like submissions based on the specification. If you have more specific areas that pertain to the specification, please submit.

title: Construction works for Longreach Hospital Chillers Replacement Project
description:
Central West Hospital and Health Service (CWHHS) is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced mechanical services contractor to undertake the replacement of three existing air-cooled chillers at Longreach Hospital.

The works include the removal of the existing chillers and the installation, integration, testing and commissioning of three Principal-supplied Carrier 30RBP-670R air-cooled scroll chillers.

The successful contractor will be responsible for delivering all associated construction works required to provide a complete, fully operational and compliant chilled-water system. This includes coordinating the works within an operational hospital environment and minimising disruption to patients, staff and clinical services.

Expected timing: Construction required to be completed by 30 June 2027

Location: Longreach Hospital, Longreach, QLD, 4730

Tenderers must refer to the project specifications and drawings for the Longreach Hospital Chiller Replacement Project for detailed information regarding the scope, technical requirements, site conditions and contractor responsibilities.

The tenderer is responsible for reviewing all RFQ documentation and identifying any discrepancies, exclusions, assumptions or additional information required to deliver the works.

title: 201251 Depot Master Plan
description:
Sutherland Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced Lead Design Consultants to submit a Tender for the development of integrated Master Plans for four (4) key operational sites. The Master Plans will provide a coordinated, long-term strategic framework to guide the future use, development and management of Council's multidisciplinary operational facilities, ensuring they continue to meet current and future service delivery, workforce and community needs.

This project encompasses Council's operational depots at Bath Road and Ethel Road, the Animal Shelter at Taren Point, and the Community Recycling Facility at Kurnell. The Master Plans will assess three (3) design options representing different scales of development: optimisation of existing facilities, redevelopment and consolidation of operations, and strategic transformation incorporating alternative sites or relocation opportunities.

This Request for Tender (RFT) outlines the scope of services required from the Lead Design Consultant and the requirements for submitting a Tender. The Contract will be awarded to the Respondent that best demonstrates the capability, relevant experience and a comprehensive understanding of the project objectives. The successful Respondent will work collaboratively with Council and key stakeholders throughout the planning and design process to deliver practical, innovative and future-focused Master Plans that align with Council's strategic objectives and provide long-term value to the organisation and the community.

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification Question: Deployment Model and Infrastructure Responsibility

Clause 7 of Attachment C (Draft QITC Comprehensive Contract V1) incorporates both Module Order Form 2 (Software) and Module Order Form 3 (As a Service), and while Module Order Form 3 identifies the acquisition as Software as a Service and specifies that the As a Service shall be provided on private infrastructure within Australian jurisdiction, the same document leaves unchecked the field under Module 3 that asks whether the As a Service will be hosted by a third party, and Module Order Form 2A contemporaneously allocates backup responsibility to the Customer; accordingly, the Supplier respectfully seeks confirmation from the Buyer that: (a) the intended deployment model is Software as a Service whereby the Supplier is solely responsible for provisioning, maintaining, securing and operating the infrastructure and environment on which the solution runs; (b) Queensland Health will not be required to host, procure, maintain, or operate any infrastructure or server environment in connection with the solution; and (c) the allocation of backup responsibility to the Customer in Module Order Form 2A is a template default that is superseded by Module Order Form 3 and does not impose on Queensland Health any obligation to manage data backup or storage infrastructure.
publicQuestions.answer:
Queensland Health is open to considering both Software as a Service (SaaS) and Queensland Health-hosted deployment models.

Suppliers are requested to provide details of their proposed solution, including the deployment model and associated infrastructure, hosting, maintenance, backup and support requirements and responsibilities.

Suppliers should provide the relevant pricing information in accordance with the options outlined in the Invitation to Offer.

Module Order Form 2 (Software) applies to Queensland Health-hosted solutions, while Module Order Form 3 (As a Service) applies to Software as a Service. The applicable module will be determined by the proposed deployment model.

Suppliers should indicate in Attachment C (Draft QITC Comprehensive Contract V1) which Module will apply.

publicQuestions.question:
Thank you for the opportunity to seek clarification regarding the De-escalation Training RFQ.

To assist in preparing an appropriately tailored and competitively priced response, clarification is requested on the following matters.

1. Participant distribution and delivery locations

Could OIR provide an indicative breakdown of the approximately 400 participants by region, location and occupational group, including the anticipated number of sessions outside Brisbane?

2. Face-to-face and virtual delivery

While face-to-face delivery is preferred, is there an indicative proportion of training that OIR would consider acceptable for delivery virtually via Microsoft Teams?

3. AI-enabled and VR scenario training

Would OIR consider AI-driven interactive scenario training and virtual reality (VR) components as complementary elements of the facilitator-led training program, where these enhance practical learning and support the specified learning objectives?

4. ICT security and privacy requirements

Are there specific ICT security, cybersecurity, data hosting, privacy or approval requirements that would apply to the use of external digital learning platforms, particularly those incorporating AI-enabled functionality?

5. Ongoing digital practice and refresher access

Would OIR value ongoing access to interactive digital practice scenarios and refresher activities between scheduled training sessions? If so, would OIR prefer these to be included in the core proposal or offered as a separately priced option?

6. Delivery scheduling and commercial arrangements

Will regional training sessions be coordinated to minimise travel costs, and will approved travel and accommodation expenses be reimbursed at actual cost? Is there a minimum number of sessions expected to be commissioned, and what arrangements would apply to short-notice cancellations or rescheduling?

7. Contract terms and intellectual property

Could OIR clarify the intended ownership arrangements for newly developed training materials and the treatment of pre-existing supplier intellectual property, including proprietary training frameworks and digital learning technologies? Could OIR also confirm the intended contract commencement and completion dates, given the differences between the RFQ and draft contract?

Thank you for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning Simon, some answers below:

1. Participant distribution and delivery locations

Could OIR provide an indicative breakdown of the approximately 400 participants by region, location and occupational group, including the anticipated number of sessions outside Brisbane?

- Locations:

The locations will depend on demand. It is anticipated that the strong majority of sessions would be delivered within the South-East Queensland area. Regional centres could include Toowoomba; Maroochydore; Bundaberg; Townsville; Cairns.

 Travel and Accommodation

Indicative pricing is required in the RFQ and travel endorsement will form part of the confirmation and scheduling of sessions with the preferred supplier based on negotiated terms in the Short Form Contract.

Note in the contract is:?“Actual travel costs will be invoiced based on expenses incurred. We will seek OIR approval for any regional travel bookings in advance and will endeavour to secure the most cost-effective options available at the time of booking”

2. Face-to-face and virtual delivery

While face-to-face delivery is preferred, is there an indicative proportion of training that OIR would consider acceptable for delivery virtually via Microsoft Teams?

- For the purposes of De-escalation training, it is preferable for delivery to be in person however there may be times where we need to accommodate participants from across Queensland where virtual delivery via Teams is preferred for access and timeliness. We would anticipate the same group size. We may deliver as one day or two half days. Preference for virtual delivery would be two half days. Please include your recommendations.

3. AI-enabled and VR scenario training

Would OIR consider AI-driven interactive scenario training and virtual reality (VR) components as complementary elements of the facilitator-led training program, where these enhance practical learning and support the specified learning objectives?

- OIR would consider, however there would be significant ICT questions that have to be answered as part of the evaluation, please include as an alternate offer to the standard offer for consideration.

4. ICT security and privacy requirements

Are there specific ICT security, cybersecurity, data hosting, privacy or approval requirements that would apply to the use of external digital learning platforms, particularly those incorporating AI-enabled functionality?

- Yes there are specific ICT requirements that would need to be considered and mitigations put in place.

 For this, the preferred supplier (after evaluation) would need to complete our internal supplier cyber questionnaire and our Cyber, Privacy and ICT areas review and confirm.

5. Ongoing digital practice and refresher access

Would OIR value ongoing access to interactive digital practice scenarios and refresher activities between scheduled training sessions? If so, would OIR prefer these to be included in the core proposal or offered as a separately priced option?

- OIR would consider, include as an alternate offer to the standard offer.

6. Delivery scheduling and commercial arrangements

Will regional training sessions be coordinated to minimise travel costs, and will approved travel and accommodation expenses be reimbursed at actual cost? Is there a minimum number of sessions expected to be commissioned, and what arrangements would apply to short-notice cancellations or rescheduling?

- Grouping:

Travel will form part of scheduling approvals and the Contact Manager will work with the preferred supplier to mitigate unavoidable travel costs

 Travel and Accommodation

Indicative pricing is required in the RFQ and travel endorsement will form part of the confirmation and scheduling of sessions with the preferred supplier based on negotiated terms in the Short Form Contract.

Note in the contract is:?“Actual travel costs will be invoiced based on expenses incurred. We will seek OIR approval for any regional travel bookings in advance and will endeavour to secure the most cost-effective options available at the time of booking”

Numbers

Are the estimated 20–30 sessions for approximately 400 frontline staff an estimate across the full contract term

7. Contract terms and intellectual property

Could OIR clarify the intended ownership arrangements for newly developed training materials and the treatment of pre-existing supplier intellectual property, including proprietary training frameworks and digital learning technologies? Could OIR also confirm the intended contract commencement and completion dates, given the differences between the RFQ and draft contract?

- Intellectual Property

Under the General Contract Conditions: “Intellectual Property Rights created or developed in performing the Contract will be owned by Customer or Supplier.

If the new Intellectual Property Rights are owned by the Customer, the Customer grants the Supplier:

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ipswich is centrally located in the booming south east Queensland region of Australia. To the east is the capital city Brisbane, and to the west are the rural and agricultural areas of the Brisbane, Lockyer and Fassifern Valleys. The city is ideally positioned on the national road network - 40 minutes drive from Brisbane, an hours drive from the Gold Coast and 60 minutes drive from domestic and international air and sea ports.
Ipswich comprises an area of 1090 square kms and has a population of 180,000 people. Ipswich enjoys a subtropical climate and is a safe, friendly and multicultural city. Residents come from 115 different ethnic backgrounds, speaking 84 languages.
As Queensland's oldest provincial city, Ipswich has a rich history. It is renowned for its architectural, natural and cultural heritage. Ipswich proudly preserves and still operates from many of its historical buildings and homes, with more than 6000 heritage-listed sites. Ipswich also has a range of charming townships within the western rural areas of the city, each with its own legitimate claims of historical significance.

buyerQuestions: Does your solution have the capability for data to be hosted onshore in Australia?

publicQuestions.question:
1. What are Council's estimated annual, monthly, or daily volumes for incoming physical correspondence (letters, envelopes, parcels, packages)?

2. What proportion of inbound mail arrives as standard flats/letters versus large envelopes, bound booklets, cheques, plans, forms, ID cards, USB drives, or physical items/parcels?

3. What is the estimated annual volume or percentage of outbound mail returned as RTS, and what specific action is required upon scanning (e.g., automated address flagging, task allocation, or basic archiving)?

4. What are Council’s requirements for physical document retention post-digitisation (e.g., standard 90-day quarantine prior to certified destruction, or permanent retention of original paper source records)?

5. Does Council anticipate redirecting physical mail via an Australia Post PO Box / DX service directly to an off-site outsourced scanning facility, or a hybrid/on-premise model where hardware/software is deployed within Council premises for local staff?

6. What are the expected service level agreements (SLAs) from mail delivery at the digitisation facility to availability within Council systems (e.g., same-day ingestion by 12:00 PM for mail received by 8:00 AM)?

7.How should non-scannable, original legal/notarised documents, tenders, cash/cheques, or sensitive/confidential executive mail be segregated and physically routed to Council?

8. What level of data capture is expected during scanning: basic metadata indexing (date, sender, doc type, recipient) or advanced line-of-business extraction (Rates Assessment No, Property ID, Application/DA No, CRN, invoice data)?

9. Is full-text searchable PDF (specifically PDF/A-1a or PDF/A-1b for long-term archiving) required for all ingested inbound documents?

10. Does Council seek machine-learning/rules-based document classification to automatically route correspondence to specific teams or individual officers, or will Council's Information Management Team manually triage digitised queues?

11. How does Council envisage digitised mail entering Objective ECM (e.g., via Objective Connect/API, automated folder drop/ingestion agent, or email ingest), and is there an existing mandatory metadata taxonomy?

12. For specific inbound types (e.g., invoices, customer applications, rate queries), does Council require automated direct-to-record creation or workflow triggers inside Oracle Fusion or other line-of-business systems?

13. Does Council have specific technical digitization standards for Queensland State Archives (QSA) compliance (e.g., minimum 300 DPI, full color vs. greyscale, image enhancement rules, and digital chain of custody certificates)?

14. How does Council require redaction or restricted access controls to be handled for sensitive incoming correspondence (e.g., legal notices, human resources, child safety, health, or code-of-conduct complaints)?

15. What specific reporting or digital chain-of-custody logging is required from envelope receipt/slitting through scanning, QA, transmission, and physical archiving/destruction?
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for your questions, please see 260527-000421 - Addendum # 1 for Councils response.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Scope and lots: Will inbound correspondence management be procured with outbound in a single RFT, or as a separate lot or later stage?

2. Consortium and partial responses: Will Council accept responses from a prime with subcontracted partners, or from a respondent covering only part of the scope (for example inbound and digitisation)?

3. Inbound volumes: What is the approximate annual volume of inbound mail items and pages, and how many sites or delivery points receive it?

4. Inbound handling today: Is inbound mail opened and sorted centrally by the Information Management Team, and is it digitised at all? Where do digitised items need to land (Objective, SharePoint)?

5. Budget and term: Is there an indicative budget or contract term for the business case? Is the RFT expected to be one contract, or a panel?

6. Evaluation weighting: What is the relative weighting of the five criteria, and how heavily does Buy Ipswich count?

7. Physical items: Is Council expecting a single supplier to hold the mail, or can print, lodgement and returned-mail handling sit with different providers?
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for your questions, please see 260527-000421 - Addendum # 1 for Councils response.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon team,

As part of our ongoing response preparation for the City of Ipswich Expression of Interest for a Digital Mailroom Solution, we kindly seek clarification on the following questions:

• Could Council please provide what the expected frequency of the mailings are (e.g. daily, weekly, monthly, or ad hoc)?

• Will the Council print files be provided via SFTP?

• Are the letters A4 in size and printed in full colour?

• How many sheets are typically included in each mailpack?

• Will printing be single-sided or double-sided on each sheet?

• What envelope size is required (e.g. DLX)?

• Will the envelope stock be supplied by Council? If not, could Council please provide a sample or specification so we can accurately quote the required stock?

• Will postage be lodged using Council's Australia Post account?

• Does Council require composition or only submission of print-ready documents?

• “Hybrid Mail” – are the communications to residents currently generated on systems such as MS Word, or is it something different?

• What is the Current Council CRM software?

Thank you in advance for your assistance.
publicQuestions.answer: Thank you for your questions, please see 260527-000421 - Addendum # 2 for Councils response.

publicQuestions.question: Could Council please advise whether an indicative budget or budget range has been allocated for this project? This would help us scale our proposed methodology and quote to meet Council’s expectations.

publicQuestions.question: Does Council expect the Supplier to provide graphic design of the final strategy for public release, or will document design be undertaken internally by Council using Strategy content and layout prepared by the supplier?
publicQuestions.answer: Council will manage the graphic design of the final strategy and document design will be undertaken internally using strategy content and layout prepared by the supplier.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello

I'd like to seek some clarification on this RFQ specifically in relation to the requirement for $10M in Professional Indemnity Insurance cover. This is well above industry standards for a tender of this type.

We are a previous supplier to Townsville City Council and have encountered this requirement before and have had it reduced to $2M in Professional Indemnity. Having tendered and successfully worked with local councils all over Australia, Townsville is the only one we've seen with this requirement. Given the nature of the tender project, this seems onerous.

Best

Stu Watters

Co- Director

Morph Consulting Services
publicQuestions.answer:
Council's standard insurance requirement for this engagement is $10 million. If your organisation is unable to meet this requirement, please include details within your submission outlining the level of insurance currently held and/or the insurance coverage you are proposing for this engagement.

Please note that not meeting the $10 million requirement will not exclude your submission from consideration. Council will review the insurance arrangements proposed and assess their suitability on a case-by-case basis as part of the evaluation process should your submission be successful.

publicQuestions.question: Can you please provide an indicative contract range? thank you
publicQuestions.answer: Please provide your price for the anticipated cost of delivering the services described in the Scope. Pricing should reflect the resources, methodology and effort required to undertake the services and should not be based solely on the available budget. Council's indicative budget for these services is up to $50,000 (excluding GST).

publicQuestions.question:
