I'd like to seek clarification on this RFQ specifically in relation to;

1. Stakeholders - Does Townsville City Council have a list of it's stakeholders that it will be able to share with the successful company?

2. Budget - What is the budget range being applied to this consultancy by Townsville City Council?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
A1 - Stakeholder list will be provided to the successful responder.

A2. Please provide your price for the anticipated cost of delivering the services described in the Scope. Pricing should reflect the resources, methodology and effort required to undertake the services and should not be based solely on the available budget. Council's indicative budget for these services is up to $50,000 (excluding GST).

publicQuestions.question: The $20M public liability/ $20M Product liability and $10M professional indemnity are all extremely high for a written report requiring no registered trades or professions and a contract indicative budget of $50k. Would council please consider removing this requirement or reduce it prior to 23 November?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council's standard insurance requirements have been listed in the RFQ. If your organisation is unable to meet this requirement, please include details within your submission outlining the level of insurance currently held and/or the insurance coverage you are proposing for this engagement.

Please note that not meeting the requirement will not automatically exclude your submission from consideration. Council will review the insurance arrangements proposed and assess their suitability on a case-by-case basis as part of the evaluation process should your submission be successful.

title: Iama Barge Ramp Upgrade Project
description:
Torres Strait Island Regional Council invites tenderers from suitably qualified tenderers for the Iama Barge Ramp Upgrade Project. The upgrade works involve the removal and replacement of damaged sections of barge ramp as per designs and includes but not limited to:

- Site establishment and disestablishment

• Documentation, project management and compliance with all regulations,

• Stakeholder Consultations in conjunction with TSIRC for temporary closure of barge ramp,

• Geotechnical Investigations,

• Survey,

• Quality Assurance and Quality Control,

• Environmental Management,

• Demolition of existing Structures,

• Excavation of materials,

• Concrete Works in tidal area,

• Precast Panel casting/supply/install,

• Installation of rock revetment, and

• Any other item included in the contract documents and not detailed above.

publicQuestions.answer:
Hi Simon,

Answers to your questions below:

Q1) The drawings require installers of post-installed fasteners to be AEFAC accredited. Will equivalent manufacturer training (e.g. Hilti) be accepted, or is AEFAC accreditation mandatory?

A1.	Equivalent training and products are permitted.

2) Please confirm the required working hours. Volume_2_Project_Brief_Barrier_and_Balustrade.pdf states site access is 7:00am-5:00pm Monday-Friday (Page 5), however night works 9:00pm-4:00am are also specified (Pages 2).

A2. Nightworks are the correct working hours: 9pm-4am.

3) If a tenderer has not not delivered a road barrier project of this type (similar projects completed though), would this experience be considered acceptable for tender evaluation?

A3. 3.	Yes, similar experience will still be evaluated.

4) If a tenderer does not currently hold formal CC2 certification, can compliance with CC2 requirements, not a formal certification, be accepted for tender submission?

A4. Recommendation is that either the fabricator holds formal CC2 Certification or they provide a CC2 Compliance Certificate and engage their own third party certifier. For tender submission, proof of CC2 compliance without formal certification would be sufficient, provided there is demonstrated intent to achieve formal certification in the near future prior to tender acceptance.

5) Would the Principal consider an extension of the tender closing date to allow tenderers sufficient time to develop a compliant submission?

A5.	Yes, a 1 week extension has been applied

A25251004

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Team,

We are currently reviewing the tender documentation for the McKinlay Shire Housing project and would appreciate clarification on the following items.

1. Lot 1 vs Lot 6

Attachment B1’s summary table and pricing workbook place the 3BR house on Lot 1 and the 2 x 2BR units on Lot 6, but the per-site sheets show the reverse. Which is correct, and which lots require Council’s Development Approval?

2. Lot areas and survey

Can Council provide lot areas, dimensions and any existing contour or identification surveys for all four lots?

3. Payment for off-site work

Will Council accept stage-based progress claims (Item 33(b)) aligned to the pricing workbook milestones, AND payment for unfixed plant and materials (Item 34) for modules completed in the factory?

4. DA and infrastructure timing

What timeframe does Council expect for the two Development Approvals, and when will the water and sewer expansion works serving the sites be complete?

5. Furnishings

The pricing workbook includes a ‘Furnishings’ line. Is any furniture or loose equipment in scope?

6. Site office

Can the Superintendent’s site office for 8 people be shared across the four sites (or provided in an existing Council building) given they are all in Julia Creek?

7. Missing documents

Please provide Council’s environmental policy and Code of Conduct referenced in Schedule 10 and Spec cl. 4.4, and confirm working hours referenced in Annexure A Item 26A.

Thanks,
publicQuestions.answer:
1. There is an error in the current Part B Attachment B1 re Lot 1 vs Lot 6. An amended Part B Attachment B1 will be provided via addendum shortly. Site 2 & Site 4 will require Council Planning Approval. This will be undertaken once the approved floor plans, elevations, sections, landscape plans and site plans are provided.

2. Council does not have contour or ident surveys of the lots. Part B Attachment B1 specifies the successful Tenderer is to undertake these.

3. Council's proposed payment arrangements are set out in Annexure Part A of the Conditions of Contract. Item 33(a) provides for monthly progress claims, while Item 34 specifies that no unfixed plant and materials are eligible for payment under Subclause 37.3. Tenderers may propose alternative payment arrangements, including stage-based progress claims aligned with the pricing workbook milestones and payments for completed off-site manufactured modules. Any such proposal must clearly identify the proposed payment milestones, supporting evidence of completed work and appropriate security arrangements. Council will consider any proposed departures as part of the tender evaluation process.

4. DA planning approval is expected to take 4 weeks from provision of all required documents. Council will complete infrastructure upgrades and expansion by 29th February 2027.

5. No loose furniture or equipment is to be supplied. Furnishings relates to blinds, etc

6. A suitable site office can be located on the Eastern end of Site 4.

7. These are public documents and can be found on Councils website at:

Code of Conduct: https://www.mckinlay.qld.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/1/about-council/documents/tenders-and-eois/policies/policies-2025/employee-code-of-conduct-september-2025.pdf

Environmental Policy: https://www.mckinlay.qld.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/2/about-council/documents/tenders-and-eois/policies/environmental-policy-version-50.pdf

Working hours for onsite work are:

6:30am to 5:30pm weekdays

8am to 4pm Saturdays

No work on Sundays or Public Holidays

title: 201253 RFT Prince Edward Park Pedestrian Bridge Design and Construct
description:
Sutherland Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to tender for the Prince Edward Park Woronora Pedestrian Bridge Renewal Project.

The project involves the demolition of the existing pedestrian bridge and the construction of a new bridge to provide a safe, compliant, and durable pedestrian and cyclist crossing over the Woronora River. The works also include the construction of new shared pedestrian and bicycle path connections associated with the bridge replacement.

The existing bridge, owned by Sutherland Shire Council, provides an important active transport link between Prince Edward Park and Prices Circuit, connecting the northern and southern banks of the Woronora River. Due to the structure's age and condition, the bridge exhibits several defects and no longer meets current design and compliance requirements, affecting its safety, serviceability, and long-term performance.

The Woronora River is an environmentally sensitive area, and the successful Contractor will be required to undertake the works in accordance with all relevant environmental approvals, statutory requirements, and project-specific environmental management measures.

Mandatory site briefing will be required. Meeting location is at Prince Edward Park Carpark off Prince Edward Park Rd Woronora NSW.

Further to the RFI answered on 21-Oct, we have this follow-up RFI related to a common flood design basis for tender.

SSC has confirmed an updated flood modelling is being prepared but not available to tenderers, and that the contractor is to determine design flow velocity. Flood velocity & flood level directly govern pier and foundation design, bridge soffit level and approach ramp lengths, and therefore the tender price.

Performance Spec. Table 4.1 dictates the soffit level to be the maximum of (a) 400mm above existing soffit level, (b) 300mm freeboard above the 1% AEP design flood level, or (c) minimum vertical clearance required by TfNSW Maritime.

The 1995 Floodplain Management Study indicates a 1% AEP level of RL 3.8 to 3.9m at the site. Section 10.3 requires flood assessment to include climate change which may increase this level by 0.5-1.0m. To comply with Table 4.1 & Section 10.3 (and subject to post-award flood modelling) the proposed bridge deck soffit level could be as high as RL 5.2m (possibly higher). The existing bridge deck soffit level is approx. 3.1m. Therefore, the proposed bridge soffit would be in the order of 2.1m higher than existing soffit leading to significant cost.

Without a common basis, the tender prices will not be comparable, and the risk of post-award changes will be priced differently by each tenderer.

We request that SSC further reviews these flood modelling concerns and provide direction to all tenderers on what to adopt for both (1) flow velocity, & (2) bridge deck soffit level.
publicQuestions.answer:
Following clarification with SSC's Stormwater Asset Team, a new flood study and hydraulic model for the Woronora River is currently being undertaken. However, Council has been advised that the updated flood modelling data will not be available until March 2027, which is beyond the timeframe required to support the current tender process.

Accordingly, tenderers should not rely on the climate change allowance referenced in Section 10.3 of the Flood Assessment, as updated modelling information is not yet available.

For tender purposes, the replacement pedestrian bridge shall be designed with a maximum soffit level increase of 700 mm above the existing bridge soffit level. Any further flood assessment, hydraulic analysis, or design verification required to support the detailed design will be the responsibility of the successful contractor as part of the Design and Construct process.

title: Forward Notification of Upcoming North Coast Line North Culvert Replacement
description:
Forward Notification only - please await tender release on 13th January 2027 before initiating queries about the project.

The North Coast Line Culvert Renewal Project forms part of Queensland Rail's ongoing program to improve the safety, reliability and resilience of the North Coast Line (NCL). Maintaining the condition and performance of drainage infrastructure is essential to protecting the track formation, managing flood risks and ensuring the ongoing reliability of rail operations.

The project involves the replacement of six life-expired corrugated metal pipe (CMP) culverts and grout fill of two CMPs located between 1322.920 km and 1327.880 km on the North Coast Line, within the Nome to Stuart section south of Townsville. The existing culverts have been identified for renewal to address their deteriorating condition and maintain the long-term performance of the corridor's drainage infrastructure.

The proposed works involve the removal of the existing culverts and construction of new reinforced concrete pipe (RCP) culverts in accordance with Queensland Rail’s Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings. The scope includes associated excavation, foundation preparation, culvert installation, headwalls, wingwalls, scour protection, drainage improvements, formation reinstatement, access road reinstatement and protection or relocation of existing services, as required at each location.

title: 2920_2026-27_TTB_47 - Gayndah STP Upgrade
description:
North Burnett Regional Council (Council) invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit an Offer for the Gayndah Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade.

The project will rehabilitate and return the existing Pond 2 Rock Filter to operation and improve downstream treatment and disinfection while maintaining treatment plant operations and recycled water supply.

The Works comprise rock filter rehabilitation and reinstatement, an additional floating treatment wetland, a new sodium hypochlorite storage and dosing system, and decommissioning and demolition of the existing dosing building following successful commissioning of the replacement system.

Council intends to award one contract to a single successful Tenderer covering the complete Works, including the design obligations expressly identified in the Specification, construction, installation, testing, commissioning and handover.

Subject: RFT 2627-001 — Request for Clarification

Please clarify the following matters to enable accurate and consistent tender pricing:

1. Bins and volumes: Confirm the required quantities of 27m³ and 37m³ bins, availability of Council-owned bins, historical collection counts by waste stream, and Sunday movements. Please reconcile the stated annual tonnages of 2,351 and approximately 2,858 tonnes.

3. Fleet utilisation: Confirm whether nominated vehicles may service other customers between Council collections, provided all contractual service requirements are met.

4. Payment terms: Clarify which payment provisions prevail where the draft contract and specification differ, including whether payment periods are measured in calendar or business days.

publicQuestions.answer:
1. Bins and volumes: Confirm the required quantities of 27m³ and 37m³ bins, availability of Council-owned bins, historical collection counts by waste stream, and Sunday movements. Please reconcile the stated annual tonnages of 2,351 and approximately 2,858 tonnes.

Answer: We require 6 x 37m2 bins and 2 x 27m2 bins with the possibility of a 3rd over our busy period. Council do not own any bins. Most Sundays we will require bin relocation only, which will be requested the day prior.

Historical bin collection counts by waste stream – please refer to the table issued in Addendum 2

The RC manages a total of approximately 2858 tonnes of waste per year collectively of which the table refers to only the hard, green and cardboard streams (2,351 tonnes)

2. Disposal destinations: Confirm the designated processing facility for each waste stream, particularly green waste, where the specification appears inconsistent. Clarify responsibility for disposal fees and cardboard rebates.

Answer:

-	Green Waste – Bulla Organics Facility, Sunbury Road, Bulla

-	Hard Waste – Heidelberg Materials Landfill, Bridge Inn Road, Wollert

-	Responsibility of disposal fees – Council is responsible for the disposal fees and is invoiced by the disposal facility. The contractor is required to provide council with detail of the net tonnage disposed of at each facility for comparison with the disposal sites charging net tonnage.

3. Fleet utilisation: Confirm whether nominated vehicles may service other customers between Council collections, provided all contractual service requirements are met.

Answer: The contractor’s nominated vehicles are able to perform other duties around servicing our bins with the requirement that their expected return time be communicated with the Recycling Centre staff and bins are replaced in the bays if they are going to be offsite for an extended period.

4. Payment terms: Clarify which payment provisions prevail where the draft contract and specification differ, including whether payment periods are measured in calendar or business days.

Answer: Council shall pay the Contractor the amount certified for payment within 20 business days of the end of the month in which all of the information required by the Supervisor to support the claim for payment was received.

The specification (v2) has been amended to reflect business days where applicable. Please refer to Addendum 2

5. Price adjustments: Reconcile the conflicting price-adjustment provisions and confirm the applicable CPI formula and first adjustment date.

Answer: The specification (v2) and draft contract (v2) have been amended. Please refer to Addendum 2

6. Clarification deadline: Confirm whether the supplier-query deadline is 9 November 2026 at 2:00 pm AEDT, as stated in the tender conditions, or the later date displayed in VendorPanel.

Answer: Supplier query cut-off deadline is 2.00pm Monday 9 November. The date in VendorPanel has been amended to reflect this.

publicQuestions.answer:
Council has intentionally structured the EOI to focus on the business outcomes, functional requirements, and mandatory capabilities required of the replacement system, rather than prescribing specific technical designs, workflows, or implementation approaches. This approach is intended to allow respondents to demonstrate how their solution can best meet Council's requirements using contemporary CRM capabilities and industry best practices.

The mandatory requirements and desired outcomes are outlined within the EOI documentation and should be considered the definitive basis for preparing submissions.

At this stage, Council does not intend to provide detailed responses to individual questions regarding specific business processes, workflows, or implementation scenarios beyond what is already documented in the EOI. Respondents are encouraged to make reasonable assumptions based on the information provided and propose the most suitable approach using their standard product functionality and established implementation methodology.

Where a respondent believes additional information would materially affect their proposed solution, they may:

1.	Document any assumptions made within their EOI response.

2.	Identify any areas where further clarification may be beneficial.

3.	Describe how their proposed solution aligns with the stated requirements.

4.	Provide alternative approaches, configurations, or implementation options where they believe these may better achieve Council's desired outcomes.

Council is particularly interested in solutions that can meet the specified requirements using standard, configurable functionality with minimal customisation. Respondents should clearly identify any requirements that cannot be met through standard functionality and explain the implications, effort, and approach required.

publicQuestions.question: Does this trades panel include internal and external painting services?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, painting services are part of this panel. Identified in Volume 1 Section 2.3 and referenced in Volume 3 - Response Schedule, in the Trade Category nomination section.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Could the Council please confirm whether we can only apply for asbestos remediation services?

The trade category nomination in Volume 3 does not specify this category; however, it is mentioned in Volume 1 – Conditions of Tender, Section 2.3 (Trades and Services Required).

Thanks.
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, asbestos remediation services are included in the panel. Volume 3 - Response Schedule, include reference in Trades Category Nomination section under "Other (Specify)" listing.

publicQuestions.question:
Question in regards to Volume 4- Schedule of Rates:

SML1 provides specialised ASP1 powerline construction services where the personnel, plant, vehicles and equipment required vary significantly for each project. A standalone hourly labour rate would not accurately represent the cost of delivering the works and may be misleading without knowing the required crew composition, design, plant, site conditions and project scope.

Will Council accept Volume 4 marked “Quoted individually in response to each RFQ” for SML1’s nominated service category, with all pricing provided on a project-by-project basis rather than through a standing schedule of rates?
publicQuestions.answer: It is recognised that ASP1 powerline construction works can vary significantly between projects and that pricing is often dependent on the specific scope, conditions, plant/equipment & resources required. For the SML1 service category, Council will accept: “Quoted individually in response to each RFQ” where a standard schedule of rates is not suitable. Suppliers are encouraged to provide any indicative pricing information or details of general pricing methodology to assist Council's evaluation.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Please confirm if the tender closing date is 30th September or 5th August?.

Thanks.
publicQuestions.answer: The SMRC Trades Panel opportunity has been extended until 30 September 2026.

publicQuestions.question: Is Snowy Monaro Regional Council interested in Consulting Arborist companies providing a tender response under the Arboricultural services.
publicQuestions.answer: Yes - Consulting Arborist companies are welcome to provide a response.

Yes. It is recognised that Quantity Survey works can vary significantly between projects and that pricing is often dependent on the specific scope & resources required. Council will accept: “Quoted individually in response to each RFQ” where a standard schedule of rates is not suitable. Suppliers are encouraged to provide any indicative pricing information or details of general pricing methodology to assist Council's evaluation.

publicQuestions.question: just following up on question below please
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello,

There will be no civil, roadwork or plant hire included in the Trades Panel. Council has an existing Plant Hire Panel currently in place, which is due for renewal in the coming months. Once this panel is relisted, there will be opportunity for businesses to apply for that panel. Council's civil works will be engaged either through the Plant Hire Panel, or separate RFQ processes for larger packages of work.

Thank you.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

Just checking to see if pole/ asset inspection is part of this tender. For the below and above ground inspection of street lighting/ field lighting/ flag poles/ Shade sails etc.
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi,

General asset inspection (data collection) does not form part of the scope of this panel.

Inspections may be required on an adhoc basis to determine the scope of repairs on particular assets, and those accepted into the panel under the specific service relevant to the asset would be engaged. (ie an electrician would be engaged to inspect a faulty circuit board).

publicQuestions.question: Does this need any surveying service?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, surveying services are considered in this panel.

publicQuestions.question:
The Schedule of Rates provides a single Apprentice labour category. Apprentice employment costs may vary according to the applicable trade, industrial instrument, age and year or stage of training.

Please confirm whether tenderers may enter “N/A” or $0 where apprentice labour is not offered as a standalone category, with any apprentice costs incorporated into the relevant trade, crew or project-specific quotation. Alternatively, please confirm whether Council requires one blended apprentice rate applicable across all nominated trade categories.
publicQuestions.answer:
Where apprentice rates will be included into the relevant trade costs, $0 can be input.

However, Council encourages businesses to provide as much practical detail as possible in order to enable informed decision making of commercial engagements.

publicQuestions.question:
The Labour Rates schedule provides a Minimum Charge row across the Normal Hours, After Hours, Saturday, Sunday and Public Holiday columns, while the Call-Out & Travel schedule separately provides Standard, After Hours and Emergency Response Call-Out fields.

Please confirm whether tenderers may nominate different minimum labour engagements for planned and reactive works, for example a four-hour minimum for planned work and weekend/public-holiday attendance, and a two-hour minimum for reactive or emergency call-outs with additional labour billed in 30-minute increments.

Where the minimum labour engagement applies, please also confirm whether tenderers may enter $0 in the separate fixed call-out fee fields to avoid charging both a fixed call-out fee and a minimum labour charge.
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, tenderers may nominate differing minimum engagements depending on circumstances. Preference would be to have either a fixed call-out fee or minimum engagement hours specified, not both.

publicQuestions.question:
The Contractor Details sheet requests a single NSW Licence Number, while tenderers may nominate multiple categories that include both licensed and non-licensed services.

Please confirm whether this field may be entered as “N/A” where the nominated contractor does not hold a single overarching NSW contractor licence, with any regulated trade work undertaken by appropriately licensed personnel or approved specialist subcontractors. Alternatively, please identify the specific licence Council requires for General Building Maintenance, Landscaping & Grounds and Arboriculture / Tree Services.
publicQuestions.answer:
Please provide all relevant NSW Licence Numbers for the services being applied for.

If all services being applied for are non-licenced services, then no Licence Number is required and "N/A" is appropriate as the response.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Team, a few questions:

1. How are rates set for the two option years?

2. Will Council accept equipment and materials charged at cost plus a markup?

3. Are travel and remote allowance rates included in the price evaluation?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. In the "Vol 4 - Schedule Rates" document, there is opportunity to provide rates for all individual Financial Years. This is intended provide you opportunity to allow for expected increases with CPI.

2. Yes equipment and materials at cost plus markup is acceptable.

3. Travel and remote allowance rates will be considered in the price evaluation.

publicQuestions.question: Volume 4 has one set of labour rates per respondent. Where a respondent nominates more than one trade category in Volume 3 (for example painting, building maintenance and grounds), can a single set of rates apply to all of those categories, or should a separate Volume 4 be lodged for each category?
publicQuestions.answer:
If there is a single rate across all services being applied for, then a single Volume 4 will be fine.

Where varying rates would be applied for differing services, multiple tabs clearly marked with which service the rate relates to, will be preferred.

publicQuestions.question: For a category that includes some licensed work, will Council accept a panel member that carries out that work through a licensed subcontractor, provided the subcontractor's licence and insurances are uploaded to LinkSafe before it starts?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, if subcontractors will be utilised on individual projects/tasks, then their details can be provided when required.

publicQuestions.question: Volume 1 asks for a rate per square metre for carpet cleaning and concreting, but Volume 4 has no field for it. Is it acceptable to state those rates in Volume 3, item 18 (Schedule of Departures, Clarifications and Assumptions)?
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes, please provide these in Volume 3 Item 18.

Please also provide a note in Volume 4 in the Summary tab where this information can be found so that this is not accidentally missed during assessment.

title: Learner Logbook Solution
description:
The core objectives of this procurement activity are to select and engage a suitably qualified supplier and offer to deliver a future Learner Logbook (LLB) solution. Delivering the future Learner Logbook solution provides an opportunity to improve the experience of Queensland learner drivers and driver instructors, which forms part of the Queensland Government's commitment to become Australia's most customer-focused government.

The new LLB solution will include a contemporary and accessible user experience on a secure, mobile device application on both Apple IOS and Android operating systems. The Department is seeking a solution that improves on the current in-use application experience for learner driver and supervisor users and department level 1 support admin users. The Department is seeking long-term value for money while delivering a modern, secure, positive and accessible user experience. Further details on what the Department is seeking are in the below in scope, and in the enclosed CDSB1 Requirements.

In Scope

The proposed procurement is intended to secure a modern, supportable, mobile-based digital application for learner drivers and supervisors and supporting admin staff portal for departmental use and reporting, including associated hosting, support, reporting, maintenance, and transition services.

Explicitly Within Scope:

•	Provision of a modern and accessible digital learner logbook application, including native mobile applications for iOS and Android

•	Provision of an Admin Portal used by Department admin users to provide level 1 customer support and perform operational duties.

•	Customisation and configuration to CDSB branding and aligning to Queensland laws, TMR graduated licensing requirements and policies

•	Hosting and operational support arrangements, including Australian-hosted data infrastructure.

•	Reporting and analytics capabilities

•	Transition-In services, including data migration from the legacy platform and comprehensive testing to ensure accurate data transfer.

•	Implementation services, testing, onboarding support and cutover activities

•	Transition-out services for end of contract

•	Maintenance, bug fixes, security maintenance. Ensure uptime and availability to users, including updates, patches and upgrades to operating system versions and Appstore availability

•	Ongoing support as level 2 point of escalation to resolve support queries from the CDSB level 1 team who deal directly with end users

Potential additional items for scope:

•	Integration and enhancement of features, including for example integration with Queensland Government agency systems for data verification and road safety learning methods. Potentially enhancements to be priced into the contract with a price list and initiated by CDSB when decision made to implement additional enhancements. However, this is a nice-to have and would not preclude a successful offer if not offered in initial offering and was offered as a pipeline activity in future years.

The QITC modules for products and services categories likely includes:

•	As a Service, for example Software As A Service (SaaS) or licensed software. Software Maintenance included, including remedial and preventative maintenance, patches, fixes and continual improvement;

•	Software Development Services for the Learner Logbook application which may include bespoke development, customisation or configuration or if additional customisation of an existing application is needed. Potentially there is a suitable learner logbook application in existence with customisation and configuration to meet the Customer’s requirements, or potentially a similar application that can be customised for the purpose of a Learner Logbook application, or a new build.

•	Managed Services (e.g. transition-in services, data migration, hosting, ongoing support with service levels, and transition-out services) system and security testing IE vulnerability testing, Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) testing, Penetration system. Support services at level 2 and above to assist CDSB admin users who are unable to resolve support issues at level 1.

•	ICT Professional Services module to be included but services to be completed under a SOW if /when required by the Customer, which may include enhancements, features, and other services required by the Department.

•	Integration Services for future integrations as required to be performed under a future statement of work (SoW).

Out of scope

•	End user (public consumer) consultation and change management.

•	Level 1 support directly with external users (e.g. learner drivers or supervisors)

•	Integrations with the TMR managed TRAILS.

The Department’s position is the Department will continue providing level 1 support direct to external users. External users contact the Department by calling, emailing, or attending a customer service centre to make support requests, that is, dealing with government staff initially. If CDSB cannot resolve the level 1 query, then the Department will escalate to the supplier, and the supplier will provide level 2 and above support.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
In 2016, the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) launched the Learner Logbook application to support learner drivers in recording the supervised driving hours required to obtain a driver licence. The application and its supporting systems were developed for TMR.

Since its launch, the learner logbook application has received only minor enhancements. The technology is now approximately 10 years old and largely digitises the processes of a paper logbook, limiting its ability to meet contemporary customer and business expectations. App-store feedback also identifies some user issues. There is an opportunity to provide an improved digital experience for learner drivers, supervisors and CDSB administrative users.

Following Machinery of Government changes in mid-2025, responsibility for the Learner Logbook solution transferred to the Department of Customer Services, Open Data and Small and Family Business (CDSB). This includes responsibility for the supporting systems and the ongoing management of the contract and support arrangements.

title: ITO - Analytical and Laboratory Services
description:
Seqwater is seeking a suitably qualified Service Provider to deliver analytical, laboratory and transport services to support water quality and environmental monitoring across its waterways, treatment plants and bulk water networks.

The core scope includes the supply of sample containers and prepacking, courier transport, sample receipt and processing, laboratory analysis, electronic data delivery, reporting, exceedance notifications, dedicated account management, technical support and customer service. The Service Provider must also provide 24/7/365 support and emergency response capability.

An optional separable portion covers services associated with Seqwater’s Bulk Chemical Testing Program.

Seqwater reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to award each separable portion independently and to different Service Providers. Tenderers may submit a response for the core scope, the optional separable portion, or both.

title: EOI Provision of Catering Services for Whyte Island
description:
Queensland Fire Department (QFD) School of Fire and Emergency Service Training (SFEST) invites

suppliers to participate in an Expression of Interest (EOI) for the Provision of Catering Services for

Whyte Island, Brisbane.

The objective of this EOI is to gain an understanding of the current markets capability to provide

catering services, including viable alternative service models, menu options, efficiencies and

opportunities to achieve cost savings. This information obtained will support the organisation in

determining the best methods to meet identified needs.

publicQuestions.answer:
1. What hours must we operate, and is there a guaranteed minimum spend or management fee to cover staffing during quiet periods?

We are not dictating hours of operation, but we expect our mealtimes will be met. At this stage of the process, we are seeking options not detailed submissions.

There is no commitment to any management fee at the moment.

2. What costs would we pay—for example, rent, utilities, cleaning and equipment maintenance?

There is currently a rent component (includes utilities and maintenance) for the current onsite services, and this would be applicable if the proposed model remains the same way.

The catering provider will be expected to clean areas utilised if providing service onsite.

publicQuestions.question:
Could QFD provide daily booked meal numbers by meal period for a representative quiet week and busy week? Separately, are average daily walk-up sales or transaction numbers available for food and barista coffee?

For the nine FFDU recruit courses in Appendix 2, how many of the 16 recruits per course typically qualify for catering? Should suppliers allow for lunch and both teas on each of the 80 training days for each eligible recruit? For the estimated 1,100 QAS officers, how many catered days per officer should suppliers assume?

Are there any days or times when walk-up food or barista coffee must be available regardless of booked numbers?

Would occasional use of Building A for meal holding, service and clean-up attract rent? If so, what indicative amount should suppliers allow, and would it be charged per use, per day or for a fixed period?
publicQuestions.answer:
Our current state includes a supplier on site which provides catering for recruits plus other catering when required. Staff are also able to purchase food and coffee. I would include all 16 recruits per course and allow for lunch and both teas.

QFD are open to alternative options, we are not necessarily looking for the same arrangement as the current state.

Further information will be provided at the next stage; for the EOI we are after proposed solutions.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning

Help Enterprises looks forward to the opportunity to tender for this service with QFP.

Our questions are as follows:

1. Can QFD provide historical catering volumes for the past three years, including breakfast, morning tea, lunch, afternoon tea, dinner, retail food sales, and barista coffee sales?

2. What commercial arrangement is QFD considering for the future service, for example a licence agreement, facility management model, commission arrangement, subsidy model, or a traditional catering services contract?

3. Will the future supplier have exclusive rights to provide catering, café, coffee, vending, and food retail services across the Whyte Island site?

4. Can QFD clarify which party will be responsible for utilities, waste disposal, pest control, cleaning, equipment servicing, preventative maintenance, and replacement of kitchen equipment listed in Appendix 1 including equipment responsibility;

 - What motored, portable, hand held and utensil equipment is available, or is Help expected to provide all of these?

 - Is there a list of Crockery and cutlery availability

5. Are there any planned capital upgrades or equipment replacements for the kitchens and dining facilities during the proposed contract period?

6. Can QFD provide indicative frequencies and notice periods for catering events, as referenced within the EOI?

7. What service level expectations apply to after-hours, weekend, public holiday, and emergency response catering requests, including minimum response times? E.g. Re Weekend schedule and requirements - Is there a specific example that can be provided that shows us how much notice is given and the highest demand: As a supported employment agency, we have specific requirements around staffing in weekend work and have to consider shifting to blended/open employment offerings if notice is too short.

8. Can QFD provide any guidance on the anticipated contract term and extension options that may be included in the Invitation to Offer (ITO) stage?

9. Will site inspections be made available to shortlisted suppliers prior to the Invitation to Offer stage to allow detailed assessment of facilities, logistics, and delivery points across the campus?

10. Will suppliers be required to maintain stock for walk-up purchases and retail sales, and can QFD provide historical sales data for sandwiches, wraps, snacks, beverages and coffee?

11. Are there any mandatory sustainability, social procurement, or local content requirements that suppliers should address as part of their submission?

12. If selected as the preferred supplier, would QFD consider allowing the successful contractor to utilise the existing kitchen and catering facilities for external commercial catering activities outside of QFD operations, provided such use does not impact QFD service delivery, security requirements, or site operational needs? If so, what conditions or restrictions would apply?

13. Would QFD support a catering model that incorporates meaningful employment opportunities for people with disability at the Whyte Island facility, and are there any site-specific requirements or considerations regarding accessibility, supervision, training, or workplace modifications that suppliers should be aware of?

14. Is Help expected to provide Consumables: e.g. foil, clingwrap, detergent, dishwasher chemicals.

15. Can you confirm that Help would be responsible for the following or is there a separate contractor;

- Cleaning & maintenance of fixed equipment, repairs/breakdowns.

- Grease trap pumping and hood & canopy service

- Rubbish removal

Thank you very much for your consideration. Helps team looks forward to your reply.

Matthew Berry

Commercial Development Manager
publicQuestions.answer: This is an expression of interest only, when we go to tender further information will be available including a site visit. QFD are only after options at this stage to help us determine our future requirements.

title: Consultancy Services Panel
description:
Ballina Shire Council invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably qualified and experienced consultants to provide professional consultancy services across one or more of the following categories:

1.	Environmental consultancy services

2.	Strategic planning services

3.	Civil engineering services

4.	Water and wastewater services

5.	Project management services

6.	Roads and traffic services

7.	Multidisciplinary consultancy services

Council will use this EOI process to establish a panel of prequalified consultants, shortlist providers for future procurement processes, or invite selected respondents to participate in future requests for quotation or tender processes.

Submission of an EOI does not guarantee appointment to a panel, inclusion in future procurement processes, or the award of any work.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ballina Shire Council is located on the New South Wales Far North Coast, 770 kilometres north of Sydney and 190 kilometres south of Brisbane. The Shire, an area of 484 square kilometres, is set amongst a picturesque rural-coastal landscape and enjoys a temperate to mild subtropical climate.

The Shires resident population is approximately 45,000 with major service centre Ballina servicing the major townships of Alstonville, Lennox Head, Wollongbar, and Wardell. As well as a number of smaller villages and localities including Cumbalum, Teven, Tintenbar and Knockrow.

Ballina Shire Council acknowledges that we are here on the land of the Bundjalung people. The Bundjalung are the traditional owners of this land and are part of the oldest surviving continuous culture in the world.

publicQuestions.question:
Council’s services spreadsheet omits a selectable Multidisciplinary Consultancy category although EOI identifies it. How should respondents nominate category G, and is a companion schedule acceptable?

May a respondent select a subcategory when only a defined structural engineering subset is offered, provided the limitations and specialist interfaces are disclosed in the methodology?

The evaluation criterion refers to category-specific publicly available standard and senior hourly rates, but the supplied workbook has only one pair of rate cells. Should respondents provide one pair overall or one pair per nominated category?

Are the EOI indicative hourly rates assessment-only, with future services priced through project-specific negotiated rates and lump-sum quotations, including travel and specialist disbursements?

How does Council assess regional/office-location contribution for a Melbourne-based specialist that regularly works in adjoining Byron Shire and will use approved local subcontractors?

Can respondents submit the names of intended specialists and state that ABN, formal consent and evidence will be provided if shortlisted, or must each prospective subconsultant be formally committed at EOI close?

For relevant-project value, will Council accept professional-service value as commercial-in-confidence (with a range or on-request disclosure), or is a numeric dollar figure mandatory?

Does Council require the entire Quality, Environmental and WHS management system manuals or are approved policies, plan summaries and sample registers sufficient? Is ISO accreditation optional?

For structural/temporary-works-only services under Roads and Traffic, must respondent hold a separate traffic-management/road safety accreditation, or is it acceptable for the traffic component to be separately subcontracted?

Are interstate engineers eligible for professional design roles subject to applicable NSW registration, and are there specific nominated disciplines/registration categories for this panel?

Are all seven categories intended to be accessible to small specialist firms, or will proposals be assessed against full-service requirements across each nominated category?

Can Council provide its Statement of Business Ethics and confirm acceptable method of signing the Conflict of Interest declaration (electronic signature or signed PDF)?

Will Council provide any standard panel deed, rate escalation provisions and interstate travel/disbursement policy before shortlisted respondents accept appointment?

Does Council intend to request specific local availability or maximum response times for emergency assessment call-outs, and may providers nominate advance mobilisation/lead times?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1) Council’s services spreadsheet omits a selectable Multidisciplinary Consultancy category although EOI identifies it. How should respondents nominate category G, and is a companion schedule acceptable?

A1) Respondents can provide details of any multidisciplinary services as a separate submission.

Q2) May a respondent select a subcategory when only a defined structural engineering subset is offered, provided the limitations and specialist interfaces are disclosed in the methodology?

A2) Yes.

Q3) The evaluation criterion refers to category-specific publicly available standard and senior hourly rates, but the supplied workbook has only one pair of rate cells. Should respondents provide one pair overall or one pair per nominated category?

A3) Respondents should provide their highest senior and standard hourly rate for all, rather than each, categories. It will be considered as an indicative gauge of a respondents competitiveness.

Q4) Are the EOI indicative hourly rates assessment-only, with future services priced through project-specific negotiated rates and lump-sum quotations, including travel and specialist disbursements?

A4) Assessment only. Pricing will be requested and provided per separate RFQ's.

Q5) How does Council assess regional/office-location contribution for a Melbourne-based specialist that regularly works in adjoining Byron Shire and will use approved local subcontractors?

A5) Council will assess locality aspects from Local and Community criteria. It is suggested that any local sub-contractors are identified and location provided as part of Local and Community responses.

Q6) Can respondents submit the names of intended specialists and state that ABN, formal consent and evidence will be provided if shortlisted, or must each prospective subconsultant be formally committed at EOI close?

A6) It is suggested that a full list of possible sub-consultants be provided with their ABN.

Q7) For relevant-project value, will Council accept professional-service value as commercial-in-confidence (with a range or on-request disclosure), or is a numeric dollar figure mandatory?

A7) Respondents can provide a range of project value or provide no amount at all.

Q8) Does Council require the entire Quality, Environmental and WHS management system manuals or are approved policies, plan summaries and sample registers sufficient? Is ISO accreditation optional?

A8) Plan summaries are sufficient. Copies of accreditation would support any undertaking a respondent makes that they hold such accreditation.

Q9) For structural/temporary-works-only services under Roads and Traffic, must respondent hold a separate traffic-management/road safety accreditation, or is it acceptable for the traffic component to be separately subcontracted?

A9) Traffic compenents can be sub-contracted. Sun-contractors can be identified in the applicable requirement.

Q10) Are interstate engineers eligible for professional design roles subject to applicable NSW registration, and are there specific nominated disciplines/registration categories for this panel?

A10) Professional staff must hold valid registration in NSW for any services offered.

Q11) Are all seven categories intended to be accessible to small specialist firms, or will proposals be assessed against full-service requirements across each nominated category?

A11) Services for any sub-category can be offered.

Q12) Can Council provide its Statement of Business Ethics and confirm acceptable method of signing the Conflict of Interest declaration (electronic signature or signed PDF)?

A12) Councils Statement of Business ethics is available from Councils website via the link provided in the specifications. Electronic Signature of signed PDF are acceptable.

Q13) Will Council provide any standard panel deed, rate escalation provisions and interstate travel/disbursement policy before shortlisted respondents accept appointment?

A13) Council will issue an invited RFQ to applicable consultants from the shortlist which will include the scope/brief for works required on a case by case basis. The RFQ will specify the contract instrument and request fully itemised pricing.

Q14) Does Council intend to request specific local availability or maximum response times for emergency assessment call-outs, and may providers nominate advance mobilisation/lead times?

A14) Council will not specify or require any defined response times.

publicQuestions.question:
We are preparing a submission for the above EOI and would appreciate clarification on how nominated service categories will be assessed.

Could Council please confirm:

1. Whether respondents must be able to deliver all services listed under a category in order to nominate for that category, or whether it is acceptable to nominate for a category where only some of the listed services can be provided. For example, under the Water and Wastewater category, would it be acceptable if your firm could provide most of the services but not all of them, such as water and wastewater treatment?

2. If partial coverage is acceptable, whether Council would like respondents to state which services within the category they do and do not offer (for example, in the Table of Services Offered or in the capability statement for that category).

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.answer: Accreditation, such as ISO, is not mandatory. Respondents must address systems management requirements by demonstrating their current actions and protocols. If respondents cite accreditation, Council would like to confirm same by sighting a copy of the accreditation.

publicQuestions.question: Will Council consider submissions from providers of digital asset and compliance management platforms (for example, hazardous materials registers) under Part A or Section 8.8? publicQuestions.question: For Question 5, Council requests at least three recent relevant consultancy/project examples. Council is currently developing a standard consultancy agreement as an available instrument for engagements under this new panel. It is currently being reviewed by Council's legal service provider.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Ballina Shire Council Procurement Team,

We are currently reviewing the Expression of Interest for the Consultancy Services Panel (EOI5071 / BSC5071) and assessing our potential participation in selected service categories.

To ensure that our submission is appropriately aligned with Council's requirements and expectations, we would be grateful if you could clarify the following additional points:

1. “Section 7.13 states Part E covers infrastructure, planning, environmental, operational and corporate projects. Can Council confirm that corporate and operational projects (e.g. business improvement, systems implementation, service reviews) are expected to be engaged through the Project Management panel?”

2. “Respondents may nominate specific sub-categories within a service category. Will submissions be assessed per sub-category or per category as a whole?”

3. “Section 14 refers to hourly rates ‘per specific category’, but the Table of Services Offered provides a single standard and senior rate. Should respondents provide one rate pair per nominated category, and should rates be quoted inclusive or exclusive of GST?”

4. “How will ‘Office Location’ be assessed: location within the Ballina LGA, the Northern Rivers region or NSW? Will a committed on-site presence or a locally based sub-consultant be considered?”

5. “For recent projects (section 12.2), will comparable public sector projects delivered outside NSW or internationally be considered, and are overseas referees acceptable?”

Thank you in advance for your time and assistance. We look forward to your response.

Kind regards,
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. “Section 7.13 states Part E covers infrastructure, planning, environmental, operational and corporate projects. Can Council confirm that corporate and operational projects (e.g. business improvement, systems implementation, service reviews) are expected to be engaged through the Project Management panel?”

A1. Council is not seeking corporate project (e.g. business improvement, systems implementation, service reviews) solutions.

Q2. “Respondents may nominate specific sub-categories within a service category. Will submissions be assessed per sub-category or per category as a whole?”

A2. Submissions be assessed per sub-category submitted.

Q3. “Section 14 refers to hourly rates ‘per specific category’, but the Table of Services Offered provides a single standard and senior rate. Should respondents provide one rate pair per nominated category, and should rates be quoted inclusive or exclusive of GST?”

A3. We are seeking indications of the highest generic senior and standard rates to gauge general price competitiveness.

Q4. “How will ‘Office Location’ be assessed: location within the Ballina LGA, the Northern Rivers region or NSW? Will a committed on-site presence or a locally based sub-consultant be considered?”

A4. Physical presence with the Ballina LGA will be scored higher, then regional, NSW, outside NSW.

Q5. “For recent projects (section 12.2), will comparable public sector projects delivered outside NSW or internationally be considered, and are overseas referees acceptable?”

A5. Public sector projects and referees within NSW will attract higher scoring. Respondents are free to submit support for any comparable projects.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Hourly rates. The “Table of Services Offered” provides for one Standard Consultant and one Senior Consultant rate per respondent, while EOI clause 14 states rates will be evaluated “per specific category”. Should respondents offering multiple categories provide one rate pair only, or a separate rate pair for each category? If per category, may this be provided as an attachment to the Excel sheet?

2. GST. Should hourly rates be submitted inclusive or exclusive of GST?

3. Multidisciplinary services (Part G). The Excel sheet has no row for Multidisciplinary Consultancy Services. Is nominating Part G in the written response sufficient, or should it be added to the sheet?

4. Submission format. Items 2–7, 9 and 10 each request “a separate document”. Will Council accept a single combined document with clearly labelled sections for each item, uploaded against each question?
publicQuestions.answer:
A1. Please provide your highest senior and standard rate

A2. Please provide rates exclusive of GST

A3 Please add as additional rows to the Excel sheet

A4. Please submit as separate documents for each question. Responses per category can be consolidated for each question.

description:
Queensland Government is seeking applications from Suppliers who wish to register to be a Preferred Supplier for Grocery, Dairy and Beverage Products. This is a follow on from the initial application request period released on QTenders in March 2021 (HSQ101256). As part of this Preferred Supplier Panel we are accepting supplier applications at any time. Suppliers who have submitted an application via the initial registration process (HSQ101256) do not need to resubmit an application.

The Preferred Supplier Panel categories include:

Grocery Products Dry Goods

Biscuits; baking mixes and supplies; flour and milled products; soups; stocks; powders; packaged desserts; savoury snacks; confectionary; nuts; grains; legumes; jelly; spreads; jams; preserves; sugar; sweetener; dry pasta; rice; noodles; cereals; oats; porridge; pulses; seasoning; dried herbs; spices; sauces; dressing; canned goods; vinegar; condiments; dried fruit; dried vegetables; fruit cups pureed fruit.

Frozen Goods

Meat; poultry; fish and seafood; vegetables; fruit; pies; pastries; cakes; generic prepared frozen meals; muffins; desserts, ice cream and convenience foods.

Miscellaneous

Packaged (chilled or dry) smallgoods such as sliced meats, fats and oils; butter; margarine; eggs and egg products; tofu; hommus.

Dairy Products All milk products (such as white milk; flavoured milk; specialty milks (soy, Ultra-high treatment and lactose free milk); long life milk; powdered milk; evaporated milk; condensed milk; buttermilk); yoghurt; custard; cream; sour cream; cheese

Beverages Tea; coffee; chocolate powders; juice; cordial; spring water; soft drink; sports drinks.

•Fresh Food (Vegetable, Meat and Bread Products)

•Texture modified foods

•Prepared meals for Therapeutic Diet Requirements of Texture Modified Diets

•Thickened fluids

•Kitchen Consumables

publicQuestions.answer:
Council has a vast portfolio of structures and buildings across our large municipality, with over 800 structures which includes up to 400 buildings.

The building portfolio is made up of the following:

•	Council staff occupied properties, such as admin centres, Corporate offices, library’s, Customer Service Centres, major sporting centres.

•	Council managed Commercial leased properties, such as Cafes, Restaurants or Caravan Parks.

•	Council managed Community leased properties, such as sporting buildings / stadiums or small local sporting clubs.

•	Council privately leased properties, such as private parkland or road reserve areas.

Regarding the number of jobs that we typically see at our properties, this is difficult to capture holistically, as this varies depending on age of the condition and age of the asset. External factors such as weather conditions and use also plays an important part in the call our rate of any one particular property.

Dear colleague,

Thank you for the opportunity to tender for this request. Please provide the following noting key interest is category 2.

1. Which roles are in Category 2? Can Council supply a Job Dictionary for one of them?

2. Roughly how many assessments a year?

3. Should our results be recorded on the Suitable Duty Register, or in a separate report that maps to it?

4. Can a psychologist sign the register, given it asks for a "Doctor / Specialist"?

5. Is telehealth acceptable for any or all of the assessment?

6. Is Council looking for reports in prose and are there any pre-determine templates (acknowledging risk ratings matrix)?

Thank you for your consideration

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Respondents,

Please find response belowL

1. Which roles are in Category 2? Can Council supply a Job Dictionary for one of them?

Council is seeking information from the market proposing possible approaches to fitness for work assessments for roles. Vendors are encouraged to provide proposals that detail an approach for how Council could conduct suitable assessments for roles at different levels of the organisation. Council has not yet determined the ongoing requirement for this category, seeking to understand how the market foresees that such an undertaking could occur for a workforce of its diverse nature and varying levels of risk.

2. Roughly how many assessments a year?

Council engaged approximately 600 new starter employees in the past 12 months.

3. Should our results be recorded on the Suitable Duty Register, or in a separate report that maps to it?

The Suitable Duty Register is utilised in our Workers Compensation Return to Work program – it is not relevant to this engagement, albeit that it is included in the Job Dictionary template. The results of your assessments should be provided on your own report template, covering suitability for relevant aspects of the role.

4. Can a psychologist sign the register, given it asks for a "Doctor / Specialist"?

Yes, a suitably qualified psychologist could provide the report on the provider’s template as per the clarification in question 3 above.

5. Is telehealth acceptable for any or all of the assessment?

Providers are encouraged to outline their assessment methodology and suitable methods of interaction with our people based on ensuring that a reliable and replicable methodology can be utilised to ensure consistency in decision making.

6. Is Council looking for reports in prose and are there any pre-determine templates (acknowledging risk ratings matrix)?

Council is seeking a standardised template/s to be provided by the Provider, ensuring that there is a consistent application of Council’s risk matrix and that recommendations are made in light of Council’s terminology to assist review and decision-making. Council reserves the right to seek further clarification or additional information from the provider on individual assessments where required.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon Yanine

Thank you for providing the information regarding the tender.

We are considering submitting a response for Category 1, Pre-employment Medical Assessments. Before progressing, we were hoping to better understand the Council’s requirements around lung function testing/spirometry.

In particular, could you please provide some further context regarding:

the rationale for including lung function testing within the current pre-employment assessment, if it is in fact included;

which roles or worker groups currently require this testing;

any identified workplace exposures that have led to this requirement, for example dusts, silica, fumes, chemicals or other respiratory irritants;

whether the testing is intended to establish a pre-employment baseline, form part of statutory health monitoring, or assess fitness for a specific role; and

what lung function information or reporting the Council currently receives from its provider, including whether there is a particular testing protocol or reporting standard required.

Understanding the underlying occupational risk and the Council’s intended use of the results will help us determine the most appropriate testing methodology and ensure our proposed service is fit for purpose.

Thank you in advance
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Respondents,

Please find responses below:

•	the rationale for including lung function testing within the current pre-employment assessment, if it is in fact included;

Lung function testing is required only for identified roles. The Safety Work NSW Codes of Practice for How to manage and control asbestos in the workplace and Managing the risks of silica from engineered stone in the workplace outline Council’s obligations in providing regular testing to workers who are likely to be exposed to airborne contaminants such as asbestos and crystalline silica. Spirometry (lung function) testing is organised every two years for employees who may be exposed to airborne contaminants.

•	which roles or worker groups currently require this testing;

Roles that have been identified for this program as part of the existing employee establishment include; Art teachers working specifically with ceramics, Qualified Trade staff, Civil Works road crews.

•	any identified workplace exposures that have led to this requirement, for example dusts, silica, fumes, chemicals or other respiratory irritants;

Environmental exposure testing is conducted by a qualified provider for Council on high-risk areas on a regular basis. This testing has established that some worker may be potentially exposed to:

Asbestos

Crystalline Silica

Isocyanates (panel beaters/painters using 2-pack paint)

•	whether the testing is intended to establish a pre-employment baseline, form part of statutory health monitoring, or assess fitness for a specific role; and

The test for new employees is intended to establish a pre-employment baseline, as part of Council’s statutory health monitoring.

Fitness for role will only be considered if a person’s results place them in a high or extreme risk category for ongoing exposure due to a pre-existing health condition that would preclude them from completing the inherent requirements of the role.

•	what lung function information or reporting the Council currently receives from its provider, including whether there is a particular testing protocol or reporting standard required;

Council adheres to the SafeWork NSW advice for Lung Function testing: Work health assessments | SafeWork NSW

The current testing regime uses a Spirometer and a Vitalograph Bacterial Viral Filter (BVF).

Individual results should form part of the overall pre-employment assessment report, highlighting the level of risk as a current baseline.

title: Sports & Recreation Plan
description:
PREPARATION OF MCKINLAY SHIRE SPORT AND RECREATION PLAN

McKinlay Shire Council invites your firm to submit a written quotation for the provision of specialised consultancy services to develop a comprehensive, forward-looking Sport and Recreation Plan.

1. Project Overview & Background

Council is committed to fostering active, healthy, and connected communities across our region. To ensure our sport, active recreation, and community infrastructure effectively meet current and future needs, Council is seeking an experienced consultancy firm to undertake a complete review and redevelopment of our strategic framework for sport and recreation.

To assist in understanding our contextual foundation and strategic alignment, Council will provide successful respondents/tenderers with copies of:

•	McKinlay Shire Council 2010 Sport and Recreation Plan

•	McKinlay Shire Council Community Strategic Plan 2019-2026

•	McKinlay Shire Council Corporate Plan 2025-2030

2. Scope of Services

The successful consultant will be required to deliver an end-to-end plan, incorporating the following core stages and tasks:

1.	In-Region Site Inspection & Facility Assessment

o	Conduct an on-site visit to the region to inspect existing sport, recreation, and community facilities (including sports grounds, arenas, aquatic centre, indoor spaces, tennis courts, gym, parks, and trails).

o	Assess facility condition, functionality, spatial coverage, maintenance/lifecycle status, and opportunities for upgrading or multi-use optimisation.

2.	Strategic Direction & Alignment

o	Review relevant local, regional, and state sport and recreation policies, funding guidelines, and demographic trends.

o	Align proposed strategy directly with Council’s overarching Strategic Plan and regional priorities.

3.	Community & Stakeholder Engagement

o	Design and execute a robust community consultation strategy targeting local residents, sporting clubs, community groups, schools, Health Service and key regional stakeholders.

o	Conduct online and physical surveys, public workshops/drop-in sessions, and targeted interviews with key sporting association representatives and community members.

o	Engage regularly with appropriate Council Staff and Elected Members to identify current and future needs for Sport and Recreation across the Shire

4.	Executive Presentations & Governance Engagement

o	Attend an initial on-site meeting to present preliminary findings, scope alignment, and key emerging themes to Council's Senior Executive Leadership Team and Elected Members.

o	Attend an on-site meeting upon completion to present the final draft plan and executive briefing prior to formal Council adoption.

Tourism: Yes, tourism opportunities and visitor usage must be integrated into the plan.

Auditing and Mapping: Open space spatial mapping is a core component. Facility Assessment: A strategic visual and functional condition assessment (e.g., identifying aging equipment, safety compliance, and maintenance needs).

Consultation: Council requires a hybrid engagement model, including a community workshop in Julia Creek and an online/paper survey for remote and outlying residents. Council will host public sessions and promote consultation via our weekly newsletter, Facebook, and local flyers.

Schedule: Council has not set fixed milestone dates and expects the successful tenderer to propose a realistic project schedule and timeframe.

publicQuestions.answer:
To ensure our methodology, resourcing and fee accurately reflect Council's expectations, could you please clarify the following:

1. Number of facilities: Could Council provide an asset register, or confirm roughly how many sport and recreation facilities need inspecting, and in which towns?

The assessment covers approximately 15 to 18 primary sport, recreation, and park facilities across the three townships of Julia Creek, McKinlay, and Kynuna. A detailed asset register will be provided to the successful contractor upon appointment to finalise the inspection schedule.

2. Multi-asset precincts: Where one precinct has several assets (for example fields, courts, amenities and lighting), should it be assessed as one facility or should each asset be assessed separately?

To ensure a cohesive strategic overview, precincts should generally be evaluated as a single site, while capturing individual component conditions (e.g., courts, lighting, or amenities) within that precinct's broader assessment to ensure no maintenance or upgrade requirements are overlooked.

3. Level of assessment: Please confirm the condition assessment is a strategic visual and functional review. That means identifying visible defects, functional limits, maintenance needs and improvement opportunities, not detailed structural, building services or compliance investigations.

Confirmed. The Sport and Recreation Plan is intended to provide a high-level strategic and functional review to support community liveability, workforce attraction, tourism, and future funding applications, rather than exhaustive engineering, structural, or compliance audits.

4. Purpose of the condition data: Is the assessment meant to guide strategic investment and grant applications, or is asset-level condition data needed for Council’s asset management system? If the latter, please advise the required format and rating scale.

The primary purpose of the data is to guide strategic capital investment, future planning, and external grant applications.

5. Facility sheets: Does Council expect a separate assessment sheet for each facility (photographs, observations, condition rating and recommended actions)?

Council welcomes contractor best practice; however, providing concise individual facility profiles or summaries containing key observations, condition ratings, and photographic logs will be valuable for executive decision-making.

6. Demand forecasting: Will Council accept strategic demand forecasting based on demographic data, local club participation, state sporting associations and community consultation, rather than separate demand modelling for each sport?

Yes. Given the regional context, Council is open to practical, strategic demand forecasting grounded in demographic data, club participation rates, state sporting body insights, and targeted community consultation.

7. Recommendations and costings: Please confirm the Plan should identify recommended upgrades, renewal priorities and future specialist investigations, with detailed technical assessment, design and cost planning to be done separately later.

Confirmed. The Plan should establish strategic priorities, upgrade recommendations, and order-of-magnitude priorities, leaving detailed technical design and formal cost planning for subsequent project phases.

8. Site visits: Has Council assumed a minimum number of site visits or on-site consultation sessions? Will Council arrange access to facilities and introductions to clubs and user groups?

Council will assist with stakeholder introductions, facility access, and local coordination. Given the geographical spread of the shire, Council welcomes Quoters to propose their recommended site visit schedule and consultation approach based on their professional expertise in remote regional communities.

9. Fee Structure and Scope Assumptions. Given that the total number of assets has not been specified, would Council accept a lump-sum fee based on an agreed asset schedule, defined inspection methodology and nominated site visits, with any material additional scope subject to prior approval?

Quoters are encouraged to submit their proposed fee structure based on the preliminary facility estimate provided. Council is open to reviewing fee models (such as lump-sum structures with clear baseline assumptions or provisional sums for out-of-scope items) during the final contract negotiation phase.

vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
This Invitation to Offer (ITO) is divided into four parts, reflecting the key categories of network infrastructure, equipment and associated services required by CITEC. Suppliers may submit a tender for any single part, multiple parts, or all four parts, in any combination.

•	Part A – Network Hardware, Support and Associated Services: Covers the supply of network hardware and associated manufacturer support, maintenance and lifecycle services required to support CITEC’s existing and future network environments.

•	Part B – Optical Network Infrastructure and Services: Covers optical network requirements, including the supply of optical equipment and associated technology, together with technical support and field services. This part is intended to support current requirements and future optical network availability, capacity and capability.

•	Part C – Break-Fix Replacement Services: Covers the supply and replacement of network equipment and components required to respond to break-fix incidents and restore network services. This includes the provision of replacement equipment and associated services necessary to maintain service continuity and operational availability.

•	Part D – Other Network Equipment and Services: Covers future capability and other equipment, technologies and associated services that may be required by CITEC from time to time, including equipment and capabilities such as virtual laboratory environments, firewalls and other network or technology solutions that fall outside the specific scope of Parts A, B and C.

The four parts are intended to provide CITEC with flexible contract arrangements that can accommodate current operational requirements while supporting future technology replacement, network expansion, service continuity and emerging technology needs. Suppliers may tender for one or more parts based on their capabilities and areas of expertise.
