publicQuestions.question:
In Appendix 1 – Functional and Technical Specification, clause 3.1.2.2 and Section 3.2.3 call for single logical-unit and stacking options, while Tables 7 and 8 (clauses 2.4.7.1–2.4.7.2) specify stacked Layer-three switches at MAN and WAN Class 2B sites. Section 3.2.3 also requires SC switches to operate SR-MPLS with Flexible Algorithm and TI-LFA. Can CITEC confirm whether these routing features and stacking must operate together on the same switches, or whether independent redundant devices are acceptable? If both cannot be supported together, which requirement takes priority?

Question Regarding: PART C Capability Response

PSNMC has provided data in the column "Customer Defined Criticality"; That entry matches one of the six columns "Offerors Select" for the various site criticality classes. Does the responder need to complete all 6 columns per site, or only the column that matches the column "Customer Defined Criticality"?
publicQuestions.answer:
In Appendix 1 – Functional and Technical Specification, clause 3.1.2.2 and Section 3.2.3 call for single logical-unit and stacking options, while Tables 7 and 8 (clauses 2.4.7.1–2.4.7.2) specify stacked Layer-three switches at MAN and WAN Class 2B sites. Section 3.2.3 also requires SC switches to operate SR-MPLS with Flexible Algorithm and TI-LFA. Can CITEC confirm whether these routing features and stacking must operate together on the same switches, or whether independent redundant devices are acceptable? If both cannot be supported together, which requirement takes priority?

CITEC does not require these routing capabilities and stacking functionality to operate together on the same physical switch platform, provided that:

The proposed solution delivers the required routing functionality, resilience, availability, and operational outcomes.

The architecture provides equivalent or better levels of redundancy and failover capability.

Accordingly, independent redundant devices are acceptable where they meet the functional and operational intent of the specification.

Where a bidder's proposed platform cannot support both stacking and the specified routing capabilities simultaneously, bidders should clearly identify this within their response and describe the alternative architecture proposed.

Question Regarding: PART C Capability Response

PSNMC has provided data in the column "Customer Defined Criticality"; That entry matches one of the six columns "Offerors Select" for the various site criticality classes. Does the responder need to complete all 6 columns per site, or only the column that matches the column "Customer Defined Criticality"?

Please complete only the column that matches the 'Customer Defined Criticality'.

publicQuestions.answer:
Please view answers below questions:

1. Is direct OEM support, certification, and L3 escalation mandatory for the optical solution?

For Parts A, B and D, suppliers must demonstrate a direct OEM relationship, maintain OEM accreditation/authorisation, and maintain access to OEM Level 2 and Level 3 support and escalation pathways.

2. What cybersecurity liabilities, penalties and indemnities apply in the event of a security breach?

The ITO requires compliance with cyber security requirements and insurance requirements. Specific liabilities, penalties and indemnities are expected to be defined in the QITC Comprehensive Contract Conditions and associated contract schedules with the successful supplier/s.

3. Who bears the cost of technology refresh if optical equipment reaches End-of-Support during the contract term?

Procurement will occur progressively based on lifecycle, funding and operational requirements and be funded as part of a standard replacement program.

4. Are virtual firewalls acceptable instead of physical appliances and what are the sizing requirements?

Yes, the firewall solution must support virtual firewall instances. Minimum requirements include 50 virtual firewall instances, 50Gbps throughput per site, 5Gbps per virtual instance, 10 million concurrent connections per site, and 1 million connections per virtual instance. Physical or virtual implementation is not prescribed provided all requirements are met.

5. How are OEM manufacturing delays treated under contractual SLA commitments?

CITEC for other questions acknowledged the current market conditions. However, there is an expectation that the successful supplier/s would work closely to prevent and manage any OEM manufacturing delays, and this would form part of the SLA agreement.

6. Must the solution interoperate with existing Adtran FSP3000 infrastructure?

Yes. Interoperability with the existing optical environment is a key requirement. The current environment includes Adtran FSP 3000 equipment. Suppliers must identify interoperability, migration approaches, replacement requirements and dependencies. Noting that alternative approaches would be considered.

7. Who will fund future firewall license, subscription and throughput growth requirements?

As previously detailed, costs associated with future procurement and lifecycle expansion would form part of the standard replacement and/or expansion program.

8. Are there separate security and availability requirements for Public Safety Network sites?

Yes. Site criticality categories define different support and restoration requirements. Enhanced Critical and Critical (000) sites receive the highest levels of support. Public safety agencies form a major portion of the environment.

9. Is local Australian spare stocking mandatory, do we require this for only optical devices.

Suppliers must propose how they will achieve replacement timeframes across site criticality levels. This is likely to require Australian local stocking to meet these needs.

10. Must L3 security resources be Australia-based and security-cleared? Is this mandatory

There is a preference for Australian based, but the suppliers needs to detail how they would meet this need under their proposed support model.

11. What are the 5-year bandwidth growth forecasts including 100G/400G requirements?

The ITO requires support for future capacity expansion and currently specifies support for 100GbE interfaces.

Please provide a capability statement and how proposed environments can be upgraded to 100/400GbE?

12. Is integration to existing EMS/NMS platforms mandatory?

Yes. Optical solutions must provide EMS capabilities and integration with CITEC's network management and operational support environment

13. What are the expected annual firewall incident and change volumes?

This information would be shared with the successful supplier/s.

14. Who provides SIMs/carrier services for out-of-band management connectivity?

OOBM scope includes cellular connectivity but responsibility for carrier services is not identified under ITO CITEC manages carrier services.

15. Will the supplier host and manage the virtual lab environment?

The ITO seeks supplier proposals and capabilities for laboratory and virtual laboratory solutions. Hosting and management responsibility is not prescribed and suppliers should propose options.

16. Existing OEMs need to be retained or multi vendor OEM support is acceptable

Existing OEMs are not mandated. Multi-vendor solutions are acceptable provided interoperability, supportability, and OEM relationship requirements are met. Multivendor OEM support is acceptable.

17. Are OOBM outages measured independently under contract SLAs?

OOBM outages will be measured independently under contract SLAs.

18. Supplier responsible for SOC operations and cyber incident response with no volume assumptions. Is a fully managed SOC expected under this contract?

No. The ITO includes firewall and security infrastructure requirements but does not request SOC operations or managed cyber incident response services.

19. Any specified OEM preferred for all HW/NW scope

No preferred OEM is specified. Existing Adtran equipment is mentioned for context only and is not intended to prescribe a vendor.

20. All these devices will be ordered at one time or will be ordered in parts

Procurement is expected to occur progressively throughout the contract term according to lifecycle stage, funding availability and operational priorities.

21. How many 1G or 10G Branch routers need to be deployed

Total installed router base is estimated at approximately 3,000 units. Port requirement will be specified at time of purchase. Please complete the pricing schedule at this time.

22. Do we require Day 2. configuration support for all network or optical devices

Part A and Part B include configuration, optimisation, maintenance, support and lifecycle services. Day 2 support is therefore within scope We require ongoing professional services support for configuration, optimisation, maintenance, support and lifecycle management services.

23. For OEM support what type of support is required-NBD/8*5/with Onsite support etc

Required service levels vary according to site criticality. Suppliers should propose support arrangements capable of meeting the required restoration timeframes. Please refer to Part C Classification Details within the Product Capability spreadsheet.

24. As per the procurement objectives-can we have the list of devices which are near EOL

This would be shared with successful supplier/s, indicative quantities and lifecycle stages have been provided to give a scale of the opportunities.

25. Can we have a scope of work for Day 1 & Day 2 activities expected from supplier

Scope descriptions are provided under Parts A, B, C and D, but detailed work packages would be provided with the successful supplier/s

26. Out of 3715 switches, how many will be 24 or 48 port switches

Referring to the Part A Switching tab within the Product Capability Spreadsheet will provide you with some indicative quantities of 24 and 48 port switches. Details will be provided at time of purchase, please complete the pricing schedule at this time.

27. OEM support will be through the respective RMA/Remote Support/Onsite support licenses subscriptions, it will be proactive support-or do we have any other expectations in terms of OEM support

Suppliers must maintain OEM L2/L3 escalation access and support CITEC's service commitments, including warranty, maintenance, repair coordination, configuration services and lifecycle management.

28. Can we have mix of different OEM for the entire architecture or a single OEM solution is required

A multi-vendor approach is permissible. There is no requirement for a single OEM, providing interoperability and support requirements are met

29. Need more claification on the secure disposal of the HW requirement

Disposal must include secure sanitisation, destruction where required, ISO 27001 accredited disposal services, environmental disposal practices, records retention and completion within 10 business days unless otherwise agreed.

30. Do we have any count on the number of sites by type-Critical, business grade, HÀ Sites, Standard, Enhanced critical

This information is provided within the Part C Capability Response tab within the Product Capability Spreadsheet.

31. Do we have any predefined service credits for the SLA adherence in terms of penalty

Any service credits or penalty regime would be defined in the final contract. The supplier can propose any preferred suggestions within their offer.

32. Billing/Invoicing will be done for CITEC or it can done for its partner agencies also

Contracting will be direct with CITEC and all partner agency billing requirements will be managed by CITEC.

33. Can we have an approximate idea of the existing infra topology especially in terms of OEM as this is also a refresh of devices and this will help to propose a compatible device/topology for the same

The ITO only identifies Adtran FSP3000 optical equipment as part of the existing optical environment. No further OEM or topology information is provided. The architecture is OEM agnostic, please refer to the technical specifications for details.

34. Will this be a complete greenfield or brownfield project in terms of deployment or a mix of both

This activity will support primarily a brownfield refresh and lifecycle replacement program, with additional support for new sites and future technology expansion.

35. How much open are we in changing the current architecture and changes if required

The ITO seeks contemporary replacement arrangements, future capability and innovation. Suppliers may propose alternative solutions provided interoperability, resilience and operational requirements are met.

36. What is the business purpose/aim that we are going for this transformation architecture or going for this implementation of Network setup

The objectives are to replace ageing end-of-life infrastructure, enable future network capabilities, maintain service continuity and supportability, and provide a resilient, scalable network platform for Queensland Government agencies over the next 5-8 years.

WAN-Brand and Hub Router connectivity should be designed in accordance with the required network architecture. Respondents should identify their proposed connectivity approach and any assumptions or dependencies in their submission.

Question 2:

Is it mandatory to support AC redundant power on CoreP and CorePE? Is it acceptable to use a conversion module to implement AC/DC conversion?

CoreP and CorePE equipment must support redundant power supplies. Respondents should identify the available AC/DC power options and any proposed conversion modules, including their impact on redundancy and resilience.

Please confirm when the separate replacement clock starts, how access, induction, transport restrictions and CITEC release/approval of stock are treated, and how best-efforts sites are designated. Are historic incident volumes and typical concurrent calls available for costing, without implying guaranteed volume?

ANSWER: The response clock starts when the supplier receives the phone call/email or ticket (to be negotiated), and the replacement clock starts at the same time. Any time taken due to induction and access restrictions does not form part of the 'clocked' time. Regular transport does form part of the clocked time and needs to be taken into consideration by respondents in their response. Unusual transport requirements to very remote sites such as the requirement for flights and boat trips, does not form part of the 'clocked' timeframe.

Based on historical data, it would be expected that up to 20 replacements may occur within a month, however this would increase in high-weather seasons.

4.	Price definitions: Please clarify the 06:00–18:00 weekday rate-card hours versus 07:00–18:00 service-support hours; the regional after-hours call and after-hours hourly descriptions both referring to three included onsite hours; and the process for agreeing designated hardware-storage bases and their 50 km metropolitan radius. We want to avoid double-counting included time or misclassifying travel.

ANSWER: The 06:00-18:00 weekday rate-card refers to the rates for work during the day (not after-hours). It is possible that work at a site may need to be scheduled from 6am due to operational requirements. The 7:00-18:00 are the standard daily operating hours for ticket/support request lodgement. Tickets may be lodged in the AM hours by CITEC, however it is expected that the response clock would not start until 7am for those criticality classes.

For after-hours rates, CITEC expects that employment agreements may include a minimum designation of 'work hours' for a call out.

Suppliers will be expected to maintain hardware storage bases at strategic locations to minimise the bulk of events occurring outside of a 50km radius from the storage base, where feasible.

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification question – Section 2.4.2.7 / QG-CDSB-2026-212 Product Capability Spreadsheet (follow-up to CITEC response dated 22-Oct-2026)

CITEC's response of 22 October 2026 says that the cost of any "associated required component" must be included in the hardware line price and noted in "Respondent Notes". However, it doesn't say how much detail that note must contain.

Our concern is that the current guidance still allows a respondent to price a low-specification configuration at a lower price, and include a brief note in "Respondent Notes" and the compliance tab that is technically compliant with CITEC's instruction but does not disclose what is, or is not, included. This would make the single line prices not comparable across respondents and could disadvantage respondents who price a complete, fit-for-purpose configuration.

To make sure responses can be evaluated on a like-for-like basis, can CITEC please confirm:

1.	Minimum disclosure: Must "Respondent Notes" list every component included in the line price, with part numbers and quantities?

2.	Pricing transparency: We note CITEC has previously advised that a BOM is not required. However, it is difficult to see how an accurate comparison can be made without the detail a BOM provides. At a minimum, must the supplementary information show the price of each component, or only the configuration that the single line price covers?

3.	Comparability: How will CITEC make sure configurations are comparable during evaluation?

4.	Treatment of omissions: If a component needed for the device to work as intended is left out of the line price, will the respondent be required to supply it at no extra cost? Or will CITEC treat the response as non-compliant for that line item?

5.	Binding nature: CITEC has previously advised that the current product set will not be ordered from. How, then, will the configuration disclosed in the notes be used to hold respondents to the line item price for future orders?

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
Please find answers below questions:

1. Minimum disclosure: Must "Respondent Notes" list every component included in the line price, with part numbers and quantities?

ANSWER: Respondents should list every component included in the line price with part numbers and quantities.

2. Pricing transparency: We note CITEC has previously advised that a BOM is not required. However, it is difficult to see how an accurate comparison can be made without the detail a BOM provides. At a minimum, must the supplementary information show the price of each component, or only the configuration that the single line price covers?

ANSWER: CITEC welcomes the provision of pricing catalogues alongside the Product Capability Spreadsheet to validate the information provided.

3. Comparability: How will CITEC make sure configurations are comparable during evaluation?

ANSWER: CITEC Subject Matter Experts will ensure that configurations are comparable during evaluation and will submit further questioning to suppliers if an offer does not look complete.

4. Treatment of omissions: If a component needed for the device to work as intended is left out of the line price, will the respondent be required to supply it at no extra cost? Or will CITEC treat the response as non-compliant for that line item?

ANSWER: If an essential component is omitted, CITEC will not expect the supply at no cost, but will treat the response as non-compliant for that line item, and/or may request further information.

5. Binding nature: CITEC has previously advised that the current product set will not be ordered from. How, then, will the configuration disclosed in the notes be used to hold respondents to the line item price for future orders?

ANSWER: CITEC acknowledges that OEMs have varied pricing and that discount rates vary. Both factors combine to form a total cost. Prices over the term of the contract should be expected to increase as historical evidence shows, and any significant increases will be investigated.

The Mackay Regional Council area is one of the fastest growing regions in Queensland. Covering the areas of the former Sarina and Mirani shires and Mackay city, it extends 7261 square kilometres.

With a population of around 110,000 as at June 2008 and a projected annual growth rate of 2.1 per cent, the region’s estimated population in 2031 is about 173,000 people.

Its coastal location is complemented by its spectacular natural environment. This includes 31 beautiful beaches, a picturesque blue river and a pristine rainforest hinterland.

Only an hour’s flight from Brisbane, the Mackay region boasts an enviable lifestyle and a buoyant economy with the benefits of a fastgrowing coastal city. It is the gateway to the rich coal deposits in the Bowen basin.

It is the largest sugar-producing region in Australia and nearly a third of Queensland’s export goods originate from the Mackay region.

There are about 25 different nationalities represented in the region, including people from Malta, South Africa, the Netherlands and Germany. The region also boasts the largest Australian South Sea Islander population.

description:
Bayside Council is seeking submissions from qualified and experienced respondents for the procurement of a cloud-based Aquatic and Recreation Management System, including implementation, configuration, data migration, integration, raining, ongoing support and maintenance services.

Tenderer can mark it as compliant but must state when the functionality will be available.

Target go-live is 31 May 2027

Unknown

Approximately 10 in total which needs to be retained if possible.

Debit Success

Ci Anywhere 2026B, preferred integration method is API.

Response:

2000 Learn to Swim participants, 1700 members, remaining visit passes depends by the time we do data migration.

This is outlined in Volume 2

Response:

Approximately 50

Response:

No but preferrable

The proposed works involve upgrading and formalising roadside drainage, pavement infrastructure and driveway connections, while minimising disruption to adjoining residents and the surrounding road network.

The successful contractor will be required to complete the works in accordance with the specifications, drawings and requirements detailed in the attached Request for Tender (RFT) documentation.

Further information regarding the scope of works, submission requirements and anticipated timeframes is provided in the attached RFT documentation.

title: Remove and Replace Roof Structures, Opal Street WTP Filters
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council operates the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant (WTP) located in Emerald, Queensland. The WTP incorporates four rapid gravity sand filters which form a critical component of the potable water treatment process.

Each filter is currently protected by an individual structural steel roof structure. Over time, these roof structures have deteriorated and are approaching the end of their serviceable life. In addition to their deteriorated condition, the existing roof structures do not adequately facilitate the operational requirements associated with periodic filter media replacement.

During future filter media replacement campaigns, one-tonne bulk sandbags are required to be lowered into the filter compartments via crane. The existing roof structures do not provide suitable openings through which these bags can be safely lowered into the filters. This creates operational difficulties and increases risk during maintenance activities.

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking responses from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures over the four rapid gravity filters.

The replacement roof structures must incorporate suitable access openings that facilitate the future lowering of one-tonne bulk bags of filter media into each filter compartment by others under a separate contract.

The Works are to be delivered under a Design and Construct Contract.

The Contractor must provide all labour, design services, engineering services, supervision, plant, equipment, materials, transport, certifications and incidentals required to complete the Works.

The Works include, but are not limited to:

• Site inspection and verification of existing conditions.

• Detailed design of replacement roof structures for four rapid gravity sand filters.

• Structural design certification by a Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ).

• Preparation and submission of design documentation and drawings.

• Attendance at, facilitation of and incorporation of feedback from an 80% design review workshop with Central Highlands Regional Council Water Utilities personnel. The Contractor must present theproposed design, demonstrate how operational requirements have been addressed, and provide draft design documentation for review prior to finalisation of the design.

• Removal and lawful disposal of existing roof structures. This includes the temporary covering of the sand filter opening to avoid any contaminants entering the filter media.

• Supply and installation of new roof structures.

• Provision of access openings to facilitate future filter media replacement activities.

• Supply and installation of all structural steelwork, roofing, flashings, lighting, stormwater runoff piping to prevent filter contamination, fixings and protective coatings.

• Final inspection and commissioning.

• Provision of as-constructed drawings and documentation.

• Handover of the completed Works.

The Contractor must be responsible for delivering a complete and fit-for-purpose solution.

Prior to commencing work on site, the Contractor must prepare, submit, revise and implement project-specific management plans suitable for the Works, including safety/WHS, environmental, quality, demolition, construction methodology/site management and traffic/pedestrian/access management plans, as applicable.

The replacement of filter media is specifically excluded from this Contract and will be undertaken by others under a separate contract.

Where the Opal St WTP Filter Media Replacement technical specification prepared by AECOM is provided with this RFT, only Sections 3.0 Materials and Construction, 4.0 Design and Documentation and 5.0 Roof Structure Removal and Reinstatement apply to this Contract, and only to the extent relevant to the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures. All other sections of that document are provided for information only unless expressly referenced in this Specification. In the event of inconsistency, this Specification takes precedence.

The Contractor must supply all labour, supervision, engineering services, design services, plant, equipment, materials, transport, temporary works and incidentals necessary to complete the Works.

The Works must be undertaken at the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant, Opal Street, Emerald, Queensland.

The Contract will commence within 7 days after the Award Letter and Contractual Arrangement are provided to and signed by the successful Contractor. Central Highlands Regional Council anticipates the contract end date to be as per the approved contract schedule.

publicQuestions.question:
Good day,

Thanks for the Site visit.

Can you clearly define the Battery limits on the Existing concrete structure.

The RFT says the contractor’s design must include verification of the existing support structures, foundations, dimensions, levels, interfaces and affected services.

This as stated is no small task and I am unsure of the intent. Due to the level of movement of the structure that was noted and commented on by CHRC rep it is evident that the current foundations have had issues. Further to this The AECOM specification is relevant here because it actually contains a dedicated “Concrete Rehabilitation” section, covering concrete breakout/removal, exposed reinforcement treatment, substrate preparation, repair materials, reinstatement, finishing, curing, inspection and testing. So I need to understand a clear battery limit.

The design requirements also explicitly say the new roof design must “include lighting and rainwater disposal.”

Can you please provide the Design or Design intent for both of these items. Where is the power coming from? Has the engineering been completed? What lights do you require and where? How many of them? Where is the rain water to go? What are the tie in points? Sorry but the CHRC Rep was not aware of any of the details.

The CHRC Rep was of the understanding that these roof structures were to fully enclose the WTP filters down and sealed onto the concrete, completely sealed from wind and rain water, also vermin proff. Please confirm this is the intent that a fully sealed area is required not just replacement roof structures.

Can you confirm the expected shutdown/staging arrangement? Can only one complete filter pair/two cells be taken offline at a time, and must each filter be completely returned to service before the next roof is removed?

What is the maximum allowable outage for each filter? Is there a preferred low-demand period or particular months when Council wants construction undertaken?

Are there existing structural drawings for all four filter concrete structures? We understand the filters were built at different times and may not be identical.

Does Council have a preferred new roof arrangement? Skillion, gable, similar to existing, or is the geometry entirely contractor-designed?

What corrosion protection system does Council expect for the structural steel? Is hot-dip galvanising acceptable/preferred, or is a duplex/coating system required? The new design has a minimum 25-year service-life requirement.

Please clarify exactly how Council expects the two access openings per filter to operate. Must operators be able to physically open them without mechanical lifting equipment, or is crane removal of a roof cassette acceptable?

Is the specified minimum 2 m × 2 m clear opening required for each individual filter cell without exception?

How does Council envisage the one-tonne bulk bags being lowered through the roof? What crane/telehandler will normally be used, and from which side of each filter?

If removable roof sections are acceptable, does Council require permanent certified lifting points and a documented lifting procedure?

What permanent working-at-heights system is expected? Static line, fall-arrest anchors, ladder attachment points, roof access walkway, or simply engineered attachment provisions?

What temporary protection is required over the open filters during demolition and construction? Does Council require a rigid engineered cover, sealed membrane system, or another defined standard?

Can a reusable temporary filter cover be moved progressively from Filter 1 to Filter 4, or does Council require multiple covers to be available simultaneously?

Are there contamination-control requirements beyond physically covering the filter? For example restrictions on grinding, hot work, galvanised material handling, drilling, dust generation or chemicals near an operating filter.

Can we perform hot works above/adjacent to the filters once an approved temporary cover is fitted? Or does Council expect essentially all cutting/welding to be completed off site?

Where can cranes be positioned for each of the four filters? We need to establish available radius and likely crane capacity.

Are there known underground services beneath the proposed crane/outrigger locations? Can Council supply service plans?

Does Council have information on pavement/ground bearing capacity for crane outriggers? If not, what verification will be required?

Who performs plant isolations — Council operators or AMM? What notice period is required?

Is condensation underneath the roof currently an issue? Does Council expect insulation or anti-condensation roof backing?

Insurance (mandatory criterion, RFT 2.4)

1. Timing of evidence (RFT 2.4, 3.3; Response section 11; Deed cl 11.1-11.2). Will Council accept a public and products liability policy that is bound and current before the closing time, evidenced by a certificate of currency dated before closing? If the insurer cannot issue the final certificate in time, will Council accept a broker's cover note or binder at lodgement, with the certificate to follow before the first Purchase Order?

-	Tenderers should provide current evidence of the required insurance cover with their submission. Where a final CoC is not available by the tender closing time, Council may accept appropriate evidence from the insurer or authorised insurance broker confirming that the required cover is current. The successful tenderer will be required to provide satisfactory CoC for all required insurances prior to contract commencement an/or issue of any PO.

2. Joint names wording (Deed Sch 1 Item 9, cl 11.3). Many liability insurers will not add a principal as a joint named insured, but will note the principal's interest and provide a principal's indemnity extension with cross liability and waiver of subrogation. Would Council accept "Kempsey Shire Council noted as an interested party, with principal's indemnity, cross liability and waiver of subrogation" as meeting Item 9?

-	Council acknowledges that insurers may use different policy structures and endorsements. Council will consider equivalent insurance arrangements where the tenderer can demonstrate that the proposed cover provides protection consistent with the requirements of the Deed. Any proposed alternative to the insurance requirements should be clearly identified in the tenderer's submission as a departure, together with supporting details of the proposed cover, for Council's assessment.

3. Products liability. For a services-only contract, is a combined public and products liability policy with a $20m limit for each of public liability and products liability acceptable? Is products liability required on an "any one occurrence" basis or an annual aggregate basis?

-	A combined Public and Products Liability policy may be acceptable provided the policy satisfies the minimum coverage and limit requirements specified in the tender and contract documents.

Tenderers should provide details of the basis and limits of their proposed cover with their submission. Any variation from the stated insurance requirements should be identified as a departure for Council's consideration.

4. Workers compensation (Deed Sch 1 Item 9). Item 9 says "Workers' Compensation or Personal Accident & Illness". Will Council accept personal accident and illness cover for subcontractors who are sole traders without employees?

-	Tenderers and subcontractors are required to maintain the insurances applicable to their business and employment arrangements. Where a subcontractor is a sole trader without employees and Workers' Compensation insurance is not applicable, appropriate Personal Accident and Illness cover may be provided in accordance with the requirements of the Deed.

Evidence of the applicable insurance arrangements may be requested by Council prior to approval of the subcontractor.

5. Motor vehicle and works insurance (RFT 3.3). Please confirm that comprehensive motor vehicle cover is "as applicable" and that works insurance (120% replacement cost) applies only if a specific Purchase Order requires it.

-	Comprehensive Motor Vehicle insurance is required where vehicles are used in connection with the Services.

The requirement for Works Insurance will apply where relevant to the nature of the works being undertaken and in accordance with the requirements of the Deed and applicable Purchase Order. Tenderers should identify any proposed departure from the stated insurance requirements in their submission.

6. Professional indemnity. Deed Sch 1 Item 9 says PI is not required, but the Response section 11 table has a PI row and PO T&C 10.a.iii mentions $1m PI for professional services. Please confirm we can answer "Not required".

-	Professional Indemnity insurance is not required for the Services under this tender. Tenderers may therefore mark Professional Indemnity as “Not Applicable” in the relevant section of the Response document.

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

Service delivery, response times and subcontracting

7. Critical Defect response (Deed cl 14.2(a), definitions in cl 1.1). Clause 14.2(a) requires a Critical Defect to be rectified within 2 hours of notification. For a scheduled footpath cleaning service, could Council please give an example of what it would treat as a Critical Defect? Would Council accept a tenderer based outside the Shire (about 450 km away) proposing either (a) a local subcontract crew, approved under cl 12.2, to attend and make safe within 2 hours, or (b) a different response window for full rectification, for example make-safe or acknowledgement within 2 hours and rectification by the next night? If so, should this be shown as a departure in the Response section 3 table?

- All defects are required to be repaired by the contractor in a timely manner. Please note Clause 14.2 will be amended to: "Without limiting clause 14.1, the Contractor must rectify a Defect within a reasonable timeframe agreed with the Contract Manager, having regard to the nature, severity and urgency of the Defect. Such notification to rectify the relevant Defect shall, where the relevant Defect is an Ordered Services Defect, be deemed to be a Variation directed under clause 13.1 unless the relevant Defect has occurred as a result of a failure to perform or complete any part of the Services in accordance with the Contract, in which case the Contractor will have no Claim arising out of, or in any way in connection with, the Defect."

8. Subcontractor approval (Deed cl 12.2, 11.1(b); Response 5.1.4). Does naming a subcontractor in Response 5.1.4 count as a request for Council's approval under cl 12.2, with approval given at award? -	Identification of a proposed subcontractor in the tender response does not, of itself, constitute Council approval of that subcontractor. 9. Local subcontractor for routine cleaning (Deed cl 12.2, 12.3). Will Council approve routine cleaning being delivered by a named local (Kempsey/Port Macquarie) subcontractor, with the head contractor managing, supervising and auditing the work and remaining liable for it? -	Council will permit the use of suitably qualified subcontractors for routine clean-ing services, subject to the approval requirements of the Deed. Proposed sub-contractors should be identified in the tender submission, together with relevant details of their capability, insurances and WHS compliance. Pricing basis and documents

10. Contract Sum (Response 9.1; Schedule of Rates). Should the lump sum Contract Sum be the estimated annual price (the total of the breakdown table for one year) or the total for the whole initial 36-month term? Are prices held fixed for the whole term, including option years, or is any annual adjustment available (Deed Sch 1 Item 6)?

- Thank you for your question.

Contract Sum: Please provide both the annual price (being the total of the breakdown table) and the overall Contract Sum for the full three-year initial term. Both amounts should be clearly stated in your response to section 9.1.

Respondents should base their Contract Sum on the rates submitted at the time of tender. Rates may be reviewed annually on the anniversary of the Contract, with any increase capped at CPI.

GST: All prices are to be inclusive of GST, including the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum, in accordance with clause 4.21 of the RFT. Where section 9 refers to rates excluding GST, please disregard this wording and provide GST-inclusive figures.

Pricing basis and documents

 - All prices must include GST. This covers the rates in the breakdown table, the annual price and the overall Contract Sum. Clause 4.21 of the RFT applies. Where section 9 asks for rates excluding GST, disregard that wording and give GST-inclusive figures.

The Specification lists "All footpaths & bin enclosures" on Belgrave St (Kempsey Traffic Bridge to Stuart St), John St (Belgrave to Verge), Forth St (Clyde St to York Lane), Smith St (Forth to Stuart) and the Riverside Park footpath (Forth to John) as approximately 8,750 mÂ², cleaned once a year before Christmas. It is about 19% of the annual area, so it materially affects the price.

13. Missing attachments (Response section 9 and 8.1). Response section 9 asks for the Pricing Schedule "in Microsoft Excel format", and section 8.1 refers to a Modern Slavery Supplier Questionnaire. Neither is among the four documents we have (RFT, Draft Deed of Standing Offer, PO Terms and Conditions, and the Response document). 15. After-hours contact (Deed cl 12.8). Is the after-hours contact only for notifications during and around programmed overnight shifts, or does Council expect an on-call attendance capability outside programmed works?

16. Water supply. May the contractor draw water from Council hydrants or standpipes in Kempsey, South West Rocks and Crescent Head? If so, what permit, metering and charges apply? Is water available at the Horseshoe Bay picnic shelter?

Where a tenderer’s proposed equipment or methodology requires an alternative water supply, such as filling a water tanker, this requirement should be considered and allowed for in their submission. Paid water fill stations are available at Sherwood and Armidale Roads (Kempsey), Belmore Road (Crescent Head), and Gregory Street (South West Rocks).

publicQuestions.question:
Rate review date

The pricing schedules for Panels B and C state that at the conclusion of each financial year, being 30 June, the tenderer may review its schedule of rates for the following financial year.

Clause 4.3(2) of the Panel Services Agreement and clause 4.1 of Annexure 1 instead say rates cannot be varied until 12 months after the contract starts. Which applies?

The 1 July date suits both Council and contractors. Works under each order are to be completed by 30 June (RFT clause 2.6) and Council issues new purchase orders from 1 July, so a rate change on that date never falls part-way through an order or a budget year. 1 July is also when the mandatory annual wage increases take effect, and wages are more than 85% of a contractor's costs for this work. Annual CPI figures line up with the financial year as well so there is clean data.

The other issue with a review tied to the anniversary of execution or commencement is that the RFT gives only an indicative timetable for those dates. In practice the anniversary could fall anywhere between February and July, so tenderers cannot know how long their tendered rates must hold and cannot price with certainty.

Can Council confirm the date of the first rate review?
publicQuestions.answer:
The option to review the schedule of rates will be at the end of the financial year, 30th June, with any changes taking effect from July 1st.

An addendum will be issued to reflect adjustment to the contract terms to align this.

publicQuestions.question:
Hours in a day

The pricing schedules ask for an hourly rate, hours in a day and a daily rate. Can tenderers nominate their own standard day length (for example 7 or 8 hours on site), and will Council compare tenders on the hourly rate or the daily rate?
publicQuestions.answer: Tenderers can set their own standard hours e.g 7 or 8 hours which is to be detailed in the returnable pricing schedule. The tenderers response to all components of the returnable pricing schedule will be reviewed.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Anne,

I’ve been reviewing the Natural Environmental Services panels tender and would appreciate clarification on whether Council would welcome a submission covering specialist environmental mapping and monitoring services.

TALONYX is an environmental intelligence consultancy. We use drones, remote sensing, GIS and spatial analysis to help land managers assess site conditions, plan works and track the results of management decisions.

For this program, our services could include:

Weed, vegetation and habitat mapping to help target and plan works.

Baseline and repeat surveys of bush regeneration, creekline, wetland and post-fire recovery sites.

Mapped records of erosion, access and visible infrastructure condition.

Spatial reporting linking completed works with subsequent observations, supporting program reporting and funding acquittals.

Panel B appears the closest fit, with potential applications under Panels A and C. I note clause 2.5 permits submissions for part of a panel.

Would Council consider these services within scope as a standalone specialist offering, or are they expected to be provided only as part of a contractor’s on-ground works package? If a specialist submission is appropriate, could you please advise which panel and pricing items would be most suitable?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer: The services outlined in Panel B and C are primarily related to on ground activities only rather than specialist environmental mapping and monitoring. Not pricing any of the other services indicated in the request issued, would result in flagging the submission for consideration on an eligibility list only.

publicQuestions.question: For a sole trader with no employees offering only suitable ride-on mowing and manual garden maintenance under Panel A, and no professional advice, tree assessment, chemicals or civil works: please confirm whether the $5 million Professional Indemnity insurance in Schedule 2 Item 16 is required for this limited scope, or whether the "if required" qualification in Item 14 applies. Please also confirm the acceptable evidence for Workers Compensation where the tenderer is a sole trader with no employees. Finally, the mechanical fuel management standard restricts ordinary work to 7am–5pm Monday–Friday: may the returnable daily rate use a 10-hour day with actual hours recorded, subject to breaks and site requirements?
publicQuestions.answer:
If you do not have professional indemnity insurance and do not consider it required for services offered please state this in your response.

A sole trader you would need to provide evidence of what cover would be in place to protect yourself, in the case of a workplace injury. Council is required to ensure any sole traders employed by it can demonstrate as a minimum personal accident insurance would be in place.

The hours proposed relate to the rate set and should be indicated in the pricing schedule, subject to adequate evidence of safe work practices.

publicQuestions.question: For a partial Panel A offer limited to ride-on mowing on open grassed areas by a sole trader with no employees, can a tender be lodged before the required insurance is in place? Please confirm the policy types and minimum cover limits for this scope, and whether certificates of currency are required at lodgement, before panel appointment or before the first work order.
publicQuestions.answer: You would need to provide evidence of what insurance you have in place. If you are already in business as a minimum some level of Public Liability insurance is required to cover you in case of injury or damage to a third party. Motor vehicle registration and insurance. Proof of insurance when submitting a tender is preferred or details for what arrangements would be put in place.

title: Construction of the Warburton (WA) Dialysis Facility
description:
NHS (Ngaanyatjarra Health Service), in partnership with Purple House, is seeking a Head Contractor to deliver a Design and Construct (D&C) commission for a new 4-chair, nurse-assisted haemodialysis facility at Warburton, in the Ngaanyatjarra Lands, Western Australia. The facility is to be delivered as a modular building, prefabricated off-site and transported to Warburton for installation and completion, with a 40-year design life.

Anticipated works commencement is 22 February 2027, with Practical Completion required by 29 October 2027.

The site is located on the Ngaanyatjarra Lands, a remote community in Western Australia. Tenderers must allow for all mobilisation, module transport, accommodation and logistics associated with a remote site of this nature.

Dairy Rd
Fyshwick, Australian Capital Territory 2609
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Jenarc is a client-side project management company that specialises in construction delivery, particularly in regional and remote areas of Australia.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Friday 13 November 2026 05:00 PM (AUS Eastern Daylight Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Jenarc, as the lead design consultant, has been working with NHS to progress the design of this facility through to 70%, with architectural and all services documentation (mechanical, structural, fire, electrical and hydraulics) now complete and included in this tender package.

As a D&C commission, the successful Head Contractor will take on responsibility for design development and documentation from 70% through to Issue for Construction (IFC), in addition to fabrication, delivery, installation, and all testing and commissioning of the facility.

The project has proceeded through the The Licensing and Accreditation Regulatory Unit's (LARU) AIP (Approved in Principle) pathway associated with its funding. All dialysis, water treatment and biomedical equipment is client-supplied; the Head Contractor is responsible for all associated services rough-in, connections and builder's work in connection required to receive this equipment.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
The successful outcome of this project is the delivery of a fully commissioned, modular 4-chair dialysis facility at Warburton, enabling community members from Warburton and surrounding Western Desert communities to access ongoing dialysis treatment on country. This supports the project's broader objectives of improved treatment attendance, better health outcomes, and continuity of cultural connection, reducing the need for patients to relocate away from family and community for treatment.

Tenderers should demonstrate a methodology and program that reflects genuine experience in remote Aboriginal communities, comparable healthcare and modular construction delivery, and a strong approach to cultural safety, WHS management, and Aboriginal employment and local subcontractor participation throughout delivery.

Charters Towers Regional Council invites tenders from suitably qualified respondents to complete the works required for the Weir Tower Access Walkway Replacement Project.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Procurement Team,

We currently reviewing the tender documentation for the Weir Tower Access Walkway Replacement (PR000138).

We would like to seek clarification on whether Council would consider an alternative design incorporating Fibre Reinforced Polymer (FRP) structural members in selected sections of the proposed walkway, in lieu of the specified steel members.

Under our proposed approach, the new intermediate trestle would remain steel, as specified in the tender documentation, while selected walkway structural components would be replaced with suitable FRP members.

Any proposed alternative would be subject to structural engineering verification and compliance with the relevant Australian Standards, design loads, performance requirements and project specifications.

Could Council please confirm:

1. Whether an alternative design incorporating FRP structural members would be acceptable for consideration.

2. Whether such an alternative could be submitted as part of our tender response, subject to supporting engineering documentation and approval.

We appreciate your clarification and look forward to your response.
publicQuestions.answer:
Respondents may submit an alternate response, however, are encouraged to do so as per clause 5.6 of the Procurement Process Conditions (included with the RFQ package).

Council has no objections to alternative design incorporating FRP structural members. That is on the basis that the Contractor submits, as part of their tender, construction issue drawing signed by an RPEQ which demonstrate compliance with the relevant Australian Standards, design loads, performance requirements, and project specifications.

Please note that all components including the handrails shall be designed and certified to be structurally adequate to both the log impact and debris loads to AS5100:2018 as defined on the Lancini Consulting Engineers drawing T26022-S002 Rev 0.

The Contractor must also demonstrate within the construction programme the impact to timeline for Fabrication drawing development prior to fabrication commences.

The Bega Valley Shire is located at the south-eastern corner of New South Wales, halfway between Australia’s two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne and three hours’ drive from the nation’s capital, Canberra.

Our community vision explains our collective aspiration that we are an inclusive and welcoming community that integrates quality of life, prosperity, sustainable development and conservation of the environment. Our connection to Country is guided by the culture and heritage of our Traditional Owners.

Bega Valley Shire Council is responsible for providing all of the typical local government services across the Bega Valley Shire including maintaining a broad range of assets valued at over $1.7 billion that allow our visitors and community alike to live, work and play.

The Bega Valley Shire is governed by an elected Council comprising nine Councillors. Councillors provide leadership and establish policy and strategic direction for the organisation and the future of the shire.

Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

Contractors to council play an important and valued role, assisting us delivering services and projects to the highest of standards and value for money.

We create a safer place to live by:

publicQuestions.question: Reading the tender documents and on page 9 of the Returnable Schedule - Schedule 7 Lump Sum offer with the breakdown of service categories, are we able to quote for the Annual Essential Safety Measures, Mechanical, Electrical and Fire only?
publicQuestions.answer: Council's preferred contracting model is to appoint a single Head Contractor responsible for the delivery and management of the full scope of Building Maintenance Services, including Fire, Electrical, Hydraulics, HVAC and other associated services. This approach is intended to provide Council with a single point of accountability, consistent service delivery and streamlined contract administration. Accordingly, Council does not intend to consider non-conforming tenders that propose splitting the scope into separate contracts. However, Council recognises the specialist expertise offered by individual service providers and actively encourages specialist contractors to participate in the tender process by partnering with a suitably qualified Head Contractor, either through subcontracting arrangements or as part of a broader service delivery team. Council welcomes such arrangements, provided the Head Contractor retains overall responsibility and accountability for the delivery of the full scope of services in accordance with the tender requirements.

publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Please refer to Schedule 6 and Schedule 11 of the Returnable Schedules. Tenderers are requested to provide details of their current systems for work health and safety management, quality management and environmental management, and how they will be applied to this contract. There is no explicit ISO compliance or certification requirement.

The successful Tenderer will be required to breakdown their PPM and ESM pricing on a ‘per building’ basis within the first thirty (30) days of Contract Award. This breakdown will then be used to benchmark and assess additional PPM and ESM tasks which may arise following the asset data verification process. The recurring PPM and ESM lump sum will then be adjusted accordingly.

publicQuestions.answer:

Drawing CIV-053 states “line and geotextile to be a design and supply item nominated by contractor. Min 50-year design life required.” Please confirm Contractors work scope.

5. Lagoon 4 retaining wall - The new block retaining wall shown on CIV-054 Section E is not dimensioned. Please provide its length, height and type.

6. Missing drawings - The drawing index lists STR-021 (Sewerage PS Flow Meter Chamber) and MEC-026 (Septage Receiving Flow Meter Pipework), but neither is included in the tender documents. Please provide.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-02 – Maturation Pond 3 HDPE liner: design life/warranty, thickness and preferred supplier

Request for Information – RFI-02

SNG Engineering requests clarification on the following items relating to the Maturation Pond 3 HDPE geomembrane liner (Spec cl 5.4(a) and 5.4(d)), so that the liner can be priced on a compliant basis before tender close.

Q1 – Design life and warranty basis

Attachment L, s7.3 Table 7-5 sets design lives of 50 years or more for several asset categories (e.g. liquid-retaining concrete 50 yrs, civil infrastructure 60 yrs) but does not list a category for the geomembrane liner. HDPE liner suppliers we have approached (including Geosynthetic and Andrew Maddocks) advise that no manufacturer will provide a warranty beyond 20 years. Please confirm: (a) the design life Council requires for the HDPE liner; and (b) that a manufacturer's material warranty of 20 years (together with the installer's workmanship warranty) is an acceptable basis for compliance.

Q2 – Liner thickness and governing document

Attachment L, s6.7 Table 6-14 (Maturation Pond Design Criteria) nominates 'Lining: 1.5 mm HDPE geomembrane' (alongside 'Storage Volume: Min 6 ML', which appears to describe the new 6 ML pond rather than Maturation Pond 3). Attachment C cl 5.4(a) and (d) do not state a liner thickness, material grade or design life for Maturation Pond 3; they refer to the IFC drawings and 'the accepted geomembrane supplier installation requirements'. Supplier advice recommends 2.5 mm HDPE. Please confirm: (a) whether Att L Table 6-14 applies to Maturation Pond 3; (b) the required liner thickness – specifically whether tenderers are to price 2.5 mm HDPE; and (c) noting Att C cl 1.1 and the precedence statement in Att C cl 2.6 ('Unless directed otherwise, the drawing sets take precedence'), which document governs the liner requirements where the Basis of Design, Specification and drawings differ.

Q4 – Protection, base and under-liner drainage/venting

Att C cl 5.4(c)-(d) require 'separation geotextile, cushioning and liner protection as detailed' and 'protective layers'; Att L s6.7 describes batter/freeboard protection options (geotextile with rip-rap, or geocell infilled with low-strength concrete or gravel) 'without nominating a single fixed solution'. Neither document specifies a concrete base slab or an under-liner drainage/gas-venting system. Please confirm the protection option to be priced for Pond 3, and whether any base slab or under-liner drainage/venting is required.

Q3 – Preferred supplier

Please advise whether Council has a preferred or nominated HDPE liner supplier/manufacturer (for example, to match the existing lagoon liners referenced in Att L s6.7), or whether any supplier meeting the specification is acceptable.

Given the tender closes 4:00 pm (Qld) / 5:00 pm AEDT on Wednesday 4 November 2026, a prompt response would be appreciated.

Subject | Maturation Pond 3 – HDPE geomembrane liner: design life/warranty, thickness and preferred supplier

References | Att C Technical Specification GRC-006-TSP-002-01 cl 5.4(a) & (d); Att L Basis of Design GRC-2503-REP-BOD-01 Table 6-14 (s6.7) and s7.3 Table 7-5

Related | RFI-01 (Spec 5.4(a), liner area) – open
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	(a) and (b) The Contractor shall nominate the proposed liner design life and warranty duration in its tender submission. This deviation from the specification will not render the tender non-conforming.

2.	(a) Table 6-14 applies to Maturation Pond 3. However, the drawing set takes precedence over Attachment L.

(b) For the purposes of evaluating conforming tenders, tenderers shall submit a base offer for a 1.5 mm HDPE liner and separately price a 2.5 mm HDPE liner as an option.

(c) Where the documents differ, the drawing set takes precedence.

3.	Council does not have a preferred or nominated HDPE liner supplier or manufacturer. Any supplier meeting the specification is acceptable.

4.	(a) The Contractor shall nominate in its tender submission the proposed embankment protection option, selecting either Option 1 or Option 2 noted on drawing CIV-054 in Attachment H, with reference to the Liner Protection Typical Detail on drawing CIV-053.

(b) Council acknowledges that the documentation does not specify a concrete base slab or an under-liner drainage/venting system. Tenderers shall submit an offer in accordance with the specification and drawings.

title: RFQ2627/005 - Forrest Avenue Wisbey Street Roundabout Detailed Design
description:
The City is seeking an experienced design consultant to undertake the detailed design of a new roundabout at the intersection of Forrest Avenue and Wisbey Street.

The upgrade is being driven by the development of the new South West Aboriginal Medical Service (SWAMS) Health Hub at Jaycee Park. The additional traffic and access demands generated by the facility require the existing intersection to be upgraded to a roundabout to maintain safe and efficient operation for all road users.

The City is providing a concept design, which the successful consultant will develop through to a construction-ready detailed design. The design is to address civil works, stormwater drainage, street lighting and service/utility design and coordination, with due consideration given to road safety, construction and whole-of-life cost, and asset lifecycle.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
4 Stephen St
Bunbury, Western Australia 6230
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: The City of Bunbury is a local government area in the South West region of Western Australia, covering an area of 65.7 square kilometres along the coast about 180 kilometres south of Perth, the capital of Western Australia.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Sunday 29 November 2026 12:00 PM (W. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
SWAMS is developing a new Health Hub at Jaycee Park, which is currently under construction and scheduled to open in 2027. As a condition of the Health Hub development approval, SWAMS is required to construct a roundabout at the intersection of Forrest Avenue and Wisbey Street to provide safe access to the facility from Forrest Avenue.

The City is project-managing the design and construction of the roundabout on behalf of SWAMS.

A concept design and a Road Safety Audit have been prepared for the intersection by Shawmac, and are provided with this Request for Quote as the basis for the detailed design (Appendices C and D). Respondents should note that the Road Safety Audit (Shawmac Traffic & Safety, ref. 2404019-RSA-001, April 2024) was undertaken on the development application plans (SWAMS Health Hub DA July 2020, Rev 3) and pre-dates the concept design at Appendix D (Shawmac drawings 2404004-201, -901 and -902, Rev B, June 2024).

The City is arranging a feature survey and utility locating, which will be provided to the successful consultant on award.

A number of existing services are located within and around the intersection. Assessment of these services, including advising whether each is to be protected or relocated, and designing/coordinating any relocations, forms part of the required scope of services.

The City is also arranging a geotechnical and environmental investigation, which is expected to be available by January 2027 and will be provided to the successful consultant.

A new Transbunbury bus stop to service the new Health Hub is included in the concept plan as a future provision only. The City has been corresponding with the PTA regarding the proposed bus stop / embayment and will supply the correspondence to the successful consultant.

Forrest Avenue is classified as a Local Distributor under the Main Roads WA functional road hierarchy. Wisbey Street is classified as an Access Road. Both roads are managed by the City.

title: Supply of Plumbing Services (Supplier Panel)
description: Gunnedah Shire Council invites suitably qualified and insured companies to tender for the Supply of Plumbing Services. This tender seeks to establish a panel of contractors for the provision of plumbing services throughout the duration of the contract.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Welcome to Gunnedah! A vibrant, warm and friendly town surrounded by the expansive Liverpool Plains and framed by the Nandewar Ranges.

The Koala Capital of the world offers much more than just our famous furry friends! With a population of approx. 12,826, Gunnedah is a commodity hub and major destination on the intersection of the Kamilaroi Highway Touring Route and Oxley Highway.

Gunnedah also offers excellent lifestyle amenities and embodies a warm welcome that is only found on rural Australia. Gunnedah Shire Council is committed to providing a friendly and helpful service to all stakeholders. We are dedicated to Gunnedah being a liveable and accessible community for all ages and demographics. Additionally, we actively promote economic and business development in the region and are proud to be a one-stop-shop for enquiries regarding our responsibilities under other NSW laws including the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, the Public Health Act and the Companion Animals Act.

Council's functions include:

Provide for development in the local area.
Provide for local services and facilities that benefit ratepayers, residents and visitors.
Protect health and provide for the welfare, wellbeing and interests of the local community.
Represent and promote the interests of ratepayers and residents.
Establish and support organisations and programs targeting the local community.
Protect the environment and improve local amenity.
Attract and provide infrastructure for commerce, tourism and industry.
Manage, improve and develop resources available to Council.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Will this panel be used for the procurement of major water and sewer infrastructure works that typically may have been procured

by Council as a single project on tender link or similar?

2. Is council also requesting the tenderer provide plant rates in Schedule 6 of the Response Schedule?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Will this panel be used for the procurement of major water and sewer infrastructure works that typically may have been procured

by Council as a single project on tender link or similar?

This panel will be used for ad hoc plumbing services. Typical activities that may be undertaken under the Contract are listed in the Description of Services.

Council has a separate Civil Construction – Water and Wastewater Panel for civil works including water main replacement. The current Contract is scheduled to expire in March 2027 and Council expects to run a tender for the new Contract before this time.

Other major water and sewer works may be procured via Tender or Formal Quotation separate to these Panels.

2. Is council also requesting the tenderer provide plant rates in Schedule 6 of the Response Schedule?

Tenderers should include rates for any plant that they believe may be required to undertake the typical activities as additional items in the Schedule of Rates.

title: 201175 Footpath Grinding and Ancillary Services
description:
Sutherland Shire Council (SSC) invites Tenders from suitably qualified and experienced person(s), firm or entities for appointment of a single Principal Contractor to provide concrete footpath grinding and Ancillary Services, on an as-needed basis, within the boundaries of the Sutherland Shire Local Government Area (LGA) as the Principal Contactor.

This RFT applies to concrete footpaths only. Pavers, asphalt, shared paths, kerb and gutter, driveways and decorative finishes are excluded.

This specification details the provision of concrete grinding to SSC’s footpath assets. The scope of work comprises of creating a safe pedestrian thoroughfare by grinding displacements in concrete footpaths. The displacements range between 5mm to 30mm in height.

publicQuestions.answer:

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Team,

Could you kind assist with the below questions:

1.	Please advise Council's estimated annual spend or metres for footpath grinding.

2.	Please confirm how length (m) is measured for payment: the length of the trip edge ground, or another measure.

3.	Appendix 1 rows for outside hours, public holidays and Saturdays: should these be $/lm rates, a % surcharge on the lm rate, or hourly rates?

4.	Appendix 1 column B lists Cronulla Ocean Pool, Shelly Park Ocean Pool, Oak Park Ocean Pool and Silver Beach Tidal Bath. Please confirm these are not part of this RFT.

5.	Appendix 1 says prices are ex GST, but Part B says prices include GST. Which applies?

6.	Please confirm that a localised pedestrian set-up (barriers and signage) at each hazard satisfies the traffic control requirement. Where site conditions need a TGS or traffic controllers, will this be paid separately?

7.	Grinding Compliance cites class V or W under Table 2 of AS 4586. Please confirm class W (BPN 45–54) is the minimum pass level, and how often Council expects NATA testing (per Work Order or per year).

8.	Our method is dry grinding with H-class dust extraction, so no wastewater is produced. Please advise which EPA approvals Council expects the Contractor to obtain.

9.	For displacements not on Council's list, is the Contractor expected to inspect every footpath in the suburb, or only grind hazards found along the listed streets? Are these paid at the same rate without separate approval?

10.	Do "Ancillary Services" include make-safe (e.g. cold-mix ramps) for hazards over 30 mm? If so, please provide a pricing line.

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:

6. Localised pedestrian set-up (barriers and signage) at each hazard satisfies the traffic control requirement

8. If your dry grinding with H-class dust extraction is to an Australian Standard, that is sufficient

9. Only grinds found on same street and paid at same rate.

10. This does not include cold-mix ramps

SSC

approx. 6000 in meter per year

SSC

title: EXPRESSION OF INTEREST - Detailed Concept Design - Newrybar Village Centre Streetscape Master Plan
description:
Ballina Shire Council is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from a suitably qualified and experienced consultant team to progress data gathering, studies and concept design documentation of key aspects of the adopted Newrybar Streetscape Master Plan to a detailed concept design standard.

This is a staged tendering process consisting initially of this EOI. An Evaluation Panel will evaluate the EOI applications received and establish a shortlist of 3 consultant teams to participate in a Selective Tender Process.

Please refer to the Expression of Interest document for further information.

Ballina, New South Wales 2478
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Ballina Shire Council is located on the New South Wales Far North Coast, 770 kilometres north of Sydney and 190 kilometres south of Brisbane. The Shire, an area of 484 square kilometres, is set amongst a picturesque rural-coastal landscape and enjoys a temperate to mild subtropical climate.

The Shires resident population is approximately 45,000 with major service centre Ballina servicing the major townships of Alstonville, Lennox Head, Wollongbar, and Wardell. As well as a number of smaller villages and localities including Cumbalum, Teven, Tintenbar and Knockrow.
