publicQuestions.answer:
1. Question: Could Council kindly indicate the likely range of liquidated damages rates for Panel 4 Work Orders, and whether a cap may be applied, noting Annexure item 36 currently shows “No Limit”? (S03 items 35–36) – helps tenderers price delay risk appropriately

Answer: Council advises that the applicable contract conditions, including whether liquidated damages apply, will be determined on a project-by-project basis. S03 – Annexure has been provided as a sample and will be completed with the relevant project-specific details at the time of RFQ.

Each RFQ will identify the form of contract under which the project will be delivered, which may be AS2124, AS4300 or Council’s Minor Works Contract, having regard to the size, scale and nature of the works.

The RFQ will include the relevant draft Work Order, Annexure or Contract Information Sheet setting out the project-specific terms of engagement. Where liquidated damages apply, the applicable rate and any limit or cap will be specified, enabling invited respondents to take these requirements into account when preparing their quotation.

2. Question: Would Council be open to considering an overall limitation of liability and a mutual exclusion of consequential loss, either in the Deed or through Work Order special conditions? (Deed; S07 cl 37.2) – aligns with common industry risk allocation and insurability

Answer: Any proposed departures from, qualifications to, or amendments to the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed, including in relation to limitation of liability or consequential loss, are to be clearly identified in Form 6 – Contract Compliance as part of the Tender submission.

Tenderers should identify the relevant clause, the proposed departure or qualification, and provide sufficient supporting information for Council’s consideration.

Any proposed departures will be considered by Council as part of the tender evaluation process. Council does not propose to amend the Tender Documents in response to this query.

3. Question: Would Council consider releasing 50% of security at Practical Completion rather than at Administrative Completion? (S05 cl 5.7; S03 item 13) – supports contractor cash flow, particularly on smaller works

Answer: Council advises that security requirements will be determined on a project-by-project basis and specified in the relevant RFQ documentation.

For projects delivered under Council’s Minor Works Contract, Council may provide for 50% of the security to be released at Practical Completion.

For projects delivered under AS2124 or AS4300, security will be reduced and released in accordance with the applicable contract conditions. Any proposed departure in relation to the timing of the reduction or release of security should be identified in Form 6 – Contract Compliance for Council’s consideration.

4. Question: Could Council please confirm our understanding that total security is 5% of the Estimated Contract Sum, provided as two bank guarantees of 2.5% each? (S05 cl 5.3(b)(i); S03 item 12) – the clause wording could be read either way

Answer: Yes. Where the Annexure of Amended AS2124 or AS4300 nominates bank guarantees as the required form of security, the security will be provided as two equal bank guarantees of 2.5% of the Contract Sum each, totalling 5%.

As previously advised, security requirements will be determined on a project-by-project basis having regard to the requirements of the particular project. The applicable form and amount of security will be specified in the relevant RFQ documentation.

5. Question: Would Council consider including latent conditions relief, similar to S05 cl 12, in the Minor Works Contract for unforeseen existing services? (S07 cl 10.1) – gives a consistent approach across contract forms

Answer: Council does not propose to amend the Minor Works Contract as part of this Tender process.

At the time of RFQ, Council may consider project-specific amendments to the allocation of latent conditions risk, having regard to the nature and risk profile of the project and where an alternative risk allocation may provide a better commercial outcome for Council.

Any proposed project-specific qualifications or conditions should be clearly identified in the Contractor’s RFQ response for Council’s consideration.

6. Question: Would Council consider allowing delay costs for Council-caused delays, and extensions of time for authority delays and force majeure events, under the Minor Works Contract? (S07 cl 1.1, 27.5) – brings it in line with S05

Answer: Council does not propose to amend the Minor Works Contract as part of this Tender process.

At the time of RFQ, Council may consider project-specific amendments in relation to delay costs and extensions of time, having regard to the nature and risk profile of the project and where an alternative risk allocation may provide a better commercial outcome for Council.

Any proposed project-specific qualifications or conditions should be clearly identified in the Contractor’s RFQ response for Council’s consideration.

7. Question: Could Council please confirm whether set-off across Contracts is intended to apply to amounts due and payable, rather than amounts claimed or estimated? (Deed cl 4(j); S05 cl 14C.3(b), 42.11) – assists cash flow planning across concurrent projects

Answer: Council notes the request for clarification. Where a Tenderer seeks clarification of or proposes a qualification or amendment to the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed this should be clearly identified in Form 6 – Contract Compliance, including the Tenderer’s proposed wording, for Council’s consideration as part of the tender evaluation process.

8. Question: Could Council please confirm the minimum professional indemnity cover required for Panel 4 tenderers undertaking construct-only works? (Form 5 note; S03 item 23A) – so we can confirm our cover meets the requirement

Answer: For Panels 2, 3, 4 and 5, Tenderers with Professional Indemnity insurance below $10 million may still submit a Tender and will not be excluded at Gate 1 on this basis. The level of coverage held must be disclosed in the Tender Response Forms and identified as a non-compliance in Form 6 – Contract Compliance for Council’s consideration as part of the tender evaluation process.

Professional Indemnity insurance is not required for projects that are strictly construct-only. However, projects delivered under the Panels may include design, engineering, certification or professional advice.

Where Professional Indemnity insurance is required for a particular project, the applicable insurance requirements will be determined having regard to the nature and scope of the services and specified in the relevant RFQ and associated Work Order documentation.

9. Question: Could Council share the typical duration expected for Panel 4 projects, and advise whether rise and fall may be considered for projects over 12 months? (S05 cl 3.1(c)(iii)) – helps account for material and labour escalation

Answer: Council advises that the duration and applicable pricing arrangements for Panel 4 projects will be determined on a project-by-project basis and specified in the relevant RFQ documentation.

Where applicable, the RFQ documentation will also identify any provisions relating to rise and fall, enabling invited respondents to take these requirements into account when preparing their quotation.

No project-specific pricing is being requested as part of this Tender process.

10. Question: Could Council please indicate the warranty periods beyond the Defects Liability Period it expects under Specification cl 22 and Annexure Part G? (P4 Spec cl 22; S05 Annex G) – helps us arrange suitable supplier warranties

Answer: Warranty periods will depend on the relevant works, equipment and products incorporated into the works. Contractors are required to obtain and pass on to Council all applicable manufacturer, supplier, installer and subcontractor warranties, with project-specific requirements identified where applicable.

11. Question: Could Council please confirm that, for electrical works, an Electrical Contractor Licence satisfies the Form 4 “Relevant Trade Licence” requirement? (Form 4; Brief s9.1) – ensures we meet Mandatory Requirement 2

Answer: A current Electrical Contractor Licence is acceptable for electrical works, provided the licence authorises the contractor to undertake the scope of works being offered and the works are carried out by appropriately licensed and qualified personnel.

12. Question: Council able to share an indicative annual spend and RFQ volume for Panel 4, and the expected split between electrical and mechanical works? (Deed cl 2.5; Briefing) – helps us plan resources to support Council’s KPIs

Answer: No. Council is unable to provide an indicative annual spend, anticipated RFQ volume, or expected split between electrical and mechanical works. The Panel does not guarantee any minimum volume or value of work, and future requirements will be issued through RFQs as needs arise.

13. Question: Housekeeping: the S05 Annexure Part F warranty deed refers to “Brisbane Housing Corporation” as Principal, and Deed cl 2.7(d) mentions “Primary” and “Supplementary” Panels, which do not appear to be defined. Could Council please confirm the intended wording? (S05 Annex F; Deed cl 2.7(d)) – minor drafting clarification

Answer: Council acknowledges the drafting errors identified. The reference to “Brisbane Housing Corporation” in S05 Annexure Part F will be corrected to reflect the correct Principal, and clause 2.7(d) of the Deed relating to Primary and Supplementary Panels will be removed prior to execution of the Contracts.

publicQuestions.question: Do you require any references?
publicQuestions.answer: References are captured under response Form 11 – Previous Relevant Experience and Track Record, which asks Tenderers to provide relevant project examples, including client contact details. These contacts may be approached as referees during the evaluation process. If any further reference checks are required, these may be requested or undertaken as part of Council’s due diligence checks.

publicQuestions.question: Please confirm if Contractor/ Tenderers has the opportunity to negotiate project specific terms when a project quotation is requested.
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes. At the time of RFQ, invited Contractors will have the opportunity to identify any proposed project-specific qualifications or conditions as part of their quotation.

The RFQ Response Form includes a section for Quotation Qualifications and Conditions, where Contractors may identify any proposed qualifications or conditions applicable to their quotation.

Any proposed qualifications, conditions or amendments will be subject to Council’s consideration and acceptance as part of the RFQ process.

publicQuestions.question: For Tier 3, will Council accept documented in-house quality and environmental management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, or is third-party certification required?
publicQuestions.answer:
For Tier 3, Council confirms that third-party certification to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 is not mandatory.

An internally developed and maintained Quality Management System and/or Environmental Management System may be accepted where the tenderer can demonstrate that the system is appropriately established, implemented and maintained and is generally aligned with the principles and intent of the relevant ISO standard.

Tenderers should provide sufficient supporting evidence to demonstrate how their management systems are implemented, monitored, reviewed and continually improved, including relevant procedures, responsibilities, risk and control processes, non-conformance and corrective action processes, document control and internal review or audit arrangements.

publicQuestions.question:
SCI/72/2027 – Panel 4 clarification questions

1. Form 5 – Workers compensation

Where a tenderer has no employees and is not required by law to hold a WorkCover Queensland policy (work is done by the principal and by subcontractors who hold their own cover), please confirm that answering the workers compensation section "N/A – as required by law" meets Mandatory Requirement 3.

2. Form 2 – Individual (sole trader) tenderers

For a tenderer that is an individual trading under a registered business name, please confirm that (a) an ABN Lookup extract and the ASIC business name registration are acceptable instead of an ASIC company extract, and (b) the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed can be executed by the individual (Execution Type 4).

3. Mandatory Requirement 4 – Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan

Please confirm that a company-level Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan (to be made project-specific for each Work Order), together with example SWMS, satisfies Mandatory Requirement 4 for Panel 4.

4. Specification 12 – KPI 2 (RFQ participation at least 75%)

Will Panel 4 RFQs be issued by sub-category (e.g. Electrical only)? Will an RFQ outside a contractor's nominated sub-categories, or one that the contractor formally declines for capacity reasons, count towards the 75% participation KPI?

5. Deed clause 6.4 – Monthly meetings

Please confirm that the monthly meeting under clause 6.4 applies only while a contractor has active Projects, and whether it can be attended online.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Form 5 – Workers compensation

Where a tenderer has no employees and is not required by law to hold a WorkCover Queensland policy (work is done by the principal and by subcontractors who hold their own cover), please confirm that answering the workers compensation section "N/A – as required by law" meets Mandatory Requirement 3.

Answer: Yes. Where a Tenderer has no employees and is not required by law to hold workers compensation insurance, responding “N/A – as required by law” is acceptable for the purposes of Mandatory Requirement 3.

2.	Form 2 – Individual (sole trader) tenderers

For a tenderer that is an individual trading under a registered business name, please confirm that (a) an ABN Lookup extract and the ASIC business name registration are acceptable instead of an ASIC company extract, and (b) the Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed can be executed by the individual (Execution Type 4).

Answer: Yes. Where the Tenderer is an individual operating as a sole trader under a registered business name, an ABN Lookup extract and evidence of the registered business name are acceptable in place of an ASIC company extract.

The Pre-Qualified Supplier Deed may be executed by the individual using the applicable execution provisions for an individual.

3.	Mandatory Requirement 4 – Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan

Please confirm that a company-level Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan (to be made project-specific for each Work Order), together with example SWMS, satisfies Mandatory Requirement 4 for Panel 4.

Answer: Yes. For the purposes of Mandatory Requirement 4, Tenderers are to complete Response Form 3b. At Tender stage, a company-level Principal Contractor WHS Management Plan, together with example SWMS relevant to the types of works being tendered, is acceptable.

Project-specific WHS documentation will be required to be developed and implemented for the relevant works, as applicable, prior to commencement.

4.	Specification 12 – KPI 2 (RFQ participation at least 75%)

Will Panel 4 RFQs be issued by sub-category (e.g. Electrical only)? Will an RFQ outside a contractor's nominated sub-categories, or one that the contractor formally declines for capacity reasons, count towards the 75% participation KPI?

Answer: RFQs will be issued to Panel Contractors considered applicable to the scope of the particular project.

Where an RFQ is not issued to a Contractor because the works fall outside its applicable scope or capability, this will not count against the Contractor’s RFQ participation KPI.

Where a Contractor is invited to participate because the works fall within its applicable scope and capability, but declines to respond due to availability or capacity constraints, this will count towards the 75% RFQ participation KPI.

5.	Deed clause 6.4 – Monthly meetings

Please confirm that the monthly meeting under clause 6.4 applies only while a contractor has active Projects, and whether it can be attended online.

Answer: Yes. The monthly meetings contemplated under clause 6.4 are intended to apply while the Contractor has active Projects. Meetings may be conducted online where appropriate.

title: Emerald Sporting Fields Top Dressing
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking quotations from suitably qualified contractors to undertake sports field renovation works at nominated sporting fields within Emerald.

The works are intended to improve turf health, alleviate soil compaction, enhance drainage, improve playing surface quality, and support the long-term sustainability and safe use of community sporting facilities.

The successful contractor shall provide all labour, plant, equipment, materials and supervision necessary to undertake the following:

•	Hollow Tine Aeration (Coring) to relieve soil compaction and improve root zone performance. (All fields except McIndoe Field#3)

•	Collection, processing and management of extracted cores where required.

•	Supply and application of approved top dressing material.

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking quotations from suitably qualified contractors to undertake sports field renovation works at nominated sporting fields within Emerald.

The works are intended to improve turf health, alleviate soil compaction, enhance drainage, improve playing surface quality, and support the long-term sustainability and safe use of community sporting facilities.

The successful contractor shall provide all labour, plant, equipment, materials and supervision necessary to undertake the following:

•	Hollow Tine Aeration (Coring) to relieve soil compaction and improve root zone performance. (All fields except McIndoe Field#3)

•	Collection, processing and management of extracted cores where required.

•	Supply and application of approved top dressing material.

•	Mechanical spreading and incorporation of top dressing to achieve a uniform surface finish of at least 10mm

•	Drag matting, brushing or similar finishing techniques to ensure even distribution of material.

•	Protection of existing turf, irrigation systems, drainage infrastructure and surrounding assets.

•	Removal and lawful disposal of waste materials generated during the works.

•	Site clean-up and reinstatement upon completion.

Topdressing material shall consist of a clean, washed, free-draining medium-coarse sand suitable for sports turf applications. The sand shall be free from clay, organic matter, weed seed, stones greater than 5 mm, and other materials. The Contractor shall nominate the proposed sand source and provide particle size distribution data upon request.

 The Contractor shall mechanically spread and incorporate topdressing material in incremental passes and shall not apply the full depth in a single pass. The material shall be distributed evenly across the nominated playing surface to achieve an average finished topdressing depth of 10 mm.

 Following each application pass, drag matting, brushing, levelling or other approved finishing methods shall be undertaken to ensure even distribution and incorporation of the material.

 Any low areas, depressions, hollows, birdbaths, surface undulations or other irregularities identified during the works shall be filled and levelled as required using additional topdressing material. Hand placement and finishing shall be undertaken where necessary to achieve a smooth, uniform playing surface and eliminate localised variations in surface level.

 Upon completion, the surface shall be free of ridges, windrows, excessive accumulations of material and abrupt level changes, and shall maintain positive surface drainage suitable for sports field use.

The Contractor is responsible for undertaking works in accordance with industry best practice, relevant workplace health and safety legislation, and manufacturer recommendations for all equipment used.

Works must be completed in a manner that minimises disruption to sporting clubs and facility users while maintaining safe access to surrounding areas. Any damage caused to Council assets during the works shall be rectified by the Contractor at no cost to Council.

Upon completion, the Contractor shall provide confirmation of:

•	Areas treated.

•	Aeration and coring methodology utilised.

•	Quantity and specification of top dressing material applied.

•	Any defects, irrigation faults or field condition issues identified during the works.

The completed surface must provide an even, safe and high-quality playing area suitable for community and competitive sporting use.

title: Design and Construction (D&C) of New Social Housing – Palm Island
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is seeking to engage one or more suitably qualified and experienced Contractors to undertake the Design and Construction (D&C) of 22 new social housing dwellings across multiple sites on Palm Island, Queensland, together with an optional additional Package comprising two (2) dwellings.

The core Works are divided into five (5) Packages, comprising 22 dwellings and 86 bedrooms. An additional Optional Package 6 comprises two (2) dwellings and eight (8) bedrooms. Tenderers may submit a Tender Response for one, several or all Packages, subject to their demonstrated capacity to deliver the Packages tendered.

The Contract is intended to provide Council with a turnkey delivery solution, under which the Contractor is responsible for all investigations, design development, engineering, certification, building approvals, procurement, manufacture where applicable, transportation, mobilisation, construction, site and infrastructure works, utility connections, testing, commissioning, statutory certification, documentation and handover necessary to provide completed, compliant and fully operational dwellings ready for occupation and handover to the Department of Housing and Public Works (DHPW), except for matters expressly identified as Council responsibilities.

Council's objective is for all dwellings to achieve Practical Completion and be ready for handover to DHPW by 31 December 2027.

Council will provide Reference Designs establishing the design intent and minimum functional and performance requirements. The Contractor will be responsible for developing and completing the design and may propose design optimisation, including prefabricated, modular, panelised or other off-site construction methodologies, subject to satisfying the requirements of this Specification, the Principal's Requirements and DHPW requirements.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council is delivering a program of new social housing on Palm Island in collaboration with the Queensland Department of Housing and Public Works (DHPW).

This procurement comprises the design and construction of 22 new social housing dwellings, providing a total of 86 bedrooms across five (5) Packages and multiple sites on Palm Island.

Package 6 (2 new social housing) is optional. Council may, in its absolute discretion, elect whether or not to proceed with and award Package 6.

Palm Island, also known as Great Palm Island, or by the Aboriginal name Bwgcolman, is the largest of twelve tropical Islands in the Palm Island Group. The settlement is named variously Palm Island, the Mission, Palm Island Settlement or Palm Community.

The group of Islands is less than 20 kilometres from the nearest point on the mainland (Lucinda) and is 65 kilometres north of Townsville over sea. The Islands are serviced by a 20 minute plane ride or one and a half hour ferry ride from Townsville and a one hour barge trip from Lucinda.

Palm Island consists of small bays, sandy beaches, fringing reefs, beautiful freshwater streams and steep forested mountains rising to the highest peak of 548 metres at Bentley Ridge. Other islands in the chain, such as Orpheus and North Palm have globally renowned resorts and marine research stations. Situated in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, the surrounding reefs are as good as any on the outer reef, presenting wonderful fishing and diving opportunities and are used extensively by locals for hunting and gathering and other cultural purposes.

Palm Island is the largest discreet Indigenous community in Australia with approximately 4,000 people residing on Palm Island. There is high mobility between Palm Island and the mainland, and the population can increase to over 5,000 people during festivals and events. There are seven suburbs on the Island, running from Butler Bay in the south to Wallaby Point in the north, with the main, central settlement area, The Mission having the mall, shops, service centres, police station, motel, hospital and health service and Council chambers. Critical services infrastructure, including the Council’s works depots, waste and recycling facility, (Ergon) power station, water and sewer treatment plants, and two water supply reservoirs are at The Farm area, Solomon and Wallaby Point.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Marcio,

I’m Kieran Shirey, founder of LOGiT Australia, an Aboriginal-owned business developing Kin-Neon (kinneon.au), a housing production approach intended to build local manufacturing, assembly and maintenance capability.

Our development work includes mobile production of interlocking stabilised earth blocks, with any use of local materials subject to suitability testing, engineering and the required approvals. We are investigating ways to reduce transport, labour and external contractor dependency while building lasting community capability.

Having reviewed the tender’s provisions for alternative materials and construction systems, we would appreciate clarification on a potential specialist role alongside an appropriately qualified D&C contractor:

1. What technical evidence and approvals must be available at tender submission for an alternative wall or material system, and what may be completed during the subsequent design and approval stages?

2. Would Council and DHPW consider a limited, engineer-reviewed component within a conforming delivery proposal, supported by a fully compliant fallback so that housing delivery does not depend on unresolved R&D? We understand that a non-conforming alternative must accompany a conforming tender.

3. For a specialist participating through a lead D&C contractor, must the specialist also attend the mandatory site visit, or can the lead contractor’s attendance satisfy that requirement?

4. If the development stage makes participation in this tender premature, is there an appropriate separate pathway for discussing a future demonstration or training project? We would follow Council’s nominated process for any such discussion.

5. Please confirm the supplier-question deadline. The Request Summary states 6 November 2026 at 2 pm AEST, while Part A clause 5.10(c) contains different wording and a reference to 6 October.

We are seeking clarification of the appropriate participation and evidence requirements at this stage. We are not representing Kin-Neon as a certified system or offering to undertake the turnkey D&C scope independently.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Technical evidence and approvals

At tender submission, proponents should provide sufficient technical information to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system and its ability to meet the Principal's Requirements, including structural performance, cyclone resistance, durability, thermal performance, maintainability and applicable DHPW standards.

Detailed engineering, testing and statutory certification may be completed during the subsequent design development and approval stages, where appropriate. However, any proposed system must have a credible pathway to compliance, and the successful D&C contractor remains responsible for obtaining all necessary approvals and certifications before construction.

2. Limited application and compliant fallback

Council is open to considering innovative materials or construction systems as part of a conforming D&C proposal, including their limited application to suitable building components.

A fully compliant fallback solution may assist in managing delivery risk. However, any proposed alternative must be clearly identified and supported by sufficient technical evidence to enable its assessment. Council cannot provide advance acceptance of an untested or uncertified system, and any proposed solution would remain subject to the applicable design review, engineering and statutory approval requirements.

3. Mandatory site visit

The mandatory site visit requirement applies to the Tenderer submitting the D&C proposal. Where a specialist participates as a subcontractor or consultant to a Principal Contractor, the Principal Contractor's attendance will satisfy this requirement. Specialist participation in the site visit is encouraged where it would assist with understanding site conditions and delivery requirements.

4. Future demonstration or training opportunities

Council recognises the potential value of initiatives that develop local manufacturing, construction and maintenance capabilities.

Should participation in the current procurement be premature, you are welcome to submit a separate proposal for Council's consideration outside the current tender process. Any future demonstration or training initiative would be subject to Council's priorities, available funding, applicable approvals and procurement requirements.

5. Clarification deadline

I confirm that the deadline for tender enquiries is 2:00 pm (AEST) on 6 November 2026, as stated in the VendorPanel Request Summary. The reference to 6 October in Part A is an administrative error, which Council will clarify through VendorPanel.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Marcio,

Thank you for suggesting I introduce my proposal to the D&C contractors tendering for Palm Island via Vendor Panel. I am an Australian architect with work spanning tropical Queensland to the Tasmanian highlands, and a particular interest in creating pragmatic, economical yet traditionally beautiful buildings and places. As an example, my open-source Tasmanian House model shows how distinctive, characterful homes can be delivered at exceptionally low cost, as documented by ABC News and other publications. During my postgraduate studies I also worked in the Aboriginal town camps of Alice Springs, gaining firsthand experience of the challenges of remote-community housing. Further examples of my work, including alternative masterplans advocating locally characteristic, picturesque and human-scaled settlements, can be found at www.lev.au and www.jirilev.au.

I believe Palm Island presents a wonderful opportunity to establish a new model for social housing, demonstrating that homes can satisfy every technical requirement, including Gold Level accessibility, durability, climatic comfort and affordability, while also contributing to beautiful streetscapes and a genuinely loved township. Some of the island's older high-set houses, generous verandahs and lattice screens already offer lovely precedents.

I would be interested in working with a Principal Contractor to study and evolve this local architectural tradition, creating varied but harmonious houses, gardens and public spaces that contribute to residents' happiness, satisfaction and pride in their community. I believe much could be achieved through thoughtful design without necessarily increasing construction costs. Palm Island could become a nationally significant example of social housing that people are proud to call home and that visitors find attractive and memorable.

Jiri Lev, architect - jiri@lev.au

Tenderers are responsible for assessing the existing port infrastructure, including pier and ramp access, vessel size and draft restrictions, unloading capabilities and associated logistical constraints.

Tenderers must determine suitable transport and offloading arrangements and include all associated requirements and costs within their tender submissions. Any assumptions regarding port access or infrastructure availability must be clearly identified.

Tenderers should identify their proposed laydown and storage area requirements (m²), including space required for site sheds and temporary facilities, within their tender submissions.

publicQuestions.question:
We have a number of clarifications listed below.

Package 4, Lot 62D – Existing Camp Demolition Ref: Addendum 1, Section 6.1 Item 2

Extent: Please provide any drawings or a description of the camp, including buildings, construction type, decks, tanks, slabs and septic.

Reinstatement: Please confirm that "reinstatement" means cleared and graded to suit the subdivision earthworks.
publicQuestions.answer:
Package 4 – Butler Bay Lot 62D: Existing Accommodation Camp Demolition

Council provides the following clarifications regarding the demolition and removal of the existing 10-person accommodation camp under Addendum 1, Section 6.1, Item 2.

1. Extent of Demolition

No detailed drawings or as-built documentation of the existing accommodation camp are available.

The D&C scope includes the complete demolition, removal and lawful disposal of the existing accommodation camp and associated infrastructure, including buildings, foundations, redundant services and other associated structures.

Tenderers are responsible for assessing existing site conditions, identifying the extent and construction characteristics of the infrastructure and allowing for all necessary works within their submissions.

2. Ownership, Access and Availability

Council will coordinate the vacation of the accommodation camp and provide the Principal Contractor with access to the site in accordance with the agreed construction program.

Council will arrange for the removal of occupants and personal belongings before the site is handed over for demolition.

The precise date of availability will be confirmed during contract finalisation and programming.

3. Hazardous Materials

Tenderers must allow for appropriate pre-demolition investigations, including hazardous materials assessments where required, and ensure that demolition activities comply with applicable legislation and WHS requirements.

Any identified hazardous materials must be managed and disposed of in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The treatment of unforeseen hazardous materials will be governed by the relevant contract provisions concerning latent conditions and variations. No separate provisional sum is established by this clarification.

4. Salvage and Relocation

For tender pricing purposes, tenderers should allow for the complete demolition, removal and lawful disposal of the existing accommodation camp.

As an alternative to disposal, Council may direct the Principal Contractor to relocate certain buildings, structures or components to another location on Palm Island.

Any such relocation requirements, including the scope, destination, methodology and associated costs, would be discussed and agreed with the successful contractor following engagement, if required, and managed in accordance with the contract's variation provisions.

5. Services Disconnection

The Principal Contractor is responsible for coordinating and undertaking all necessary service isolations, disconnections, capping and removal of redundant services associated with the demolition works, including engagement with relevant service providers where required.

Redundant infrastructure must be removed or appropriately terminated to ensure the site is safe and suitable for the proposed subdivision and subsequent residential development.

6. Foundations and Fill

The D&C scope includes removal of existing foundations, slabs, footings and other subsurface infrastructure to the extent necessary to accommodate the proposed subdivision infrastructure, earthworks and residential development.

Tenderers must also allow for the assessment and appropriate management of unsuitable material encountered during the works.

7. Demolition Waste Disposal

Palm Island does not have a landfill facility, only a Waste Transfer Facility.

The Principal Contractor is responsible for the removal and lawful disposal of all demolition waste on the mainland, including any hazardous materials, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

All associated waste handling, loading, transport, barge freight and mainland disposal costs must be included in the lump-sum tender price.

8. Site Reinstatement

Council confirms that site reinstatement means removal of the existing camp infrastructure and preparation of the cleared site to accommodate the proposed subdivision earthworks and associated residential development.

The final site levels, grading, compaction and associated works must be coordinated with the subdivision civil design and applicable engineering requirements.

General

Tenderers must review the Reference Designs, supporting documentation, mandatory site inspection findings and relevant addenda, undertake any additional investigations considered necessary and include the required demolition and site preparation works within their Package 4 lump-sum tender price.

Any material assumptions, exclusions or proposed departures must be clearly identified in the tender submission.

132 Ashfords Road, Gregadoo NSW 2650

Description

The project involves the design, supply, installation, commissioning, maintenance and servicing of nine replacement leachate and groundwater extraction pumps at the Gregadoo Waste Management Centre (GWMC). title: Commercial Development and Operation of Workers Accommodation Precinct – Palm Island
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council invites proposals from suitably qualified and financially capable organisations for the commercial development, establishment and operation of a Workers Accommodation Precinct on Palm Island, Queensland.

The precinct is intended to support Council's extensive capital works program and other construction, infrastructure and commercial activities anticipated on the island over the coming years.

Council seeks flexible, commercially sustainable proposals for accommodation facilities and associated infrastructure, potentially including furnished and air-conditioned accommodation, catering and dining facilities, recreational amenities, laundry, carparking, contractor laydown areas and essential services.

Proponents are encouraged to undertake their own market demand assessments and propose suitable accommodation capacity, development staging, investment arrangements and operating models.

Council's preferred arrangement involves a privately financed and operated facility, with the operator contracting directly with accommodation customers and paying Council rent for the use of the land. Proposals involving Council contributions towards enabling infrastructure may also be considered.

Initial accommodation operations are targeted to commence from April 2027. Council is progressing the Development Application separately, and the successful proponent will be required to coordinate with Council's planning consultants and undertake mobilisation activities concurrently with the approvals process.

Proponents are invited to propose commercially appropriate lease durations, renewal arrangements and rental structures. Consideration will also be given to the potential adaptability of the precinct for future hospitality and tourism accommodation purposes.

The proposed development site is located on Great Palm Island, Queensland, within an area endorsed by Council for this purpose.

Further project details, requirements and submission conditions are provided in the Invitation to Tender documents.

Tender closing date: Monday, 23 November 2026 at 2:00 pm AEST.

All formal tender enquiries and submissions must be made through VendorPanel.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council (Council) is progressing a substantial capital works program involving housing, roads, utilities, community infrastructure, tourism facilities and other developments. These projects, together with additional investments by government agencies and private developers, are expected to generate significant demand for temporary workforce accommodation on Palm Island.

Existing accommodation facilities have limited capacity to support the anticipated construction activity. Council therefore intends to facilitate the establishment of a commercially operated Workers Accommodation Precinct.

Site and land arrangements

The proposed precinct is located within the Town Area defined under the Palm Island Improved Future Land Practices Indigenous Land Use Agreement (2010). The site has been endorsed by the elected Council, which has confirmed its authority to grant the relevant land interest.

The successful proponent will be expected to enter into an appropriate commercial land tenure arrangement with Council, with the lease duration, renewal arrangements and rental structure to be determined through the procurement and negotiation process.

Planning and development coordination

Council is independently progressing the Development Application through Milford Planning and Langtree Consulting Engineers.

Proponents must ensure their proposed accommodation concepts, layouts, infrastructure requirements and staging arrangements are compatible with the overarching planning and development approval process.

The successful proponent will be required to liaise with Council's appointed consultants and progress mobilisation activities concurrently with the Development Application, targeting initial accommodation operations from April 2027, subject to statutory approvals.

Accommodation and infrastructure requirements

The precinct should provide safe, comfortable, appropriately serviced accommodation suited to Palm Island's remote location and tropical climate.

Proponents should consider accommodation configurations, catering and dining facilities, recreational amenities, laundry, parking, contractor laydown areas, utilities, wastewater management, cyclone resilience, accessibility and other operational requirements.

Accommodation capacity, development staging and infrastructure solutions are intentionally not prescribed. Proponents are expected to assess the market independently and propose commercially viable solutions capable of responding to demand over time.

Commercial considerations

Council prefers privately financed development and operations, with accommodation customers contracting directly with the operator and the operator assuming commercial occupancy risk.

Council contributions towards enabling infrastructure may be proposed where justified. All proposals must include land rental consideration payable to Council.

The potential for future conversion to hospitality and tourism accommodation is desirable but is not a mandatory requirement.

Proponents should refer to the Invitation to Tender documentation, indicative site plan and capital works information for further details.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a commercially sustainable, professionally managed Workers Accommodation Precinct that supports the delivery of Palm Island's substantial capital works program while generating long-term economic and community benefits.

Desired Outcomes

Establish operational workforce accommodation from April 2027, with capacity and subsequent expansion determined by demonstrated market demand.

Deliver safe, comfortable, cyclone-resilient and appropriately serviced accommodation suited to Palm Island's remote tropical environment.

Provide suitable supporting facilities, including full catering and dining services, recreational amenities, laundry, parking, contractor laydown areas and essential infrastructure.

Encourage private sector investment, with proponents independently assessing demand, securing customers and managing commercial occupancy risk.

Establish a financially sustainable arrangement that generates ongoing land rental income for Council.

Enable progressive infrastructure development and expansion in response to construction activity and other accommodation opportunities on the island.

Support local employment, training, Indigenous business participation and economic development.

Desirable Features (Non-Mandatory)

Private ensuite rooms or self-contained accommodation units.

Flexible modular infrastructure that can be relocated, expanded or reconfigured.

High-quality recreational facilities, including a gym and communal spaces.

Energy-efficient design, renewable energy solutions and sustainable water and wastewater management.

Accommodation and facilities adaptable for future hospitality and tourism operations.

Commercial proposals that minimise Council's financial contribution while providing attractive long-term lease returns.

Conditions and Performance Expectations

The successful proponent will be expected to:

Coordinate closely with Council, Milford Planning and Langtree Consulting Engineers throughout planning, design and mobilisation.

Maintain a realistic implementation programme targeting operational readiness from April 2027.

Comply with applicable planning, building, work health and safety, environmental, cultural heritage and operational requirements.

Maintain appropriate insurances, licences, certifications and documented management systems.

Provide effective facilities management, maintenance, housekeeping, catering, security and emergency response arrangements.

Maintain transparent accommodation tariffs, booking arrangements and agreed mechanisms for future price adjustments.

Meet agreed standards for accommodation availability, cleanliness, maintenance, catering quality, customer service and incident response.

Provide regular performance reporting covering occupancy, accommodation capacity, operational performance, maintenance, safety and agreed community benefits.

Maintain the leased land and facilities in good condition and comply with agreed end-of-lease and site handback obligations.

Key Project Benefits

The project is expected to strengthen Palm Island's capacity to deliver major infrastructure and housing investments, reduce accommodation constraints affecting construction contractors, attract private investment, generate rental revenue for Council and create local employment and business opportunities.

Council also recognises the potential longer-term value of infrastructure that could support hospitality and tourism activities following the peak construction period.

Council welcomes innovative proposals and alternative commercial arrangements, provided they demonstrate financial viability, credible delivery capability, appropriate risk allocation and measurable benefits to Palm Island and its community.

Proponents should refer to Parts A, B, C and D of the Invitation to Tender for the detailed requirements, proposed commercial framework and return schedules.

These arrangements must address:

2. Future Tourism and Hospitality Uses

Site and land arrangements

The proposed precinct is located within the Town Area defined under the Palm Island Improved Future Land Practices Indigenous Land Use Agreement (2010). The site has been endorsed by the elected Council, which has confirmed its authority to grant the relevant land interest.

The successful proponent will be expected to enter into an appropriate commercial land tenure arrangement with Council, with the lease duration, renewal arrangements and rental structure to be determined through the procurement and negotiation process.

Enable progressive infrastructure development and expansion in response to construction activity and other accommodation opportunities on the island.

Private ensuite rooms or self-contained accommodation units.

Flexible modular infrastructure that can be relocated, expanded or reconfigured.

High-quality recreational facilities, including a gym and communal spaces.

Accommodation and facilities adaptable for future hospitality and tourism operations.

Commercial proposals that minimise Council's financial contribution while providing attractive long-term lease returns.

title: HEPA Vacuum maintenance
description: The purpose of the H Class HEPA Vacuum Maintenance Services is to support FRV in maintaining its HEPA rated vacuum equipment, ensuring compliance with safety and legal standards, safeguarding workers from hazardous dust exposure, and keeping all sites and fleet assets clean, safe, and operational. The purpose of this procurement is to establish a contract for the supply and support of commercial-grade HEPA filtration vacuum equipment suitable for FRV's operational environment.

Tenderers should demonstrate that the proposed equipment is compatible with FRV's intended operating conditions, maintenance practices, consumables, accessories, training requirements and workplace health and safety obligations. Where applicable, Tenderers should identify any proprietary components, system dependencies, accessory requirements, interoperability considerations or infrastructure requirements necessary for the successful deployment and ongoing operation of the equipment.

vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes: FRV is seeking a solution that not only meets the mandatory technical and commercial requirements but also delivers operational, environmental and lifecycle benefits. Tenderers are encouraged to describe any enhanced warranties, preventative maintenance arrangements, service level commitments, training programs, equipment innovations, sustainability initiatives, reporting capabilities or other value-added benefits that will improve contract outcomes and support FRV's operational requirements. This information will assist FRV in assessing overall value for money and long-term benefits of the proposed solution.

Management and Capability

Methodology

Methodology

Environmental Sustainability

Environmental Sustainability

Environmental Sustainability Framework
Question ES3 – Continuous Environmental Improvement

Describe how environmental performance will be monitored, measured and continuously improved throughout the contract term. Include examples of environmental outcomes achieved under comparable contracts and any initiatives that may provide additional sustainability benefits to FRV.

Occupational Health & Safety

Occupational Health & Safety

Commercial Viability - FV2

Commercial Vialbiltiy - FV3

Failure to provide the financial statements as indicated above with the tender submission will eliminate the offer from further consideration in the assessment process.

In addition to reviewing financial statements, Dun & Bradstreet Risk of Failure Report (DRS) or similar checks may be conducted by FRV.

rovide details of any material contract disputes, significant contractual breaches, litigation, regulatory investigations or enforcement actions relating to the provision of similar services within the last five (5) years. Include the outcome and any corrective actions implemented.

title: Main Road Campbells Creek Tributaries – Flood Study
description:
Mount Alexander Shire Council ('Council') are seeking to engage a suitably qualified consultant to deliver and undertake a comprehensive flood study and develop conceptual design/s for flood mitigation solutions along Main Road (and adjacent tributaries) in Campbells Creek township.

The successful consultant will provide specialist expertise in flood modelling, hydraulic and hydrologic assessment, climate change adaptation, planning and conceptual engineering design to improve understanding of flood behaviour within the Campbells Creek catchment, including the interaction between riverine flooding, stormwater runoff and tributary flows.

The consultant will define the existing flood behaviour in the study area and the identification and evaluation of measures to mitigate and manage flood risk in the study area – including, but not limited to, recommendations for flood planning overlays, reviewing the performance of existing drainage, investigating potential mitigation works and updating emergency management plans.

The Texas Multipurpose Health Service (MPHS) Primary Healthcare Upgrades Project will improve the functionality, capacity and operational efficiency of the existing health service facility to better support current and future healthcare needs within the Texas community. The project includes the establishment of a new General Practitioner (GP) clinic within the existing hospital site, together with targeted refurbishment, reconfiguration and minor extensions to address identified clinical, administrative, staff amenity, security and storage deficiencies.

Establishing the GP clinic within the hospital site will provide opportunities for greater integration between primary and hospital-based healthcare services. The GP clinic will be able to utilise relevant existing hospital infrastructure and support facilities, including pathology and other shared clinical services, reducing the need to duplicate facilities and improving coordination between primary and acute care.

Texas MPHS is experiencing increasing demand for emergency and aged-care services. The proposed upgrades will therefore also improve the facility's capacity and functionality to support these priority service areas, including improvements to Emergency Department patient flow and triage, aged-care storage and supporting facilities, and associated staff and patient amenities.

The project will make efficient use of the existing building footprint by repurposing and reconfiguring existing spaces wherever practicable, supplemented by targeted new works where additional capacity is required. Key improvements include accommodation for the new GP clinic, improved administration and clinical support areas, additional staff and patient amenities, enhanced storage, establishment of an Emergency Department triage function, and improved security at the Community Health reception.

The works will be planned and delivered with consideration of the ongoing operation of Texas MPHS and the need to maintain safe and functional healthcare services throughout construction. The project will seek to minimise disruption to clinical and support services while delivering durable, compliant and fit-for-purpose outcomes.

•	Modify or Construct stormwater drainage as specified on the drawings.

•	Supply and install seat as specified.

•	Supply and Install bollards as specified on the drawings.

•	Install signage and line marking including symbols, white thermoplastic rumble strips as specified on the drawings

•	As Built and handover documentation.

•	Clean site and remove any rubbish to the satisfaction of the superintendent.

In addition to the above, Contractors are to visit the site and make their own investigation and assessment of site conditions.

title: Cyber Security Operations Centre CSOC
description:
SR91442681, Request for information, managed Cyber Security Operations Centre

Energy Queensland is seeking information from established suppliers for a managed Cyber Security Operations Centre (CSOC) service across its corporate IT and Operational Technology (OT) environments.

The indicative scope includes 24x7 security monitoring, alert triage and investigation, incident notification and escalation, threat hunting, threat intelligence, detection and security platform engineering, OT security monitoring, and on-demand incident response and digital forensics. It also includes service management, incident exercises, knowledge transfer, transition and exit support.

Suppliers must support Microsoft Sentinel as EQL’s target security information and event management platform and integrate with EQL’s security platforms and ServiceNow. The service will operate alongside EQL’s internal teams, with EQL retaining incident command, risk acceptance and operational decisions.

This request is intended for suppliers with - An operational Australian-based 24x7 CSOC, Brisbane-based engagement and access to incident response, forensic and OT specialists.

Proven managed monitoring capability across both IT and OT environments.

Relevant electricity-sector or Australian critical infrastructure experience, supported by two comparable customer references.

Capacity to keep all EQL data handling within Australia, with no offshore access.

Willingness to use the Queensland Information Technology Contracting (QITC) framework for a future engagement.

This is an information-gathering and capability-screening activity, not a request for tender or a commitment to procure. It is not intended for software-only, advisory-only, penetration testing or staff augmentation offerings. Responses will inform EQL’s future service requirements and sourcing approach.

title: TVP/26/15 AQUALIFE FEASIBILITY STUDY
description:
The Town of Victoria Park (Town) invites submissions from suitably experienced Respondents to develop a feasibility study, needs analysis and redevelopment options for the possible redevelopment of the Town’s Aqualife facility.

This will be achieved by detailed research, analysis of a variety of inputs, confirming alignment with strategic objectives, considering stakeholder needs, completing a range of preparatory assessments and filtering possible options into a shortlist of more promising options through a multi-criteria assessment.

The feasibility study will specifically consider the potential for migration of the facilities, assets and services currently provided at the Town’s Leisurelife facility to the Aqualife site.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:

Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Located 10 minutes from the Perth CBD and home to state and national-level sporting grounds, Curtin University, green spaces galore and thriving communities, all centred around Albany Highway – one of the longest main strips in the Southern Hemisphere, packed with all manner of restaurants, cafes and retail stores – the Town of Victoria Park is a cultural hub nestled on the southern banks of Derbarl Yerrigan (the Swan River).

Suburbs within the Town include Victoria Park, East Victoria Park, Lathlain, Carlisle and Burswood, as well as sections of Welshpool, Bentley and St. James, with the current population of 38,000 expected to grow to 77,000 by 2050.

While the Town as we know it today has existed since the early 90s, recorded history of the area dates back to pre-European settlement, where there was evidence of Aboriginal presence on the Perth Coastal Plain and the site near the present-day Causeway was known as ‘Matta Gerup’ (knee deep). The Town’s Mindeera Advisory Group is named for Mindeera Springs, which served as a neutral meeting point for different tribes near this area. In 1829 the first non-Indigenous people settled in the area and the first land grants were issued. Originally established in 1894, it was absorbed into the City of Perth in 1917, before being proclaimed an independent municipality and closely resuming its original boundaries in 1994.

- Whether windscreens, windows, mirrors and other exterior glass require cleaning to a particular standard.

- Whether any surfaces or components are specifically excluded from routine cleaning.

- Whether Council has a documented cleaning checklist, inspection criteria or photographic examples used to assess the 95% Quality of Clean KPI.

- Whether additional requirements apply to heavy grease, accumulated waste residue or heavily contaminated vehicles.

**2. Working at Heights and Fall Protection**

Schedule 5, Response Annexure 2, Section 1 identifies managing the risk of falls, including working at heights above two metres, among the activities to be addressed through appropriate risk assessments, JHAs and/or safe work instructions.

Could Council please confirm:

- Whether cleaning elevated vehicle surfaces is required as part of the routine service.

- Whether suitable fixed platforms, gantries, mobile elevated-access equipment or other fall-prevention facilities are available within the wash bays.

- Whether Council provides certified anchor points or other approved fall-protection systems where required.

- Whether safety harnesses, fall-restraint or fall-arrest equipment are anticipated for any cleaning activities and, if so, whether this equipment is supplied by Council or the contractor.

- Whether Council has existing procedures for elevated access, fall protection, equipment inspection and emergency rescue.

- Whether additional training, competency verification or authorisations are required.

- Whether elevated surfaces are excluded from cleaning where suitable access and fall-protection arrangements are unavailable.

**3. Wash Bay Housekeeping and Environmental Management**

It is anticipated that routine wash bay housekeeping and preparation between vehicles may form part of the contractor's responsibilities.

To clarify the extent of these obligations, could Council please advise:

- Whether the contractor is responsible for removing accumulated mud, debris and waste residue between vehicles and at the conclusion of each shift.

- Whether Council has an existing site-specific Environmental Management Plan, waste-management procedure or environmental operating requirements applicable to the wash facilities.

- Whether the contractor is required to follow Council's existing environmental procedures or develop and submit a separate environmental management procedure for approval.

- What arrangements exist for the collection, containment and disposal of solid waste, sludge, wash-water residues and other materials generated during cleaning.

- Whether designated waste collection points, sediment traps, drainage treatment systems and other environmental infrastructure are provided and maintained by Council.

- Whether pre-start inspections, shutdown procedures, equipment checks and general wash bay maintenance are undertaken by Council personnel or form part of the contractor's responsibilities.

- Whether any maintenance or housekeeping obligations apply outside scheduled vehicle-cleaning activities.

**4. Detergent, Equipment and Consumable Management**

Schedule 2 identifies that Council provides high-pressure water, including hot water, and detergent.

Could Council please clarify:

- Whether Council manages detergent ordering, replenishment and storage.

- Whether the contractor is responsible for monitoring detergent stocks, refilling containers or dispensing systems, and associated chemical handling.

- Whether Council provides Safety Data Sheets and approved chemical handling procedures.

- Whether Council is responsible for servicing and maintaining pressure-washing equipment, hoses, dispensing systems and associated wash bay infrastructure.

- Whether additional cleaning products, consumables or equipment are expected to be supplied by the contractor.

- Whether vehicle drying equipment is available or whether vehicles are ordinarily permitted to air dry.

**5. Site Inductions and Safe Operating Procedures**

Schedule 2, Clause 4.12 identifies that contractor personnel may be required to undergo site induction and comply with Council's access and security requirements.

Could Council please advise:

- What site inductions, safety training and authorisations are required before personnel commence work.

- Whether Council provides site-specific safe operating procedures covering vehicle movements, wash bay operation, high-pressure cleaning, chemical handling and environmental controls.

- Whether additional requirements apply to simultaneous operations (SIMOPS), including concurrent wash bay activities and vehicle movements.

- Whether specific licences, training or competency verification are required beyond the stated HR licence requirement for personnel operating Council vehicles.

- The anticipated timeframe for arranging and completing inductions for newly nominated personnel.

- Whether induction and authorisation records are maintained by Council or must be supplied and maintained by the contractor.

**6. Operational Continuity and Contingency Personnel**

To ensure continuity of service in the event of unforeseen personnel absences, emergencies or operational disruptions, could Council please confirm:

- Whether appropriately qualified, insured and inducted relief, subcontracted or labour-hire personnel may be engaged on a contingency basis, subject to Council's approval requirements.

- Whether prior written approval is required before contingency personnel attend the depot.

- Whether contingency personnel must complete the same induction and authorisation process as regularly assigned contractor personnel.

- Whether any additional insurance, licensing, documentation or notification requirements apply.

This enquiry is specifically intended to clarify Council's requirements for maintaining service continuity in unforeseen circumstances.

**7. Fleet Scheduling and Wash Bay Availability**

Could Council please clarify:

- Whether the nominated fleet may be cleaned progressively across the full fortnightly service cycle, provided all required vehicles are completed within the agreed period.

- Whether Council allocates particular vehicles for cleaning on specific days or whether the contractor may propose a schedule for Council approval.

- Whether all three designated wash bays are available for simultaneous contractor use.

- Whether vehicles are ordinarily available throughout the specified 3:00 pm–11:30 pm service window.

- How vehicles unavailable due to operational requirements, delayed returns or other circumstances are coordinated and rescheduled.

- Whether historical information regarding typical vehicle condition or cleaning durations is available to assist tenderers in estimating resource requirements.

**8. Site Inspection**

We would also appreciate an update regarding our earlier request for a site inspection, if one can be accommodated.

An inspection would assist tenderers in assessing vehicle configurations, wash bay facilities, elevated access arrangements, environmental controls, safety requirements and cleaning expectations.

Thank you for your assistance and consideration of these questions.

We appreciate the opportunity to clarify these matters to support the preparation of an accurate, safe and compliant tender submission.

Kind regards and thank you in advance.
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 17/Nov/2026 08:08 AM)

Hi Jason,

Please see Council's responses below.

1. External Cleaning Scope and Quality Standards

Council does not currently maintain a documented cleaning checklist, inspection guide or photographic examples. The required standard is that vehicles are cleaned to a satisfactory condition in accordance with the Contract requirements and the applicable Key Performance Indicators.

Routine cleaning includes the external surfaces that can be safely accessed from ground level using the equipment provided within the wash bay facilities. Vehicle roofs are excluded from the routine cleaning scope.

The removal of accumulated dirt, mud, road grime, waste residue and similar contaminants is required as part of the service. Where vehicles present with excessive grease or contamination, tenderers may propose suitable cleaning methods as part of their submission.

2. Working at Heights and Fall Protection

Routine services do not require working at heights.

Contractors are expected to clean vehicle surfaces that can be reasonably reached from ground level using pressure cleaning equipment and long-handled cleaning tools. Vehicle roofs and other elevated surfaces requiring fall protection equipment are excluded from the routine cleaning scope.

Council does not provide fixed platforms, gantries, elevated work platforms, anchor points, fall-arrest systems or similar working-at-height infrastructure within the wash bays.

3. Wash Bay Housekeeping and Environmental Management

Contractors are expected to leave the wash bays in a clean and tidy condition following completion of services and remove any waste or debris generated through their activities.

Council maintains site-specific environmental and waste management procedures. The wash bays are fitted with drainage infrastructure and associated environmental controls which are maintained by Council.

Additional site-specific requirements, including any start-up or shutdown procedures, will be addressed during site induction.

4. Detergent, Equipment and Consumable Management

Council supplies, stores and replenishes the detergents required for the service.

Relevant Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and chemical handling information will be made available to the successful contractor as part of the site induction process.

Council is responsible for the maintenance of the pressure washing equipment, detergent dispensing systems and wash bay infrastructure provided for contractor use.

No vehicle drying equipment is provided. Vehicles are ordinarily permitted to air dry following cleaning.

5. Site Inductions and Safe Operating Procedures

All contractor personnel will be required to complete site induction and comply with Council's safety, security and access requirements prior to commencing work.

Site-specific safety requirements and operating procedures relevant to the wash bay facilities will be provided to the successful contractor during the mobilisation and induction process.

Any personnel required to operate Council vehicles must hold the licence requirements specified within the tender documentation.

6. Operational Continuity and Contingency Personnel

Council will permit the use of relief, subcontracted or labour-hire personnel, provided they meet all applicable contractual, insurance, licensing and induction requirements.

Any replacement personnel must obtain Council approval and complete the same induction and authorisation requirements as regularly assigned personnel prior to attending site.

7. Fleet Scheduling and Wash Bay Availability

The successful Supplier will have use of two (2) wash bays between 3:00 pm and 11:30 pm, Monday to Friday.

All fleet vehicles return to the depot daily. As a guide, the majority of the fleet (approximately 42 trucks) typically returns between 2:30 pm and 3:00 pm on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. On other weekdays, some vehicles may return later than this due to operational requirements and service demand (~3:30pm).

The scheduling and sequencing of vehicle washing is at the discretion of the Supplier, provided all required vehicles are cleaned within the agreed service periods and performance requirements of the Contract.

Council does not allocate specific vehicles to specific cleaning days and suppliers may determine the most efficient cleaning schedule to meet the service requirements.

Regards,

Candice

All Suppliers,

Please note that the Buy Ipswich criterion was discussed during yesterday's site inspection.

title: ITT259 - Aquatic Supervision (Lifeguard Services) - Aura Lagoon and Parklands, Caloundra South
description:
Tenders are invited from experienced and qualified aquatic facility operators for the provision of lifeguard services, together with the day to day operational duties at an aquatic facility within Aura Parklands (Aura Lagoon), located within the Caloundra South Priority Development Area (PDA), for a fixed term of three (3) years with option to extend for two (2) further years, commencing March 2027 and expiring on March 2030.

The aquatic facility will include all supporting infrastructure, including plant room and equipment, lifeguard tower and supervision zones, duty manager office, staff lunchroom and amenities, first aid room, storage areas, public change rooms and amenities, dedicated changing places facility, BBQ areas and shelters and water play.

Aura Parklands and Lagoon is an exciting new “South Bank style” urban parkland destination for the Sunshine Coast, offering a wide range of attractions, leisure facilities and event spaces which is currently under construction and due for completion in April 2027.

The aquatic facility is designed as the central feature of Aura Parklands , comprising approximately 2,100m2 of water surface area and designed for all abilities access, with a maximum depth of 1.8m.

The lagoon is proposed to be unfenced and reliant on lifeguard services and security patrols after hours to ensure public safety is maintained at all times.

The contract requires the successful operator will have responsibility to provide all required staff including lifeguard services and undertake day to day operational duties.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Does Council remove or manage contamination levels in FOGO and GO before it is transported to the final processing facility?

2. What level of contamination (i.e. 2% by mass) does Council consider to be deemed as "ordinary contamination".

3. Does Council have any specified days that it would like to deliver FOGO and GO?

4. What definition or classification does Council use for Processed product? e.g. does it need to meet AS4454 criteria or other specification?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Does Council remove or manage contamination levels in FOGO and GO before it is transported to the final processing facility?

A1. No. Council does not undertake pre-processing or contamination removal of FOGO or GO prior to delivery to the processing facility. Material is delivered as collected, and the Service Provider is responsible for monitoring contamination levels, managing contamination, processing the material, and disposing of any contamination or residual waste in accordance with the Contract requirements.

Council's waste collection contractor does, however, undertake a fortnightly bin audit program. During these audits, staff visually inspect up to 60 FOGO bins per fortnight for contamination. Where contamination is estimated to exceed 10% of the bin contents, the bin is not collected, and educational material is provided to the resident. Where contamination is estimated to be less than 10% of a bins content, the bin is collected and tagged with an educational notice identifying the incorrect materials observed.

________________________________________

Q2. What level of contamination (i.e. 2% by mass) does Council consider to be deemed as "ordinary contamination"?

A2. Council has not prescribed a specific contamination threshold or percentage for ordinary contamination. Tenderers are required to propose contamination thresholds, measurement methodologies, and management procedures as part of their tender submission for Council's review and approval. Ordinary contamination is expected to be managed by the Service Provider as part of the contracted processing services. Prohibited or hazardous waste is treated separately under the Contract. For information, Council's household organics bin audit undertaken by Ann Price Consulting in May 2026 estimated the average contamination rate within Ballina Shire household organic bins to be approximately 3.9%. This figure is provided as historical performance information only and is not intended to represent a contractual contamination threshold.

________________________________________

Q3. Does Council have any specified days that it would like to deliver FOGO and GO?

A3. Council has not specified particular delivery days for FOGO or GO deliveries. However, the RFT requires the processing facility to be available to receive Delivered Material during the minimum operating hours specified in the tender documentation.

For information, Council aims to collect and deliver a relatively consistent quantity of material across each weekday to support the efficient operation of its collection services and transport resources. Tenderers should therefore anticipate regular weekday deliveries, with delivery volumes generally distributed as evenly as practicable throughout the week.

The minimum receival hours specified in the RFT are:

•	Monday to Friday: 7:00am to 3:30pm

•	Weekends and Public Holidays: 9:00am to 2:00pm

Council's expectation is that the facility will be capable of accepting Delivered Material during these times.

________________________________________

Q4. What definition or classification does Council use for Processed Product? For example, does it need to meet AS4454 criteria or another specification?

A4. Processed Product is defined as any product recovered from or produced using the Delivered Material during the provision of the Services. Processed Product must comply with AS 4454-2012 Compost, Soil Conditioners and Mulches where applicable. The Service Provider must also comply with all relevant NSW EPA requirements, including any applicable Resource Recovery Orders, Exemptions, and the Compost Order in force at the time.
