publicQuestions.question:
Council has listed RRJ PVC pipe from 80 to 200mm. Can we use 80 & 100mm SWJ pipe downstram of the control valve ?

Can we install a flow meter downstram of the filter for flow monitoring ? There is not on the pump shed drawings / If so would council prefer magflow or a mechanical flow meter ?

Is the filter backflush mechanism hyddraulically driven or electrically driven ?

Council specifies that services need to me manually potholes. Can they be HydroVaced ?

Do sprinkler laterals need to be sand bedded ?

Do the all pipe collars need to be raised off the trech floor as specified ?? Even 25, 40 & 50mm pipes ?? This is an overkill

Council specifes in the 90day warranty period that material that are damaged throgh vandelism and theft are to be replaced at the contrcors expensive !! Are you for real ??

Council specifies 2.5mm cable in the tender. You can acheive valve closure up to 3km's with 2.1mm. Can we use 2.1mm ??

Can we specify another Control System other than Galcon GSI. MRCC uses Hunter. Can I quote Hunter ??
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Tenderer

Please find the below replies.

1. Council has listed RRJ PVC pipe from 80 to 200mm. Can we use 80 & 100mm SWJ pipe downstream of the control valve ?

No. Council requires Rubber Ring Joint (RRJ) PVC pipe to be maintained as specified for all lines from 80mm to 200mm, including downstream of the control valves. Swan Hill soils are prone to seasonal movement, shifting, and thermal expansion/contraction. RRJ provides the necessary joint flexibility to prevent catastrophic cracking under sports ovals, whereas SWJ creates a rigid line vulnerable to ground shear.

2. Can we install a flow meter downstream of the filter for flow monitoring ? There is not on the pump shed drawings / If so would council prefer magflow or a mechanical flow meter ?

Yes, a flow meter is highly desirable. Please install it downstream of the filter in the pump shed. Council prefers an electromagnetic flow meter (magflow) rather than a mechanical meter. Magflow meters have no moving parts, meaning lower long-term maintenance, zero pressure drop across the device, and superior accuracy when handling raw or slightly turbid water typical of irrigation reserves.

3. Is the filter backflush mechanism hydraulically driven or electrically driven?

The backflush mechanism itself is hydraulically driven (using the system's internal water pressure via hydraulic valves to reverse the flow), but it is initiated by an electrical signal/controller (usually a 24V AC or DC pulse trigger via a differential pressure switch or timer). Tenderers must ensure the design accommodates electrical control wiring back to the main cabinet.

4. Council specifies that services need to me manually potholes. Can they be HydroVaced ?

We prefer manual potholing, however, using Hydrovac may be considered as long as due care is taken not to disturb the existing assets. Requested to mention both the options in your quote, if possible.

5. Do sprinkler laterals need to be sand bedded ?

Yes, all sprinkler laterals must be sand bedded. To protect the PVC lines from localized damage and friction leaks caused by sharp clay clods or stones during trench backfilling and future soil compaction, a minimum 75mm to 100mm sand envelope (bedding and overlay) is required. Relying on native site backfill for lateral lines is not approved.

6. Do the all pipe collars need to be raised off the trench floor as specified ?? Even 25, 40 & 50mm pipes ?

Yes, this rule applies across all specified sizes. Raising the collars/sockets off the trench floor ensures that the pipe barrel rests evenly on a continuous underlay of compacted bedding sand rather than bridging across high spots. This avoids localized point-loading stress on the joints once the trench is backfilled and heavy turf-maintenance machinery runs over the ovals.

7. Council specifies in the 90 day warranty period that material that are damaged through vandalism and theft are to be replaced at the contractors' expense.

Please ignore the vandalism and theft part.

8. Council specifies 2.5mm cable in the tender. You can achieve valve closure up to 3km's with 2.1mm. Can we use 2.1mm??

No. Please adhere strictly to the 2.5mm² cable specification. While 2.1mm² cable may achieve valve closure mathematically up to 3km under perfect conditions, Council specifies 2.5mm² to account for standard electrical degradation, voltage drop under heavy simultaneous multi-valve operations, and future network expansions. Sticking to 2.5mm² ensures system reliability and fits Council's regional maintenance compatibility requirements.

9. Can we specify another Control System other than Galcon GSI. MRCC uses Hunter. Can I quote Hunter??

Council prefers sticking to the specifications. However, please feel free to quote for alternatives as well.

publicQuestions.question:
Clarification – PVC trench widths and depths

Could Council please confirm the trench width and minimum pipe cover requirements for all PVC pipework, including the DN200 mainline from the pump station to the irrigation valves and all smaller pipes down to DN25, including sprinkler submains and laterals?

The PVC detail on Sheet 3 specifies a minimum trench width of the pipe outside diameter plus 200 mm, allowing 100 mm clearance each side. Does this apply to every pipe size, or would narrower trenches be accepted for smaller pipes where the required bedding, support and compaction can be achieved? If permitted, please specify the minimum widths.

The 600 mm minimum cover is shown on the HDPE/RCP details, while the PVC detail only dimensions 50 mm minimum bedding below the pipe and 150 mm protective embedment above it. Please confirm whether 600 mm cover also applies to all PVC pipe sizes, or specify the minimum cover permitted for mainlines, submains and laterals, including any increased requirements at road, driveway or access-track crossings.

For clarity, please state cover as the distance from finished ground level to the top of the pipe, rather than total trench excavation depth.
publicQuestions.answer:
•	Mainlines (DN80 to DN200): The strict rule of pipe outside diameter (OD) plus 200mm minimum trench width must be maintained for all primary lines. This provides a mandatory 100mm of side-support clearance on each side of the pipe to allow proper compaction of the sand envelope and to visually inspect the Rubber Ring Joints (RRJ).

•	Smaller Lines (DN25 to DN50): For the smaller sub-mains and sprinkler laterals (DN25, DN40, DN50), a narrower trench width is acceptable down to a minimum of the pipe OD plus 100mm (50mm clearance on each side). This variance is strictly conditional on the contractor demonstrating void-free side-support tamping and a complete sand embedment zone around the pipe barrel.

Minimum pipe cover is defined as the distance from the finished ground surface level to the top crown of the pipe barrel. To protect the lines from Swan Hill's highly seasonal clay shifting and aggressive turf care machinery (such as deep spiking and coring), the following cover schedule applies:

•	Mainlines (DN80 to DN200): 600mm minimum cover across all zones.

•	Submains & Laterals (DN25 to DN50): 450mm minimum cover within sports fields and established garden boundaries.

•	Roads, Driveways, and Vehicle Access Tracks: 750mm minimum cover is required across all pipe sizes. If existing underground utilities prevent achieving a 750mm depth at a crossing, the pipeline must be retrofitted through a heavy-duty protective conduit sleeve with a minimum of 450mm cover.

publicQuestions.question:
1 We note that no geotechnical investigations have been undertaken for the project and that the Contractor is required to accept full responsibility for subsurface and groundwater conditions. Could the Principal please confirm whether any historical geotechnical reports or relevant ground condition information are available for the site? Additionally, given the lack of geotechnical information, could the Principal confirm whether unforeseen ground conditions, including rock excavation, unstable ground and groundwater ingress, would be treated as latent conditions and subject to a variation under the Contract?

2. Section 2 – Introduction of Part B Specification_V2.0 refers to “Decommissioning of the old pump shed and existing pump pit (no work on the shed for the Tennis Club).” Could the Principal please clarify the extent of the decommissioning works, including the dimensions and construction materials of the existing shed and pump pit, the number of pumps and extent of pipework and associated equipment to be removed, and whether complete demolition, removal or backfilling is required? Photos of the existing facilities would also be appreciated to assist with accurate tender pricing.

3. Could the Principal please confirm the location of the existing three-phase power supply connection point and the approximate cable run length required to supply the proposed pump station?

4. Can you please confirm if the pumps are operating under flooded suction or suction lift conditions? The current drawings show check valves on the suction side. If this is a suction-lift application, we understand the need for check valves on the suction side. If it is flooded suction, we recommend relocating the check valves to the discharge side as per standard practice.

5. Could the Principal please provide any available water quality analysis for the source water, particularly typical and peak levels of Total Suspended Solids (TSS), turbidity, pH, and any known algae or organic loading? Information on particle size distribution and seasonal variations in water quality would also be appreciated to assist with the selection and sizing of the filtration system.

6. Could the Principal please confirm the available supply pressure and flow rate for the automatic filter backwash cycle, including during periods of low irrigation demand? The proposed filter requires a minimum operating pressure of 2 bar and a backwash flow rate of approximately 5.6 L/s. Please confirm whether these requirements can be met under all operating conditions, taking into account the backwash discharge line backpressure. If the available pressure and flow rate are insufficient, please confirm whether a dedicated backwash pump and supply pipeline should be included in the Contractor's scope. If required, please identify the available water source and proposed connection point.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. There is an existing geotechnical investigation report that was used to design the irrigation system. It will be added as addendum. Please note unforeseen ground conditions, including rock excavation, unstable ground and groundwater ingress would be treated as latent conditions and subject to a variation under the Contract. The variation needs to be approved by the principal prior to any works commencement in the affected area/location. For more information related to variations, please refer to the tender documents.

2. The existing pump shed is not to be demolished. The tender specification or BOQ does not ask for the shed to be demolished.

3. There is an existing power to the shed. However, running cables for additional power to the shed (only if required) is on the principal. Tenderer doesn't have to consider this. But it is requested to propose the pumps as per the existing power, refer section 4.3.3. of the specifications for Electrical Power Requirement.

4. Operating Condition (Suction Lift): The pumps operate under suction lift conditions, not flooded suction.

 o	Pit Installation - Section View (refer tender drawings) shows the pump shed positioned on top of the dam embankment (minimum bank elevation 68.80 m), drawing water via a DN250 stainless steel suction pipe equipped with a DN250 S/S foot valve from the storage dam (maximum storage elevation 68.50 m, drawing down to 65.80 m).

 o	Provision to be made on the pump manifold for vacuum priming of the pump set.

 o	Additionally, the Grundfos NBG 100-65-200/217 pumps are noted as non-self-priming.

Valve Configuration: Because the system relies on suction lift and vacuum priming, check valves are required to maintain prime. Note that Drawing Sheet 2 of tender drawings (Typical Pump Station Details) currently illustrates check valves on the suction manifold side of each pump, while Sheet 7 also specifies a foot valve at the bottom of the suction line.

5. There is no water quality analysis report. The source water is non-potable raw water from the storage dam. Water to storage dam is supplied from GMW Channel. 400-micron automatic screen filter is recommended to be installed as the baseline requirement.

6. System Operating Pressure & Flow:

 o	The pump station is designed to maintain a constant operating pressure setpoint of 60 m head (approx. 5.88 to 6.0 bar) across all demand conditions—from near-zero flow (managed by the 7.5 kW VSD jockey pump, duty 7.2 L/s @ 60 mH) up to peak irrigation demand (56 L/s @ 60 mH).

 o	Because the automatic filter is installed on the pump station discharge manifold, the available supply pressure upstream of the filter will consistently be ~6 bar during normal system operation, exceeding your required 2 bar minimum.

 o	During low-demand periods, the jockey pump alone supplies 7.2 L/s at 60 m head, which exceeds the 5.6 L/s backwash flow rate requirement. However, if the system is in a "Low Flow Stop" standby state with zero irrigation demand, the filter controller will need to trigger a pump start (or run a backwash cycle immediately prior to system shut-down) to ensure the 60 m head is active.

Backwash Discharge Line & Backpressure:

 o	The backflush line must be sized according to the filter manufacturer's specifications and discharged back into the water storage.

 o	Because the discharge point is at atmospheric pressure at the top of the storage dam bank (~68.80 m EL, roughly 0–1 m above the pump shed floor), static backpressure is negligible, leaving ample differential pressure (~5.8+ bar) across the filter for backwashing.

•	Dedicated Backwash Pump: A dedicated backwash pump is not included in the design or scope, as the main/jockey pump manifold provides sufficient pressure and flow directly at the filter inlet.

publicQuestions.answer:
Irrigation Control System – Multi-Core vs. Wireless Radio Architecture & Cable Sizing

• Control Architecture Clarification (No Multi-Core Field Trenching Required): Following technical review with HR Products (the national distributor for Galcon), the irrigation control system is not reverting to a long-distance multi-core field wiring network. Instead, the Galcon 24-Station GSI Cellular Controller (GSI24AC) at the pump shed will be paired with an Irri-Gator 915MHz Wireless Radio System (comprising a 64-station input board G8R64AC, external transmitter G8RTX, and omni-directional aerial G8ROMNI).

• Field Valve & Receiver Arrangement: Communication to all Stage 1 and future Stage 2 field valves will occur wirelessly via 915MHz radio to local potted field receivers (G8RRX1SP / G8RRX2SP) mounted inside the valve boxes, connected to 12VDC latching solenoid coils.

• Wire Sizing & Spare Cores: Because long-distance multi-core control cables are eliminated from the trenches, Council will not be issuing active/common wire sizing tables or spare core schedules for Stage 2. Tenderers are only required to allow for short, local 12VDC control wiring tails (with a 1 m service coil as per Sheet 3) between the valve box radio receivers and the adjacent DC latching solenoids, plus the GPO and interface cabling inside the pump shed.

(Note: Council already utilizes this exact Galcon GSI + Irri-Gator wireless architecture across other parks and reserves to avoid long copper runs).

title: Mayne Yard ELP Sheds Fire System Upgrade
description:
Queensland Rail is undertaking the Mayne Yard Electric Locomotive Provisioning (ELP) Sheds Fire Systems Upgrade at Mayne Yard, Bowen Hills. The ELP Sheds form part of Queensland Rail’s major maintenance and stabling facility, which operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week and supports rail operations across the Southeast Queensland network.

The project involves upgrading the existing fire protection systems across the seven ELP buildings, comprising L, M, N, O, O1, P and Q Blocks. The works include replacement and upgrade of dry fire detection and alarm systems, emergency warning systems, smoke extraction and associated communications, cabling and infrastructure, together with testing, commissioning and handover.

The works are required to be delivered within a live operational rail environment, with Mayne Yard remaining operational during construction. This creates significant staging, access, isolation and operational interface requirements, including coordination with maintenance activities and rail movements.

To manage these constraints, the works are structured into Separable Portion 1 (SP1) for development and validation of the delivery methodology, access, staging, isolation requirements, detailed programming and stakeholder coordination, followed by Separable Portion 2 (SP2) (optional) for supply, installation, testing and commissioning of the works.

305 Edward St
Brisbane City, Queensland 4000
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
Founded in 1865, Queensland Rail has a proud history of connecting Queensland communities and supporting local jobs, industries and economies. We are committed to providing a customer-focused, safe, modern and world-class rail service for Queenslanders.

With total assets of $8.0 billion, and a network that extends more than 6,600 kilometres across the state, we are also focused on providing customers and Queenslanders with an efficient and value for money service.

Our 7,500 strong workforce delivers services across our South East Queensland and Regional networks, including Travel and Tourism services and Regional Freight.

Our South East Queensland team provides 8,392 services each week, supporting our customers to reach their destination safely and on-time. In 2019-2020, 44 million passenger trips were taken on the South East Queensland network (a decrease of approximately 20 per cent compared to 2018-2019, associated with COVID-19).

The Regional networks commuter and rail tourism markets are serviced by the Travel and Tourism products. These comprise eight services connecting Regional communities across Queensland with other Regional centres and the South East Queensland corner. These services support the Queensland tourism industry through the provision of unique rail tourism experiences including special events and charters through the operation of a small fleet of heritage services.

Our Regional networks and Freight team provides rail access for freight operators and other Queensland Rail supply chain customers to enable the critical transport of resources and general freight across the state.

We are proud of the role we play in providing vital passenger and freight services and we are dedicated to ensuring that our systems, procedures and practices reflect the highest standards of corporate governance.

title: Design and Construction of Dog and Duck Bridge
description:
Forbes Shire Council (Council) invites tenders to appoint one suitably experienced and qualified party capable of delivering the design and construction of a bridge over the existing Dog and Duck Floodway located on Wirrinya Road approximately 9km south of Forbes at Bundaburrah Creek. The project is funded through the NSW Government Regional Transport Resilience Fund and seeks to improve the resilience, safety and serviceability of the existing crossing. The project has completed environmental assessment and hydraulic investigations and is considered ready to proceed to detailed design and construction.

The Contractor shall be responsible for the detailed design, certification and construction of the bridge structure in accordance with the Specification.

There is a non-mandatory pre-lodgment site meeting at 10:30 AM on Thursday, 26 November 2026 at Wirrinya Road, 6.1 km’s south of the Newell Hwy

(33°27'5.52"S, 147°57'57.58"E). Please contact Council's Nominated Contact Person to RSVP. Attendance is not mandatory.
